tree:19elbjw0gs059a.relation: Following devils while thinking oneself guided: the worst kind of misguidance.

tree:0t3mdql1dgm06h.why: God establishing the truth by His words: at Badr, cutting off the disbelievers (8:7), and against the claim that the Prophet forged the Quran (42:24).
tree:0t3mdql1dgm06h.relation: God makes the truth stand by His words, in battle and in revelation.

tree:1x6gjxf10r8v6j.why: Two images of the dead coming out of the graves: like scattered locusts (54:7) and rushing as if to a target (70:43). Same scene, different simile.
tree:1x6gjxf10r8v6j.relation: The Resurrection scene drawn with two similes.

tree:0t1q79p0ic728p.why: Nothing is hidden from God: Abraham says it in prayer (14:38), and it is shown on the Day when all come out before Him (40:16). Negation differs, which a memorizer must note.

tree:0lv02tn19511rt.why: God does not break His promise: said to those hastening the punishment (22:47) and about the Romans' coming victory (30:6). 'Will never' vs 'does not' is the trap.
tree:0lv02tn19511rt.relation: God's promise holds, whether of punishment or of victory.

tree:0e2yfie0jsz3da.why: Both describe the patient believers who repel evil with good and spend from what they are given, in a different order and with a different reward named.
tree:0e2yfie0jsz3da.relation: The same character praised in two places: patience, repelling evil with good, spending.

tree:1rn0fba11o3bya.why: Two neighbouring ayat: on the Day they are called to prostrate and cannot (68:42), because in the world they were called while healthy and refused (68:43).
tree:1rn0fba11o3bya.relation: Contrast: the call refused in health becomes the call they cannot answer.

tree:1w1acct13pkkzr.why: Those who call to the Fire: idolaters one might marry (2:221) and Pharaoh's leaders (28:41). 2:221 contrasts it with God calling to the Garden.
tree:1w1acct13pkkzr.relation: Contrast: who invites to the Fire and who invites to Paradise.

tree:0q0skmm1sdpbd6.why: Houses of God and the remembrance of His name: the worst wrongdoer prevents it (2:114); in houses God allowed to be raised it is done morning and evening (24:36).
tree:0q0skmm1sdpbd6.relation: Contrast: blocking the mosques vs filling them with remembrance.

tree:0ck2kmb1ihd6zj.why: Both are about God's will in guidance: He did not will to purify some hearts (5:41); whom He wills to guide, He opens his chest (6:125). The words are common but the theme is the same.
tree:0ck2kmb1ihd6zj.relation: God's will behind a heart's purity or openness to Islam.

tree:0o4ad461lvwiow.why: The same warning: do you feel safe that He will not send a storm of stones on you? 'Do you then feel safe' (17:68) vs 'or do you feel safe' (67:17), and what follows differs.

tree:1146qvq00gl73u.why: Both invite people to look at creation: the shadows bowing (16:48) and the sky and earth around them (34:9). The opening differs ('have they not' with and/so).

tree:030ilgs1qwndgu.why: Two reminders of blessings made for people: night for rest and day for sight (27:86), a safe sanctuary (29:67). The opening differs by one letter.
tree:030ilgs1qwndgu.relation: Signs of mercy that should lead to faith, yet they deny.

tree:1dtnbfu1b4iqh2.why: What Satan wants: to lead far astray through seeking judgment from false authorities (4:60), and to sow enmity through wine and gambling (5:91).
tree:1dtnbfu1b4iqh2.relation: Satan's aims named plainly in two places.

tree:0agzlh80mqdj32.why: God will replace you with another people: if you do not go out to fight (9:39), if you turn away from spending (47:38). Same threat, two duties.
tree:0agzlh80mqdj32.relation: God does not need us; turning away from His cause means being replaced.

tree:07k1ff20vl7z9m.why: Both close a parable with 'thus God sets forth parables': the foam and the water (13:17) and the good tree (14:25). Neighbouring surahs, close wording.
tree:07k1ff20vl7z9m.relation: Two parables of truth that lasts: what benefits stays, the good tree gives fruit.

tree:17nu8k4027hozw.why: The words match but the structure does not: 2:102 says the sorcery they learn does harm them and does not benefit, 10:18 says the idols neither harm nor benefit. Under the card rules that is a different phrase, and the subjects (magic, idol worship) differ too.

tree:1hx46p50iq2tzx.why: Both threaten a painful punishment to those who hang back from fighting in God's cause: the believers at Tabuk (9:39) and the Bedouin who stayed behind (48:16).
tree:1hx46p50iq2tzx.relation: Same warning against holding back when called to go out.

tree:1mxv0ql14i9z03.why: Only the short clause 'and pardons much' is shared, with different subjects: the Prophet passing over much that the People of the Book hid (5:15), and God pardoning sins behind misfortunes (42:30). A rare phrase alone with different subjects is not enough.

tree:0gwk7ol0lbfc1r.why: Only the stock closing 'He knows what you do' is shared, with different lead-ins. Keeping oaths (16:91) and God accepting repentance (42:25) are different subjects.

tree:0yrwzpy07xltas.why: Only 'they know that God' is shared. Hypocrites who forget that God knows what they hide (2:77) and the slanderers who will know on the Day that God is the clear Truth (24:25) are different subjects.

tree:1uftfc21rbreh2.why: The only two places where God covers the day with the night, each in a passage listing signs of creation (the heavens and Throne in 7:54, the earth and its fruits in 13:3).
tree:1uftfc21rbreh2.relation: Night and day as a sign of the Creator's ordering.

tree:0ckk3tt0vq96ld.why: Forgiving those who wronged you: Joseph forgives his brothers (12:92), and the believers are told to forgive a relative who slandered (24:22), with 'do you not love that God forgive you?'
tree:0ckk3tt0vq96ld.relation: Similarity: a wronged man's forgiveness of kin, and the hope of God's forgiveness that should move us to it.

tree:077hb2w055vnhs.why: The only two ayat ending 'and they do what they are commanded', both about angels: those who fear their Lord above them (16:50) and the stern keepers of the Fire (66:6).
tree:077hb2w055vnhs.relation: Angels' complete obedience, as worshippers and as guards of the Fire.

tree:1jpuse90nbr081.why: Only 'they have no power over anything' is shared. The showy spender losing his reward (2:264) and the People of the Book having no control of God's grace (57:29) are different subjects.

tree:0gag7nx0qscvyn.why: The same question on the Day of Judgement, 'what answer were you given / did you give?', put to the messengers (5:109) and to the people they were sent to (28:65).
tree:0gag7nx0qscvyn.relation: Both sides of the message are questioned: the senders and the receivers.

tree:1vzgj3w1ryuqh8.why: Two cries of regret: the owner of the ruined garden wishing he had not associated (18:42), and the one given his book in his left hand (69:25). Same words, the world and the Hereafter.
tree:1vzgj3w1ryuqh8.relation: Regret too late, in this life and in the next.

tree:0uk332u0x0371k.why: Believers saying 'our Lord, we believe' and then asking: to be written with the witnesses (5:83), for forgiveness and mercy (23:109). Same opening, different request.

tree:1ysh7cy1788iog.why: Two neighbouring ayat on divorce, both turning on whether the couple can keep within God's limits. A memorizer must keep apart the wording and endings of each.

tree:0xxxygf1vt9wkf.why: Two calls to the believers, to be mindful of God (8:29) and to repent sincerely (66:8), both promising that He will remove their bad deeds, then a different reward.
tree:0xxxygf1vt9wkf.relation: Taqwa and repentance both wipe away sins.

tree:1wsy4wr1p0kdx9.why: Neighbouring surahs, same promise in the singular: whoever believes and does good (64:9) or whoever is mindful of God (65:5) has his sins removed, then the reward differs.

tree:0fyvpy61bqzmag.why: Only the common phrase 'it is not for us to' is shared. Shu'ayb refusing to return to his people's religion (7:89) and the believers told how to answer the slander (24:16) are different subjects.

tree:0fk2x2a180rbey.why: Both deny that God has a son: glory be to Him (4:171) and how could He when He has no consort (6:101).
tree:0fk2x2a180rbey.relation: The same denial argued two ways: transcendence and creation.

tree:1mw42hv15vlw09.why: Two prophets disowning any authority over revelation in the same words: Jesus never said what he had no right to (5:116), Muhammad cannot change the Quran of his own accord (10:15).
tree:1mw42hv15vlw09.relation: Similarity: a messenger only conveys; he does not add or alter.

tree:16qmkb31fhspnv.why: Same surah, same closing that differs in its last word: 'what they used to do' with two different verbs (6:108, 6:159). A classic memorizer's trap.

tree:1yycytr1njvhun.why: Only 'be sent down on you from' is shared. The envy of those who disbelieve (2:105) and the rain at Badr (8:11) are unrelated subjects.

tree:19z3yw60lpqee8.why: Both are signs of the sky with lightning: He sends down hail from mountains of cloud (24:43) and water that revives the earth (30:24).
tree:19z3yw60lpqee8.relation: From the same sky come harm and mercy, fear and hope.

tree:0n3j1do00bg3zi.why: Turning back on one's heels, both as a test of following the Messenger: the change of qibla (2:143) and the rumour of his death at Uhud (3:144).
tree:0n3j1do00bg3zi.relation: Tests that show who truly follows the Messenger.

tree:1dxj4qt171oc6l.why: Who guides to the truth: God, not the partners (10:35), and the Book the jinn heard (46:30).
tree:1dxj4qt171oc6l.relation: God guides to the truth, and so does His Book.

tree:1efd0us02xe9bk.why: Only 'the Day of Resurrection, then' is shared, a common time phrase. Jesus raised up (3:55) and the one who defrauds (3:161) are different subjects.

tree:14y8m231k2kl3n.why: Only 'the Day of Resurrection, what' is shared, and the 'what' is a different word in each (a negation in 5:36, a relative pronoun in 16:92).

tree:0e55gvs19xgwqk.why: Joseph (12:22) and Moses (28:14) receive judgment and knowledge in almost identical ayat, differing only by 'and was mature'; Lot (21:74) shares the gift but continues with his rescue. A key memorizer card.
tree:0e55gvs19xgwqk.relation: Similarity: God's gift of wisdom to prophets as the reward of the doers of good, each then tested.

tree:08uastr14m8w9r.why: The deniers' question 'when we are bones ...?' twice in al-Isra with the same tail (17:49, 17:98) and once in an-Nazi'at with 'decayed' (79:11). The memorizer must keep the tails apart.
tree:08uastr14m8w9r.relation: The same denial of resurrection, answered each time by God's power to create.

tree:0ozij4o0dy5loc.why: Those who believe in God and His messengers: rewarded for not dividing between them (4:152), counted among the truthful and the witnesses (57:19), and the Garden prepared for them (57:21).
tree:0ozij4o0dy5loc.relation: Faith in all the messengers and what it earns.

tree:1yohl1b0scod55.why: The rebuke 'were not My verses recited to you?' to the people of the Fire, with three different endings: turning on heels (23:66), denying (23:105), arrogance (45:31).
tree:1yohl1b0scod55.relation: Every excuse falls away: the verses were recited, and they turned away.

tree:0w9cswh13prj9t.why: Three deeds done seeking God's pleasure: giving one's self (2:207), spending wealth (2:265), and doing good in private counsel (4:114). Same intention, three forms.
tree:0w9cswh13prj9t.relation: Seeking God's pleasure is what gives a deed its worth.

tree:0mwec57183785h.why: The same line of prophets three times close together in al-Baqara: the god of Jacob's fathers (2:133), the faith of believers (2:136), the false claim that they were Jews or Christians (2:140).
tree:0mwec57183785h.relation: One chain of prophets, one religion, claimed wrongly by others.

tree:0j9ami71pxbnxj.why: Following only the revelation: the Prophet says he follows what is revealed to him from his Lord (7:203) and is told twice to follow it (10:109, 33:2), with different tails.
tree:0j9ami71pxbnxj.relation: The Messenger's only path is the revelation.

tree:0tc7mbo0ndco6o.why: A classic: told to follow what God sent down, they answer that they follow their fathers, with 'found' as two different verbs (2:170, 31:21); 7:3 gives the command itself.
tree:0tc7mbo0ndco6o.relation: Revelation against blind imitation of the forefathers.

tree:1vrk9bc18yugj8.why: An appointed term followed by 'then': the term of a life and the return to God (6:60), the stages of the unborn child (22:5), and the sacrificial animals until they reach the House (22:33). The two al-Hajj ayat are a memorizer's pair; 22:33 has a different subject.

tree:0ovpt240gsaa5s.why: God took the covenant of the prophets (3:81), of those given the Book (3:187), and of the Children of Israel (5:12). Same opening, three covenants.
tree:0ovpt240gsaa5s.relation: Covenants taken by God and how each was kept or broken.

tree:1j6tc3n0g54z2h.why: Mocked messengers and the end of their deniers: 'then I seized them, and how was My punishment', with two different last words (13:32, 40:5 vs 22:44).
tree:1j6tc3n0g54z2h.relation: God gives the deniers time, then seizes them.

tree:0rd6fq21cpbgoq.why: Classic mutashabih: Pharaoh's people and those before them were seized for their sins, closing differently in 3:11 and 8:52; 40:21 applies the same to earlier nations.
tree:0rd6fq21cpbgoq.relation: Past nations seized for their sins as a warning to the present.

tree:1dbfakn037nd47.why: The believers driven out of their homes: promised reward (3:195), permitted to fight back (22:40), and given a share of the spoils (59:8).
tree:1dbfakn037nd47.relation: The emigrants' sacrifice and God's answer to it.

tree:1meef7u1xx39vm.why: The Children of Israel told to enter the gate prostrating: the order of the commands is reversed between 2:58 and 7:161, and 4:154 recalls it among the covenants. A key memorizer card.
tree:1meef7u1xx39vm.relation: One command in the story told three times.

tree:0m5buw71wsayih.why: Abraham's words in al-Baqara: his prayer for a safe land (2:126), his argument with the king (2:258), and his request to see the dead raised (2:260). Same opening, close together.
tree:0m5buw71wsayih.relation: Abraham's faith seen in prayer, in debate, and in seeking certainty.

tree:1b5n5ft1sdm71z.why: When God is mentioned: believers' hearts tremble (8:2, 22:35), while the hearts of those who deny the Hereafter shrink when He alone is mentioned (39:45).
tree:1b5n5ft1sdm71z.relation: Contrast: the same remembrance moves one heart to awe and another to disgust.

tree:0n1pger04zd0sl.why: Divorce rulings that open the same way: 2:231 and 2:232 share the first clause then split (do not retain to harm / do not prevent remarriage); 65:1 addresses the Prophet. A memorizer's card.

tree:0pz25k21owkuqw.why: Each time a test comes, a group of them turns: fearing people when fighting is ordered (4:77), turning away from judgment (24:48), associating after relief (30:33).
tree:0pz25k21owkuqw.relation: A pattern of character: a party turns away when faith is tested.

tree:1nfr8k10ba8tdj.why: 'Then I would surely be among the wrongdoers' with different lead-ins: said to the Prophet (2:145), by the witnesses (5:107), and by Noah (11:31). A memorizer's trap.

tree:0lo4iye0uck68o.why: Man's character when evil touches him: despairing (17:83), full of long prayer (41:51), anxious (70:20). 17:83 and 41:51 share the whole first half.
tree:0lo4iye0uck68o.relation: Human weakness in hardship, described from three sides.

tree:1lk3reb08xgnxf.why: God sends a wind on a people: as help for the believers against the confederates (33:9), and as a raging wind destroying 'Ad (41:16, 54:19).
tree:1lk3reb08xgnxf.relation: Contrast: the same wind is victory for believers and destruction for deniers.

tree:1tudq9x015hovz.why: Seeking refuge with God: 7:200 and 41:36 are nearly identical about Satan's prompting, differing in the closing names; 40:56 seeks refuge from proud disputers. A classic memorizer card.

tree:0xq1yrb0urf22x.why: Pharaoh and his chiefs met the signs with arrogance: 'a criminal people' in 7:133 and 10:75, 'a haughty people' in 23:46. Same story, one word changed.

tree:0081pi81he479c.why: Three prayers in Al Imran asking forgiveness of sins, each adding a different request: protection from the Fire (3:16), steadfastness (3:147), dying with the righteous (3:193).

tree:140rdyf1uubj17.why: 'Forgive us and have mercy on us' in three prayers, each closing with a different praise of God: our Protector (2:286), the best of forgivers (7:155), the best of the merciful (23:109).

tree:0cjzslx1in2ah3.why: The command to set one's face to the religion, upright: once in Yunus (10:105) and twice in ar-Rum (30:30, 30:43) with different continuations. A clear memorizer's card.
tree:0cjzslx1in2ah3.relation: The same command tied to the natural disposition (30:30) and to the coming Day (30:43).

tree:0oo78441hbmy9a.why: 'Most of them do not reason' closes three ayat with different lead-ins (and / rather / none). The subjects differ (invented taboos, polytheists who admit God sends rain, people calling from outside the rooms), so its value is mainly for the memorizer.

tree:0wvw7n01k507bq.why: Iblis refusing to prostrate, told three ways: refused and was arrogant (2:34), refused to be with those who prostrate (15:31), refused, end of ayah (20:116). Key memorizer card.
tree:0wvw7n01k507bq.relation: One story: pride as the first disobedience.

tree:1bm26zk1nlwmty.why: The polytheists follow only conjecture and only guess: 6:116 and 10:66 in the third person, 6:148 addressing them directly. Same words, a pronoun to watch.
tree:1bm26zk1nlwmty.relation: Polytheism rests on guesswork, not knowledge.

tree:17jx9970epbjsl.why: What are the deniers waiting for? 6:158 and 16:33 open identically and then differ; 18:55 asks what keeps people from believing, with the same expectation of punishment.
tree:17jx9970epbjsl.relation: Delaying faith until the signs or the punishment come, when it is too late.

tree:1ma02dh1hpdbh9.why: 2:282 and 4:29 both make an exception for trade, 'unless it be a trade' (cash trade in hand, trade by mutual consent): two rulings on dealings in the same words. In 28:19 the verb is second person ('unless you want to be a tyrant'), a different word that only looks the same.
tree:1ma02dh1hpdbh9.changes: Removed 28:19: its verb is 'you be' (second person, addressed to Moses), not 'it be' (a trade); a different word in a different structure.
tree:1ma02dh1hpdbh9.relation: Two rulings on trade: debts must be written except cash trade; wealth may not be taken except by trade with consent.

check.why: In 28:19, 'that you be' is second person masculine (a tyrant). In 2:282 and 4:29 it is 'that it be' (a trade). A different word, so removing it is right.

tree:0w7ezrk1g6xr78.why: The hypocrites exposed with 'truly it is they who are ...': the corrupters (2:12), the fools (2:13), the liars (58:18). The two al-Baqara ayat are a famous pair with different endings.
tree:0w7ezrk1g6xr78.relation: What the hypocrites call others is what they are.

tree:1x2of3p0082lab.why: 'Evil indeed is what ...': twice about bearing burdens (6:31, 16:25), once about how they judge a daughter's birth (16:59). The verb at the end is the trap.

tree:1nje9a41u2bicq.why: 'Except a few of them' in the Talut story twice (2:246 turning away from fighting, 2:249 drinking from the river) and in 5:13 about the Children of Israel's treachery. Same people, same pattern.
tree:1nje9a41u2bicq.relation: Only a few remain faithful when tested.

tree:1jutam60m0eaka.why: All three rows stay. 4:22 and 4:23, neighbouring rulings on forbidden marriages, both close with 'except what has already passed'. 41:43 has the same exception with the same relative and the same particle, then another verb ('what was said to the messengers before you'): exactly where a reciter could carry 'has passed' over. Different subject, same words and structure, so it is not removed.
tree:1jutam60m0eaka.relation: What is past is pardoned in marriage law; what is said to the Prophet was said to every messenger before him.

tree:0tl3j3515aahux.why: 'Except whom He has mercy on': no refuge from the flood but His mercy (11:43), people keep differing except whom your Lord has mercy on (11:119), and none is helped on the Day except whom God has mercy on (44:42).
tree:0tl3j3515aahux.relation: God's mercy as the only exception from ruin.

tree:02og4jy1dmoxfa.why: 27:87 and 39:68 describe the blowing of the Trumpet in nearly the same words, terror in one and swooning in the other, both with 'except whom God wills'. In 25:57 the one who wills is the person himself ('except whoever wills to take a way to his Lord'): the relative is the subject of the verb, a different structure.
tree:02og4jy1dmoxfa.changes: Removed 25:57: there the person is the one who wills, while in 27:87 and 39:68 God wills; a different structure.
tree:02og4jy1dmoxfa.relation: The two blasts of the Trumpet told twice: terror and swooning, with God's exception in both.

tree:0t3ldzx0va7zjd.why: 'Only a clear warner' with three lead-ins: 'he is' about the Prophet (7:184), 'I am' from Noah (26:115), 'and I am' from the Prophet (46:9). A memorizer's trap.

check.why: Keep is right: 'only a clear warner' with three different lead-ins is a real memorizer trap.

tree:1kx13gd1hef4d9.why: Loss in this world and the next with no helper: deeds void (3:22), punishment of the disbelievers (3:56), and the hypocrites who return to disbelief (9:74), whose tail differs.

tree:05qvi0i0u6ryg0.why: To God belongs the heavens and the earth, and to God all returns: 'matters return' in 3:109 and 57:5, 'the destination' in 24:42. A memorizer's trap.

tree:0ksqk6109qz2ld.why: The killing of the prophets without right listed among the crimes of the Children of Israel, three times with different continuations (3:112, 3:181, 4:155).
tree:0ksqk6109qz2ld.relation: One crime recalled in each charge sheet against them.

tree:0ycm4a709lv8ql.why: The Garden promised to the mindful: described with rivers and shade (13:35), with rivers of water, milk, wine and honey (47:15), and as the eternal Garden contrasted with the Fire (25:15).

tree:0lp9ixr1dglw9z.why: Worldly life, then the Day: the enjoyment of this life then return to Us (10:23), then brought to account (28:61), then disowning each other (29:25).
tree:0lp9ixr1dglw9z.relation: What is enjoyed together in this life is followed by reckoning.

tree:0qweih90ysoem3.why: Wanting this life and its adornment: paid in full here (11:15), what is with God is better (28:60), the Prophet's wives offered the choice (33:28).
tree:0qweih90ysoem3.relation: The choice between this world's adornment and what is with God.

tree:0gs3pec10m5m9g.why: 31:33 and 35:5 share the warning 'let not the life of this world deceive you'; 18:28 tells the Prophet not to turn his eyes from the poor believers seeking this world's adornment. Same warning about the world's lure.

check.why: Keep is right: 31:33 and 35:5 share a long clause, and 18:28 fits the theme.

tree:1ksc6m802fe51k.why: 'Fear God, to whom you will be gathered' closes rulings on hunting in ihram (5:96) and on private talk (58:9); 6:72 has 'and He it is'. A memorizer's trap.

tree:1bq27aj19c5lad.why: 6:99 and 16:10 both open 'He it is who sends down water from the sky' and then list what grows from it. In 4:136 the verb is passive ('the Book that was sent down before'), and 'from' starts 'before', not 'the sky': a different word and structure.
tree:1bq27aj19c5lad.changes: Removed 4:136: a passive verb about the earlier Book, with 'from before', not water from the sky.
tree:1bq27aj19c5lad.relation: Rain from the sky as a sign: plants, fruit and drink, told twice.

tree:13yi9k80a0wg6s.why: The Quran confirms what came before it: 6:92, and twice with 'it is not forged, but a confirmation ... and a detailing' with different objects (10:37, 12:111).

tree:12p0zrz1mn1k8l.why: Rewarded by the best of what they did (29:7, 39:35) and punished by the worst of what they did (41:27). Same words, one changed.
tree:12p0zrz1mn1k8l.relation: Contrast: believers judged by their best deeds, deniers by their worst.

tree:0iq8gqk1bhnp1u.why: He who gives life and death: Abraham's answer to the king (2:258), and twice as His description with different tails (23:80, 40:68).
tree:0iq8gqk1bhnp1u.relation: Life and death as the proof of the Lord.

tree:0qi9dff0iurgpv.why: Both speak of the believers among you and of succession on earth: God promises to make them successors (24:55), and tells them to spend from what He made them successors over (57:7).
tree:0qi9dff0iurgpv.relation: Succession on earth is both a promise and a trust to spend from.

tree:0v455xi1ocvaj8.why: 'Those who were mindful of their Lord': 3:198 and 39:20 open with the same 'but' and give gardens vs lofty rooms; 39:73 shows them driven to the Garden in groups. A real slip for memorizers.
tree:0v455xi1ocvaj8.relation: The reward of the mindful: gardens, rooms, and the welcome at the gates.

tree:1nsju9x0orrfnr.why: 'Those of them who did wrong': an exception in 2:150 and 29:46, and those who changed the word in 7:162 (where 'of them' is the detail that differs from 2:59). Useful for memorizers.

tree:1wugham0nmo2z8.why: Only 'those who disbelieved, to' is shared, in three senses: until the Day (3:55), gathered to Hell (8:36), driven to Hell (39:71). The Hell pair already has its own card; 3:55 is unrelated.

tree:0el1dob0kyv821.why: Only the phrase 'those who disbelieved in their Lord' is shared; the three ayat say different things (they set up equals, they bear chains, their deeds are ashes). Nothing to confuse or ponder together.

tree:0nksemv1r7fi4z.why: Only 'those who disbelieved: no' is shared, with three unrelated sayings (the Hour will not come, do not listen to the Quran, make no excuses today).

check.why: Drop is right: only 'those who disbelieved: do not' is shared, with three unrelated sayings.

tree:0qfhhcv138dpnn.why: 3:10 and 3:116 are identical for most of the ayah (wealth and children will not avail the deniers) and end differently: fuel of the Fire / companions of the Fire. A classic pair for memorizers. In 34:31 'never' governs their own vow 'we will never believe', a different verb and structure.
tree:0qfhhcv138dpnn.changes: Removed 34:31: its 'never' governs 'we believe', not 'will avail them'.

tree:1sgi4uy19fng6y.why: 'Those who disbelieved will have' is a stock opening of the punishment formula, found in many places. These three ayat add nothing that sets them apart from the rest.

tree:0jond7x0s2u9j3.why: Only 'those who disbelieved ... if' is shared, in three unrelated settings (prayer in fear, ransom on the Day, wishing they were Muslims).

tree:02nmnmv0m7a3yd.why: The deniers' demand for a sign: 13:7 and 13:27 identical and then answered differently; 25:32 asks why the Quran was not sent down all at once.
tree:02nmnmv0m7a3yd.relation: Demands for signs, answered with what the Messenger is and why revelation came gradually.

tree:0xpvho40vpzf20.why: 'Where are your / My partners whom you claimed?': 'your partners' in 6:22 and 'My partners' twice in al-Qasas (28:62, 28:74). A pronoun a memorizer must hold.

tree:0r1qvd80o2xaue.why: All three rows stay. 'Those who do not find' is the same words and structure in all three: those who find nothing but their effort (9:79), nothing to spend (9:91), no means to marry (24:33). The subject differs only in what is lacking, which is no reason to remove 24:33; it is the place a reciter could slip.
tree:0r1qvd80o2xaue.relation: Those who lack means: mocked by hypocrites, excused from war, told to stay chaste until God enriches them.

tree:0xfiepl1yo7i4v.why: Only 'those after them' is shared: the followers of the messengers fighting (2:253) and the nations after Noah (40:31). Unrelated subjects.

tree:0cqcfp2151v06k.why: Three places telling what God forbade the Jews and why: for their wrongdoing (4:160), for their transgression (6:146), and 'We did not wrong them' (16:118).
tree:0cqcfp2151v06k.relation: The prohibitions on the Jews were a penalty for their own wrong.

tree:0zad4xc1dczn12.why: Only 'those who are, from ...' is shared, a grammatical frame with different objects (signs, idle talk, prayer) and opposite subjects (deniers and believers).

tree:0jxw71m02ro8t0.why: 21:16 and 38:27: 'We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them' in play / in vain. In 44:29 'and what' is a negation ('and they were not given respite'), a different word, like the owner's example.
tree:0jxw71m02ro8t0.changes: Removed 44:29: its 'and what' is a negation, not 'and what is between them'.
tree:0jxw71m02ro8t0.relation: Creation has a purpose: not play, not in vain.

tree:1p4sjnt1pcwljb.why: 11:107 and 11:108 are mirror ayat: the people of the Fire and of the Garden abide as long as heavens and earth last, except as your Lord wills, with different endings. In 19:93 'except' follows 'everyone in the heavens and earth' and is not followed by 'what your Lord wills': a different structure.
tree:1p4sjnt1pcwljb.changes: Removed 19:93: a different structure (everyone will come as a servant).
tree:1p4sjnt1pcwljb.relation: Contrast: the same eternity for the wretched and the happy, closed differently (He does what He wills / a gift never cut off).

check.why: In 19:93 the exception follows a negation ('there is none in the heavens and earth but'), a different structure, so removing it is right.

tree:0024pow1u55k90.why: Questions about the heavens and earth answered by 'say: God': to whom belongs (6:12, 'to God'), who is Lord (13:16), who provides (34:24).
tree:0024pow1u55k90.relation: Arguing from creation to God's sole right to worship.

check.why: Keep is right: a question about the heavens and earth answered by 'say: God', three times on the same argument.

tree:0mfcqy102whqmf.why: Only 'the heavens and the earth, not' is shared, and the 'not' starts a different sentence each time (no god but He, it will not come but suddenly, they are not equal).

tree:0hcoqvy0go1swa.why: Intercession only for one granted it: who took a covenant with the Merciful (19:87), whom the Merciful permits (20:109), who bore witness to the truth (43:86).
tree:0hcoqvy0go1swa.relation: Intercession belongs to God and is given only by His leave.

tree:0au26pz1s6au7b.why: Sun, moon and stars made subservient by His command (7:54, 16:12, same words), and prostrating to Him (22:18).
tree:0au26pz1s6au7b.relation: The heavenly bodies serve and worship their Creator.

tree:1usc1n11rsslmv.why: Glad tidings to those who do good deeds: gardens (2:25), a great reward (17:9), a good reward (18:2). Neighbouring 17:9 and 18:2 differ by one word.

tree:1m13ar911h020j.why: Punishment 'because of what they used to ...', ending with three different verbs: defiantly disobey (6:49), turn away (6:157), spread corruption (16:88). A memorizer's trap.

tree:15w2typ1r6lyu1.why: The punishment on the Day of Resurrection: doubled for the sinner (25:69), the evil punishment twice in az-Zumar (39:24, 39:47).

tree:1x0ye7m1mydyye.why: The Book, judgment and prophethood given to prophets: none would then call to worship himself (3:79), if these reject it others will hold it (6:89), and given to the Children of Israel (45:16).
tree:1x0ye7m1mydyye.relation: The trust of the Book and prophethood, and how it passes on.

tree:1wtpprn09e5tjn.why: Lying knowingly: some of the People of the Book say lies about God while they know (3:75, 3:78), and hypocrites swear to lies while they know (58:14). The verb before it (say / swear) is the trap.
tree:1wtpprn09e5tjn.relation: Deliberate lying about God and under oath.

tree:014w1v11hjl7m3.why: Only 'God' next to 'those who disbelieved' is shared, across three unrelated sentences (worst of creatures, the Fire promised, turned back in rage).

tree:0zpzdiq1m8mfb2.why: God, the One, the Subduer, closing three ayat with different lead-ins: Joseph's question to his prison companions (12:39), 'no god but' (38:65), 'He is' (39:4).
tree:0zpzdiq1m8mfb2.relation: Oneness argued against many lords, against other gods, against a son.

tree:0hjyokj1vx4b3f.why: 'God sees His servants' closes three ayat: after God's pleasure for the mindful (3:15), after 'your duty is only to convey' (3:20), and after the believer of Pharaoh's people entrusts his affair to God (40:44).

tree:06b06240svkys2.why: Selling God's signs or covenant for a small price: the believing People of the Book do not (3:199), the oath-breakers did (9:9), and believers are told not to (16:95).
tree:06b06240svkys2.relation: The small price of this world against what is with God.

tree:0iybcsn0zasqcj.why: 'Better and more lasting': the converted magicians about God (20:73), and what is with God set against worldly enjoyment, twice with different tails (28:60, 42:36).
tree:0iybcsn0zasqcj.relation: What is with God outlasts everything this world gives.

tree:0aqsjx50dsrx1x.why: 'God is full of bounty' on the worlds (2:251), on the believers (3:152), great bounty (3:174). The ending is the trap.

tree:0wboesr0pcnp0n.why: 59:6 and 59:7 are neighbouring ayat on what God gave His Messenger as spoils without fighting, opening almost the same. 9:97 has a different governing verb ('what God sent down to His Messenger').
tree:0wboesr0pcnp0n.changes: Removed 9:97: a different governing verb (sent down, not gave as spoils).

tree:02ee8721umpb1o.why: 'Those whom God has favoured among the prophets': the company of the obedient (4:69) and the prophets who fell in prostration (19:58). 6:53 has a different verb (the mocking 'has God favoured these among us?') and a different 'from'.
tree:02ee8721umpb1o.changes: Removed 6:53: a different verb and structure.
tree:02ee8721umpb1o.relation: The favoured company: whoever obeys is with them (4:69), and who they were (19:58).

tree:1tp2bkq1nq35pc.why: 'God is Free of need, Praiseworthy' closes three ayat on spending, gratitude and disbelief, with three different lead-ins ('that', 'then indeed', 'and God'). A memorizer's trap.
tree:1tp2bkq1nq35pc.relation: God needs neither our charity, our thanks nor our faith.

tree:0jq3g8p0gzzczz.why: A pattern: 'whoever ... God, then God is ...' with three different closings (swift in account, mighty and wise, severe in punishment). Subjects differ; the value is keeping the closings apart.

tree:0wdddkn05ioug7.why: 'For them is a punishment' is one of the commonest formulas; here it follows different subjects (disbelieving in the signs, hurting the Prophet, straying from God's way). Nothing to set these three apart.

tree:0q13sgk03k6wwq.why: 'God ... what He wills' is a very common phrase; here with three different verbs (erases, does, creates) and unrelated subjects. Nothing specific to learn from these three.

check.why: Drop is right: a very common phrase with different verbs.

tree:1x8jgv01m862k8.why: Barring believers from God's way and seeking to make it crooked: the People of the Book (3:99) and Shu'ayb's people (7:86), in nearly the same words. In 9:18 'who believes' is the subject of a different sentence (who maintains the mosques).
tree:1x8jgv01m862k8.changes: Removed 9:18: 'who believes' there is the subject, not the one turned away; a different structure.
tree:1x8jgv01m862k8.relation: The same sin in two peoples: turning believers from God's path and wanting it crooked.

check.why: In 9:18, 'who believes in God' is the subject of a different sentence about maintaining mosques, not the object of 'bar from God's way'. Removing it is right.

tree:1amnnfb02xcpyt.why: 'God and His Messenger, those ...': those who obey them will receive mercy (9:71), those who oppose them are among the most humiliated (58:20), the emigrants who support them are the truthful (59:8).
tree:1amnnfb02xcpyt.relation: Contrast: obeying and supporting God and His Messenger vs opposing them.

tree:1ubgnxt083sohz.why: 8:20 and 8:46 both command 'obey God and His Messenger, and do not ...' with a different warning (turning away / disputing). In 9:29 the words fall in 'what God and His Messenger forbade, and they do not follow', a different structure.
tree:1ubgnxt083sohz.changes: Removed 9:29: 'and not' starts a new clause about the enemy, not a command to believers.

tree:0y1qiso0et6lxy.why: These are three of many an-Nisa ayat closing with 'and God is ...'; the subjects (spending, manslaughter, emigration) are unrelated. A general pattern, not a card.

check.why: Drop is right: a general closing pattern with unrelated subjects.

tree:18q65fe1xqal8a.why: 'And for them is a punishment' is a stock closing; the three ayat (hypocrites, those who reject the signs, apostates) end with three different adjectives but share nothing more specific.

tree:16bpoqk10th5w2.why: All three rows stay. 'God judges between you' is the same words and structure in 4:141, 22:69 and 60:10. The first two go on 'on the Day of Resurrection'; 60:10 stops and closes with 'God is Knowing, Wise'. That is exactly where a reciter could add the Day, so 60:10 belongs in the card.
tree:16bpoqk10th5w2.relation: God judges between people both in His law now (60:10) and on the Day (4:141, 22:69).

tree:0l71jty1p058d0.why: 'Did I not tell you?' from God to the angels (2:33), from Jacob when his sight returned (12:96), and from the best of the garden owners (68:28). Each time the one who knew is proven right.
tree:0l71jty1p058d0.relation: Knowledge vindicated: God, Jacob, and the wise brother.

tree:107xelt195stpp.why: Mankind as one nation: they were one and then differed (2:213), God could have made them one (11:118), and if not for that risk He would give the deniers houses of silver (43:33).
tree:107xelt195stpp.relation: Unity and difference among people as part of God's plan.

tree:1bhaehy0n1x5lw.why: Asking for a short delay: from the fighting (4:77), from the punishment (14:44), from death to give charity (63:10). Three forms of the verb, one wish.
tree:1bhaehy0n1x5lw.relation: Wishing for time that will not be given.

tree:0lzvu2u154ixgg.why: 'And to God is the destination' closes three ayat after different lead-ins: a warning about taking disbelievers as allies (3:28), God's dominion (24:42), purification (35:18).

tree:0x35lyp1i5jmqh.why: Classic al-Ma'ida pair: 'to God is your return, all of you, and He will inform you of what you ...' ending 'differ about' (5:48) vs 'do' (5:105); 11:4 has the short form.

tree:1vdnadi0ymscpk.why: 24:48 and 24:51 contrast the hypocrites who turn away when called to God and His Messenger for judgment with the believers who say we hear and obey. In 4:100 the governing word is different (emigrating to God and His Messenger).
tree:1vdnadi0ymscpk.changes: Removed 4:100: a different governing word (emigrating to, not called to).
tree:1vdnadi0ymscpk.relation: Contrast: two answers to the same call, turning away and 'we hear and we obey'.

tree:0b3f9k51jnikk5.why: Taking a way to one's Lord: 73:19 and 76:29 are identical ('this is a reminder, so whoever wills ...'), and 25:57 says the Prophet asks no wage except that people take that way.
tree:0b3f9k51jnikk5.relation: The message is a reminder; the choice to take the path is left to each person.

tree:12h12qt1h5jk5x.why: The Prophet states his command: to worship God and not associate (13:36), to worship the Lord of this city (27:91), to worship God sincerely (39:11). Close wording, different objects.

tree:1ajoseb1tojsad.why: 'That was a nation that has passed' twice in al-Baqara (2:134, 2:141, identical), and 13:30 sends the Prophet to a nation before which nations had passed.
tree:1ajoseb1tojsad.relation: Each generation bears its own deeds; ancestry does not save.

tree:0lbvlob1w7uw67.why: 'Had God willed He would have made you one nation, but ...' with three reasons: to test you (5:48), He guides and leaves astray (16:93), He admits whom He wills to His mercy (42:8).
tree:0lbvlob1w7uw67.relation: Why people differ: test, guidance, mercy.

tree:0jq5i2d16zejsr.why: The real pair here, 8:28 and 9:22 ('with God is a great reward'), already has its own card. 31:34 ('with Him is knowledge of the Hour') is a different phrase, so this card only repeats the pair with an outsider.

tree:1n6is4b1q6ahj5.why: 'God is Strong' with two closings: severe in punishment (8:52) and Mighty (57:25, 58:21). Both later ayat are about God supporting His messengers.
tree:1n6is4b1q6ahj5.relation: God's strength shown in punishing deniers and making His messengers prevail.

tree:03dfpkj0cbh4g1.why: 'And indeed God, He is ...' with three closings: Mighty and Wise (3:62), best of providers (22:58), Free of need and Praiseworthy (22:64). Two in one surah, close together.

tree:0tjqro20t5x9ik.why: 'You follow only ...': 'a bewitched man' in the deniers' mouth (17:47, 25:8, near-identical with the same next ayah), and 'conjecture' said to the polytheists (6:148).
tree:0tjqro20t5x9ik.relation: The deniers' charge turned back on them: they are the ones following mere guesses.

tree:1lh8pd80x69mi2.why: 'If you are patient and mindful' three times in Al Imran: their plot will not harm you (3:120), angels will reinforce you (3:125), that is of firm resolve (3:186).
tree:1lh8pd80x69mi2.relation: Patience and taqwa as the believers' defence against enemies.

tree:0oe3ut41x9lmm8.why: 'If you disbelieve, then ...': twice in an-Nisa with 'to God belongs what is in the heavens and earth' and different closing names (4:131, 4:170), and 'God is free of need of you' (39:7).
tree:0oe3ut41x9lmm8.relation: Disbelief harms only the disbeliever; God needs nothing.

tree:12inzzf0vlgyv1.why: 'Indeed your Lord is full of ...': forgiveness for people despite their wrong (13:6), bounty on people (27:73), forgiveness and painful punishment (41:43).
tree:12inzzf0vlgyv1.relation: God's forgiveness and bounty held together with His punishment.

tree:0lxxfkr1cxauf5.why: Only 'if you have' is shared: a victory from God in the hypocrites' talk (4:141) and a plot in the challenge on the Day (77:39). Unrelated.

tree:1rur5qx1q9cnkt.why: 'If you must do something' closes a proposal in three stories: Joseph's brother suggesting the well (12:10), Lot offering his daughters (15:71), Abraham's people calling to burn him (21:68).

tree:1p6zkxz1suyeoz.why: 'If you are in doubt ...': about the Quran (2:23), about the Prophet's religion (10:104), about the Resurrection (22:5), each followed by an answer.
tree:1p6zkxz1suyeoz.relation: Doubt answered by a challenge, a stand, and a proof from creation.

tree:0z2352l0l20t83.why: 51:59 and 52:47, at the ends of neighbouring surahs, warn: 'indeed for the wrongdoers' a share like their companions' / a punishment before that. 39:47 is 'if the wrongdoers had', a different particle and structure.
tree:0z2352l0l20t83.changes: Removed 39:47: its particle opens a hypothetical ransom, a different structure.
tree:0z2352l0l20t83.relation: Two closing warnings to the wrongdoers in neighbouring surahs.

check.why: 39:47 'and if those who did wrong had' is a different particle construction from the other rows, so removing it is right.

tree:0t4qw7s1k6u07m.why: The inheritance ayat repeat 'if he / they / she has no child' with different pronouns (4:11, 4:12, 4:176). Essential for memorizers of the shares.

tree:0bokegc05f0e26.why: 'This is surely a sorcerer': Pharaoh's chiefs (7:109) and Pharaoh himself (26:34) say 'learned', near-identical with the same next ayah; the deniers of Muhammad say 'clear' (10:2).
tree:0bokegc05f0e26.relation: The same accusation against Moses and against Muhammad.

tree:0n2yt9b1jp5ziv.why: 'This is surely a ... thing' with three endings: wondrous (11:72, Sarah), astonishing (38:5) and intended (38:6), the last two neighbours. A memorizer's trap.

tree:19vms7s0lzu71a.why: 'I am only a warner': and bringer of good news (7:188), clear (26:115 Noah, 46:9 Muhammad). The lead-ins and the endings differ.
tree:19vms7s0lzu71a.relation: Every messenger only warns; he has no power of his own.

tree:0dezfip04gxqv7.why: 'And we will surely guard him': Joseph's brothers promise it twice (12:12, 12:63) and fail; God says it of the Reminder (15:9) and keeps it.
tree:0dezfip04gxqv7.relation: Contrast: people's promise to guard fails, God's guarding of the Quran does not.

tree:1h4ja9b1r67mhf.why: 'I am only a clear warner': 'and only' after 'the signs / the knowledge is with God' (29:50, 67:26), and 'that I am' in 38:70. A memorizer's trap.

tree:10iqp4y02hmww6.why: God sent down His tranquillity: at Hunayn (9:26), in the cave (9:40), at Hudaybiya (48:26). Same words in three moments of fear.
tree:10iqp4y02hmww6.relation: Calm sent down from God at moments of danger.

tree:0r497gs0y4u0j2.why: When told to believe in or follow what God sent down, they answer with their own: what was sent to us (2:91), what we found our fathers on (2:170, 31:21).
tree:0r497gs0y4u0j2.relation: Rejecting revelation in favour of tribe and forefathers.

tree:07ri62q0ox7opc.why: 'We sent down the Book to you': to explain what they differ in (16:64), is it not enough (29:51), for people in truth (39:41). Three openings to keep apart.
tree:07ri62q0ox7opc.relation: The purposes of the Book sent down.

tree:0kj0i6603lsvko.why: 'We produced after them another generation' (6:6, 23:31) and 'other generations' (23:42). Singular vs plural, two in the same surah.

tree:1bztgvr1rcwl85.why: 'Your duty is only to convey' with three tails: God sees His servants (3:20), on Us is the reckoning (13:40), 'the clear conveying' (16:82).
tree:1bztgvr1rcwl85.relation: The Messenger conveys; guidance and reckoning belong to God.

tree:1sjezpg0w96uik.why: 9:55 and 9:85 are near-identical about the hypocrites' wealth and children, with small differences ('so that' vs 'that', 'and' vs 'nor'); 33:33 shares 'God only wants' for the household of the Prophet.
tree:1sjezpg0w96uik.relation: Contrast: God wills punishment through the hypocrites' wealth, and purification for the Prophet's household.

tree:12134y41d2vxhg.why: Knowing it is the truth from their Lord: the believers about the parable (2:26), the People of the Book about the qibla (2:144), those given knowledge about the revelation (22:54, 'from your Lord').
tree:12134y41d2vxhg.relation: Who recognises the truth, and what they do with that knowledge.

tree:10hkxzs0vd4ibg.why: 'Indeed He, of all things, is ...' with three closings: encompassing (41:54), knowing (42:12), seeing (67:19). A memorizer's trap.

tree:0ielk09020od5h.why: 'I fear God, Lord of the worlds' from Adam's righteous son refusing to kill (5:28), and the same words from Satan disowning his followers (8:48, 59:16).
tree:0ielk09020od5h.relation: Contrast: the same words as true fear in one mouth and as a hollow excuse in Satan's.

tree:1qndnua1ul3c0o.why: 15:4 and 26:208: 'We never destroyed a town but that it had' a known term / warners. 28:58 opens 'how many a town We destroyed', a different structure with no exception.
tree:1qndnua1ul3c0o.changes: Removed 28:58: 'how many' instead of the negation with exception, a different structure.
tree:1qndnua1ul3c0o.relation: No town is destroyed without a term and without warners.

check.why: Removing 28:58 is right: 'how many' is a different word from 'never'.

tree:1tuq4ja1jr75b4.why: Lot saved with his family except his wife: 'she was of those who stayed behind' (7:83, 29:32) vs 'We decreed her to be' (27:57). Same story, a key word changed.

tree:0noyiza0x3p90y.why: 'Follow / recite what is revealed to you of ...': your Lord (6:106), your Lord's Book (18:27), the Book (29:45). A memorizer's trap.

tree:1l76jlr0mndomp.why: 'Those, their deeds are void': apostates (2:217), polytheists maintaining the mosques (9:17), those who indulged like earlier nations (9:69). Tails differ.
tree:1l76jlr0mndomp.relation: What makes deeds worthless: apostasy, polytheism, and following the ways of the doomed.

tree:0jdq9ra0ynt0ee.why: 'Those are in error ...': far (14:3) vs clear (39:22, 46:32). A one-word memorizer's trap, and all three describe people who turn from God's call.
tree:0jdq9ra0ynt0ee.relation: Loving this world, hard hearts, refusing the caller: all lead astray.

tree:0o6lfmt1w80n8d.why: 'Those will enter the Garden': not wronged a speck (4:124), not wronged at all (19:60), provided without account (40:40). 4:124 and 40:40 share 'male or female, being a believer'.

tree:06m2jyr1j25zhr.why: The believers' certainty in the Hereafter: 'and in the Hereafter they are certain' (2:4) vs 'and they, in the Hereafter, are certain' (27:3, 31:4, identical). Openings of three surahs.

tree:0fyaxmp1vu4zml.why: 'In fairness, a duty on ...': the mindful (2:180 bequest, 2:241 divorced women) and the doers of good (2:236). One word to keep apart within al-Baqara.

tree:0uc4xd800c6rec.why: Moses sent with Our signs and clear authority, three times (11:96, 23:45 with Aaron, 40:23), each followed by whom he was sent to and their response.

tree:1aalce81kgk0hc.why: 'I am free of what you associate': the Prophet (6:19), Abraham (6:78), Hud (11:54). Three prophets, three forms of 'I'.
tree:1aalce81kgk0hc.relation: Every messenger declares himself free of his people's idols.

tree:0lezwhi1u3wsr8.why: 'Give them tidings of a painful punishment' after killing prophets (3:21), hoarding gold (9:34), and denial (84:24). Same ironic 'tidings'.

tree:1updx2g1mt8qga.why: Only 'some of you over others' is shared: preference among people (4:32, 16:71) and household members moving among each other (24:58), a different sense. Nothing more specific links them.

tree:1v4pvks0cu4lei.why: Adam's descent: 'Go down, some of you enemies to others' (2:36, 7:24) and 'Go down, both of you' (20:123), each with a different tail. Key memorizer card.

tree:0chxjb914lmwl7.why: 'Drew upon themselves God's anger': 2:61 and 3:112 describe the Children of Israel in close words, with the order of humiliation and poverty changed; 8:16 says it of one who flees battle.

tree:06iy83m10lbums.why: 'Is He not able to ...?': create the like of them (36:81), give life to the dead (46:33, 75:40). Arguments for the Resurrection.
tree:06iy83m10lbums.relation: The One who created the heavens can raise the dead.

tree:1g1bt1i1wf1gl6.why: 'Rather, they are a people ...': who ascribe equals (27:60), contentious (43:58), transgressing (51:53). One word changes; all describe the deniers.

tree:0sy67iz1hqnt4b.why: 'Of what you do, He is Knowing' is a stock closing found in many places; these three (pledges, the messengers' food, entering houses) share nothing more.

check.why: Drop is right: a stock closing.

tree:1shvmpe16lvq6w.why: 'A drink of boiling water and a painful punishment for what they used to deny' (6:70, 10:4, identical), and 'the severe punishment' in 10:70. A memorizer's trap.

tree:157m8th07at1kd.why: Water giving life to a dead land, followed by three different tails: we give drink to cattle and people (25:49), thus you will be brought out (43:11), thus is the coming out (50:11).
tree:157m8th07at1kd.relation: Rain reviving the land as proof of the Resurrection.

check.why: Keep is right: water reviving a dead land, in three places with three different tails, a real memorizer set.

tree:0vdesl50gdnwe7.why: Selling the Book for a small price: writing it with their hands (2:79), hiding it (2:174), casting it behind their backs (3:187). Three forms of one sin.
tree:0vdesl50gdnwe7.relation: Corrupting, hiding and abandoning revelation for small gain.

tree:0rfw8pj1qqjvaj.why: 27:39 and 27:40 are neighbouring offers to bring the Queen's throne 'before you ...': before you rise (the jinn) / before your glance returns (the one with knowledge). 7:123 has a different governing verb (Pharaoh's 'you believed in him before I permit').
tree:0rfw8pj1qqjvaj.changes: Removed 7:123: a different governing verb (believed in him, not bring it).
tree:0rfw8pj1qqjvaj.relation: Two offers, two speeds: the strength of a jinn against the power of knowledge from the Book.

check.why: I would keep 7:123. 'It, before that' followed by a verb has the same structure there; only the story differs. The Clarifications say that is not a reason to remove a row. Its twin 20:71 belongs in a card of its own as well.

tree:0ma8y8o1gmdo9e.why: 'A slander and a clear sin' closes three ayat on wronging the innocent: taking back a wife's dowry (4:20), blaming an innocent for one's sin (4:112), hurting believers undeservedly (33:58).
tree:0ma8y8o1gmdo9e.relation: Injustice to the innocent is counted as slander.

tree:1buja7m1aptrpe.why: 'We make no distinction between any of them': 2:136 and 3:84 are near-identical (to us / upon us, and 'what was given'), and 4:152 praises those who do not distinguish.
tree:1buja7m1aptrpe.relation: Faith in all the prophets alike.

tree:0zhiisj18jc1mh.why: 'Clear proof has come to you from your Lord': Salih (7:73) and Shu'ayb (7:85) in identical openings, then their different commands; 6:157 says it of the Quran.
tree:0zhiisj18jc1mh.relation: Each prophet came with clear proof before the call to obey.

tree:1eoi7lu0ienq42.why: Ships that sail the sea: with what benefits people (2:164), by His command (22:65), by God's favour (31:31). The word after 'sea' is the trap.
tree:1eoi7lu0ienq42.relation: Ships as a sign of God's favour and command.

tree:0wqpbqj1ry49h1.why: Saying about God: 'what you do not know' in 2:169 (Satan's command) and 7:33 (what God forbade), and 'nothing but the truth' in 4:171.
tree:0wqpbqj1ry49h1.relation: Speaking about God without knowledge is among the gravest sins.

tree:1ghzmqk0b4hmlw.why: 'Then to Him you will be returned' closes three ayat on life, death and return: you were dead and He gave you life (2:28), He begins and repeats creation (30:11), His is all intercession (39:44).
tree:1ghzmqk0b4hmlw.relation: Every argument ends at the return to God.

tree:0uzxbq50lqdwkl.why: Selling for a small price, 'those ...': those who hide the Book eat fire (2:174), those who sell God's covenant have no share (3:77), and those of the People of the Book who do not sell have their reward (3:199).
tree:0uzxbq50lqdwkl.relation: Contrast: those who sell the covenant and those who refuse to.

tree:0q6746713n52ip.why: 'They made partners for God': the jinn (6:100), partners who created like Him (13:16), name them (13:33). Two in the same surah.
tree:0q6746713n52ip.relation: Every argument against the partners they invent.

tree:0t4zou40d7ow16.why: 'Strove with their wealth and their lives': the emigrants and helpers (8:72), the Messenger and those with him (9:88), the true believers (49:15).
tree:0t4zou40d7ow16.relation: Striving with wealth and self as the sign of true faith.

tree:1ngexpv1v6yfcb.why: 'Hell, and wretched is the resting place' closes three ayat: gathered to Hell (3:12), short enjoyment then Hell (3:197), those who refused their Lord (13:18).

tree:0xgxjd31bttnxb.why: 'Hell, and evil is the destination': those who did not emigrate (4:97), who oppose the Messenger (4:115), the hypocrites and polytheists (48:6). Same closing, two in an-Nisa.

tree:0mx0g350ku9z55.why: All three rows stay. 'Until, when ... came' is the same words and structure in all three: death comes to one of you (6:61), to one of them (23:99), Our command came (11:40). Only the subject differs, and that is where a reciter slips between them.
tree:0mx0g350ku9z55.relation: The moment that comes: death for each soul, the command for Noah's people.

tree:1hec4rx0pdu73r.why: 'Those against whom the word came true': 41:25 and 46:18 continue identically ('among nations of jinn and men before them'), and in 28:63 they disown their followers.
tree:1hec4rx0pdu73r.relation: The decree on those who misled and were misled.

check.why: Keep is right: 41:25 and 46:18 share a long identical clause, and 28:63 has the same opening on the same theme.

tree:1ypboy01oojabk.why: 'We created man from ...': clay of altered mud (15:26), an extract of clay (23:12), a mixed drop (76:2). Stages of man's creation.
tree:1ypboy01oojabk.relation: Man's humble origin, from earth and from a drop.

tree:089grrd0y0n7zh.why: 'Better than what they amass': God's forgiveness for those killed in His way (3:157), His bounty and mercy (10:58), your Lord's mercy (43:32).
tree:089grrd0y0n7zh.relation: God's mercy against everything people gather in this world.

tree:1826ru11y3mxhx.why: 'That is more likely to ...': that witnesses testify truly (5:108), that the Prophet's wives are content (33:51), that believing women are recognised (33:59). Same wording, two in one surah.

tree:1cqktvi10spfuq.why: 'That is the upright religion': of the sacred months (9:36), of worship of God alone (12:40), of the natural disposition (30:30). 12:40 and 30:30 continue identically.
tree:1cqktvi10spfuq.relation: Calendar, monotheism and human nature all called the upright religion.

tree:1b6nmwe0xy1st0.why: 'Taste the punishment of burning': 3:181 and 8:50 are followed by the same next ayah ('that is for what your hands put forth'); 22:22 has it in Hell itself.

tree:1qrazda0o75a0i.why: Three prophets' prayers opening 'My Lord, forgive me': Moses adds his brother (7:151), Solomon asks a kingdom (38:35), Noah his parents and the believers (71:28).
tree:1qrazda0o75a0i.relation: Each prophet starts with forgiveness before asking.

tree:083ax4103m9y6x.why: 'Lord of the Great Throne' closing a declaration of God's oneness: the Prophet's reliance (9:129), the question to the deniers (23:86), the hoopoe's words (27:26).
tree:083ax4103m9y6x.relation: The Lord of the Throne is the only one worth relying on and worshipping.

tree:0ww5w8u1m1uye4.why: 'My Lord, grant me': Zakariya asks for good offspring (3:38), Abraham for wisdom (26:83) and for a righteous son (37:100).

tree:13vcymi1rccvue.why: 'Our Lord, do not make us': with the wrongdoing people (7:47), a trial for the wrongdoing people (10:85), a trial for the disbelievers (60:5). Close wording, three speakers.

tree:01sbb881888ai2.why: 'And provided you with good things' after three reminders of blessings, then different tails: that you may give thanks (8:26), do they believe in falsehood? (16:72), that is God your Lord (40:64).

tree:1e3uf3k0h4c4m6.why: 'And We provided them with good things': the Children of Israel (10:93, 45:16) and the children of Adam (17:70), with different tails.
tree:1e3uf3k0h4c4m6.relation: Favour given, and how it was received.

tree:1dmugvq04rpxg8.why: Comfort to the Prophet: 'messengers before you were denied', with three tails: they came with clear proofs (3:184), they were patient until help came (6:34), to God all matters return (35:4).
tree:1dmugvq04rpxg8.relation: The Prophet is not the first to be denied; the earlier messengers' patience is his model.

tree:06f8s350kriyw1.why: 'Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, and ...': they would not believe (7:101) vs God would not wrong them, they wronged themselves (9:70, 30:9, identical tails).

tree:1xybp5w0g48peq.why: 'I am the messenger of God to you': Muhammad to all mankind (7:158), Moses to his people (61:5), Jesus to the Children of Israel (61:6), the last two neighbours.
tree:1xybp5w0g48peq.relation: Three messengers with one claim, and how each was received.

tree:0powjgu1lh9amo.why: 'We adorned the nearest heaven': with the adornment of the stars (37:6) vs with lamps (41:12, 67:5), each with a different purpose after it.

tree:1sadbxu0sd2dgc.why: 'When their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour nor advance it': 7:34 and 16:61 without 'so', 10:49 with it. A one-letter memorizer's trap.

tree:182qkia0aspwk8.why: Only 'the way of God, then' is shared: spenders (2:262), emigrants who died (22:58), and disbelievers who blocked the way (47:34). Different subjects and structures.

tree:046czgk1ip1hdc.why: 'You will come to know who ...': 'so you will' in 6:135 and 11:39, 'you will' without 'so' in 11:93 after the same 'work according to your position'. A known trap.
tree:046czgk1ip1hdc.relation: The messengers' confident warning to their people.

tree:16lsoaa1cqubkg.why: 'Sufficient is God as witness between me and you' with three tails: and whoever has knowledge of the Book (13:43), He is aware of His servants (17:96), He is the Forgiving (46:8).

tree:1gi79xs03f3m2o.why: Scripture as 'a detailing of everything and guidance and mercy': the Torah (6:154), the Quran's stories (12:111), the Book sent to the Prophet (16:89, 'clarification').
tree:1gi79xs03f3m2o.relation: The same description for the Torah and the Quran.

tree:0rp1bna0r98p5a.why: The idols 'create nothing and are themselves created' (7:191, 16:20, 25:3), each with a different lead-in and next words.
tree:0rp1bna0r98p5a.relation: The basic argument against idols: a created thing cannot be a god.

tree:15fjhza13ikwxy.why: 'The darknesses of land and sea': who saves you from them (6:63), stars to guide you in them (6:97), who guides you in them (27:63).
tree:15fjhza13ikwxy.relation: God's guidance and rescue in the dark, as proof of His oneness.

tree:120h1i60v8ajye.why: 'Perhaps your Lord will ...': destroy your enemy (7:129, Moses), have mercy on you (17:8), remove your misdeeds (66:8).
tree:120h1i60v8ajye.relation: Hope held out by God in three situations.

tree:05jhsux0pyr6xh.why: Moses' staff: 'and behold, it was a clear serpent' (7:107, 26:32, identical with the same next ayat) vs 'it swallowed what they faked' (26:45).

tree:03dgsc81be1eys.why: Only 'on those who believe' is shared, in three unrelated sentences (a plot to unsettle believers, no blame for food, Satan has no power).

tree:0urh0ga0cwb998.why: 6:125 and 10:100 both close 'God places defilement on those who do not ...' (believe / reason). In 9:91 the words follow 'there is no blame', a different governing phrase.
tree:0urh0ga0cwb998.changes: Removed 9:91: the phrase is governed by 'no blame on', not 'places defilement on'.
tree:0urh0ga0cwb998.relation: Defilement falls on those who do not believe and do not reason.

tree:1hgkrrc1o1zcng.why: Only 'on the Children of Israel' is shared, after three different verbs (prescribed, fulfilled, narrates). Different subjects, nothing to confuse.

tree:1116xj11bowxe9.why: 'Does not urge the feeding of the poor' (69:34, 107:3) vs 'you do not urge one another' (89:18). A short ayah with a pronoun trap.
tree:1116xj11bowxe9.relation: Neglect of the poor as a mark of the one who denies the Judgment.

tree:08nv3z517k9bp3.why: 'On Him I rely, and to Him I turn': Shu'ayb (11:88) and the Prophet (42:10) with 'I turn', and 13:30 with 'my return'. A one-word trap.

tree:1dlgnm40dlpabg.why: 2:134 and 2:141 say 'you will not be asked about what they used to do', while 15:92-93 swear 'We will ask them all about what they used to do'. Same words, opposite statement. 15:93 alone is only the phrase, so the oath before it is added.
tree:1dlgnm40dlpabg.changes: Added 15:92 before 15:93 so the oath that gives the phrase its meaning is shown. The rows that already read on (2:135, 2:142, 15:94) are kept as they are.
tree:1dlgnm40dlpabg.relation: Contrast: no one is asked about another nation's deeds, yet every one will be asked about their own.

tree:1743k0q0jxmi2a.why: Barring from the Sacred Mosque: do not let hatred for those who barred you lead to aggression (5:2), the polytheists deserve punishment for barring (8:34), the disbelievers barred you at Hudaybiya (48:25).
tree:1743k0q0jxmi2a.relation: The same wrong, and how believers must respond to it justly.

tree:12uqox11oaowf5.why: Distraction from the remembrance of God: wine and gambling (5:91), trade that does not distract the true men (24:37), wealth and children (63:9).
tree:12uqox11oaowf5.relation: What distracts from God's remembrance, and those who are not distracted.

tree:09m0ig101dfpq3.why: All three rows stay. 'With God, it is ...' then a comparative in all three: better (16:95), better and greater in reward (73:20), more guiding (28:49). 28:49 has the same words and structure with another comparative, a likely slip.
tree:09m0ig101dfpq3.relation: What is with God is better than any price, and His Book is the best guide.

tree:02hh2vr1vhvtzh.why: Only 'with God, and God' is shared, joining three unrelated sentences (ranks, reward, those not equal). No relation and no slip.

tree:1djy1h21nigge6.why: 'With their Lord are gardens': beneath which rivers flow (3:15), of bliss (68:34), of Eden (98:8). The mindful's reward in three descriptions.

tree:1exbgld0xvbdst.why: 'And the life of this world deluded them': those who took their religion as play (6:70, 7:51, with 'play and amusement' in reverse order) and the jinn and men confessing (6:130).
tree:1exbgld0xvbdst.relation: This world's delusion behind mocking the religion.

tree:18qadgb091k7fn.why: 'A people with whom God is angry': hypocrites who take them as allies (58:14), believers told not to (60:13), and God's anger on the hypocrites and polytheists (48:6).
tree:18qadgb091k7fn.relation: Allying with those under God's anger shares in their fate.

tree:0q7g11c0xrp230.why: 'Seeking bounty from God and pleasure': the companions of the Prophet (48:29) and the emigrants (59:8), and 'bounty from God and favour' in 49:8. A one-word trap.

tree:12wo6vo1ghqdie.why: 9:38 and 13:26: the enjoyment of this world, compared to the Hereafter, is only a little / a passing enjoyment. In 11:16 'in the Hereafter' has another sense (they have nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire), not the comparison.
tree:12wo6vo1ghqdie.changes: Removed 11:16: 'in the Hereafter' means place there, not 'compared to'; a different sense.
tree:12wo6vo1ghqdie.relation: This world weighed against the Hereafter is little.

check.why: 11:16 is a different structure: 'they have nothing in the Hereafter except', not 'the life of this world in the Hereafter is only'. Removing it is right.

tree:14yjxio11ytx1u.why: 'In the Hereafter they are the greatest losers' (11:22, 27:5) vs 'the losers' (16:109). One word, three places.

tree:1hpzdhp18feq9r.why: Only 'in the earth, or' is shared, a fragment that joins two halves of three unrelated questions.

tree:0mx8nrx111f2yn.why: 'Good in this world' and the Hereafter: the believers' prayer (2:201), God's promise to the emigrants (16:41), and what was given to Abraham (16:122).
tree:0mx8nrx111f2yn.relation: The good of both worlds asked for, promised, and given.

tree:1beb1fr0wmp7hb.why: 'For them in this world is disgrace, and in the Hereafter a great punishment' (2:114, 5:41, identical tails) vs 22:9 in the singular with a different tail.

tree:1wiq6ve0qhuh3i.why: God's knowledge of what is in the sky and earth (singular 'sky'): He knows all speech (21:4), it is in a Book (22:70), nothing hidden but in a clear Book (27:75).

tree:1xgartn012atyp.why: Pharaoh's chiefs advise sending gatherers to the cities: 'send' with two different verbs in 7:111 and 26:36, followed by 'every learned sorcerer' in two forms; 26:53 has Pharaoh sending them after Moses.
tree:1xgartn012atyp.relation: The same summons twice: against Moses' signs and against his escape.

tree:1dgh1d61vp0bxo.why: 'We will remove whatever rancour is in their hearts': the people of the Garden in 7:43 and 15:47, with different continuations. In 59:13 'from' is the comparative after 'greater fear', a different word.
tree:1dgh1d61vp0bxo.changes: Removed 59:13: its 'from' is comparative (more feared than God), a different structure.
tree:1dgh1d61vp0bxo.relation: Paradise is first a heart cleansed of rancour.

check.why: 59:13 'greater fear in their hearts than God' is a different structure from 'We removed whatever rancour was in their hearts'. Removing it is right.

tree:1rydi6y1lu3476.why: 'We sent no prophet / warner to a town but ...': hardship took its people (7:94), its affluent said we disbelieve (34:34), we follow our fathers (43:23).

tree:1hoqpcd1fw4l1r.why: 'In the hearts of those who ...': terror cast into the disbelievers' hearts (3:151, 8:12), compassion and mercy placed in the hearts of Jesus' followers (57:27).
tree:1hoqpcd1fw4l1r.relation: Contrast: God puts terror in one set of hearts and mercy in another.

tree:00wlle91hog2n5.why: 'In the fire of Hell': hoarded gold heated (9:35), the building on a crumbling edge (9:109), the disbelievers forever (98:6). Different images of the same end.

tree:11d433x04gnsvn.why: 'One of them said': Joseph's brother (12:10), one of the cave sleepers (18:19), a dweller of the Garden recalling his companion (37:51). Same opening, three stories.

tree:1ij5fi21lvaoxm.why: 'Moses said to them': throw what you will throw (10:80, 26:43, identical) vs woe to you, do not invent lies (20:61).

tree:0kw12w919vhopx.why: Abraham's argument with the star, moon and sun: 'this is my Lord' three times in a row, each followed by a different conclusion when it sets.
tree:0kw12w919vhopx.relation: Step by step from the setting bodies to the One who does not set.

tree:1qo0web03upzkv.why: 'They say we believe, and when they are alone ...' with their devils (2:14), with each other (2:76), they bite their fingers in rage (3:119). Hypocrites' two faces.

tree:1ehct2c1dg63di.why: 'You are only ...': a fabricator (16:101) and 'one of the bewitched' said to Salih (26:153) and Shu'ayb (26:185) with different next ayat.

tree:0i0fxwm1hxi27y.why: Abraham's guests say 'Peace': he answers 'peace' (11:69, 51:25) or 'we are afraid of you' (15:52). Same scene, three tellings.

tree:1qtxi3x18vk7lz.why: 'If you do not desist, you will surely be among ...': Noah's people threaten stoning (26:116), Lot's people expulsion (26:167); 7:149 is the calf-worshippers' repentance in the same 'if not, we will be' pattern.

tree:1fqq0od1ejnydn.why: 'This is clear magic' against Moses (27:13) and Jesus (61:6), and 'this is magic, and we disbelieve in it' against the Quran (43:30).

tree:0xkt89a1vkyfk6.why: 'How many generations We destroyed before them': 20:128 and 32:26 continue 'walking in their dwellings' with different endings (and 'from before' in 32:26); 36:31 says they do not return.

tree:1yev3gn1rvcfyh.why: 'He has failed who ...': invents lies (20:61), carries injustice (20:111), corrupts his soul (91:10).

tree:1fdeo6w1gzll9i.why: 'Lost are those who ...': deny the meeting with God (6:31, 10:45) and kill their children (6:140); 6:140 and 10:45 end with 'and they were not guided'.

tree:1r3lw02123ymd6.why: 'He has strayed far' (4:116, 4:136) vs 'strayed clearly' (33:36), after association, disbelief, and disobeying God and His Messenger.

tree:12mesea1ah5vta.why: All three rows stay. 6:37 and 13:27 answer the same demand for a sign with 'say: God ...' and two answers (He is able / He leaves astray whom He wills). 7:28 has the same command and structure answering another claim (God does not command indecency). Same words, different subject, so it stays.
tree:12mesea1ah5vta.relation: Two replies to the same demand for a sign: God is able, and guidance is His.

tree:12ykh4u00w8fd2.why: All three rows stay. 'Say: perhaps ...' in the same words and structure: perhaps it is near (17:51), perhaps some of it is close behind you (27:72), perhaps my Lord will guide me (18:24). The first two answer the deniers' 'when?'; 18:24 is the same opening a reciter could carry on wrongly.
tree:12ykh4u00w8fd2.relation: Hope and warning in one phrase: the Hour may be near, and guidance may be nearer.

tree:1dou3zv18hh0sd.why: 'Say: bring your proof': 'if you are truthful' in 2:111 and 27:64, and 'this is the Reminder' in 21:24. Against false claims and false gods.
tree:1dou3zv18hh0sd.relation: Every false claim is met with the demand for proof.

tree:04v4lfr17daaux.why: 'Say: are they equal ...?': the blind and the seeing (6:50, 13:16) and those who know and those who do not (39:9).
tree:04v4lfr17daaux.relation: Knowledge and sight vs ignorance and blindness.

tree:0d93rhu0ih8gsa.why: 'Little do you remember' closes three ayat with different lead-ins: following other protectors (7:3), the One who answers the distressed (27:62), not the word of a soothsayer (69:42).

tree:0ehbjp40be68v2.why: Joseph's shirt: torn from the front (12:26), from the back (12:27), seen torn from the back (12:28). Three neighbouring ayat that turn on one word.

tree:0vqn941067pem3.why: 'Protect us from the punishment of the Fire': 'and protect' in 2:201 and 3:16, 'so protect' in 3:191. Three believers' prayers.

tree:05csozn0ka8eq1.why: 'A people who do not believe' is a stock phrase; here it ends three unrelated statements (signs do not help them, Joseph left their creed, the Prophet's complaint). Little to confuse or ponder.

check.why: Drop is right: a stock phrase ending unrelated statements.

tree:0zt3mq91fvs2q7.why: 'And the command of God is ever done' (4:47, 33:37) vs 'a decree determined' (33:38), the last two neighbours.

tree:09l2fp80j3gm7w.why: 'Even if he is a near relative': no false witness (5:106), be just in speech (6:152), no one carries another's burden (35:18).
tree:09l2fp80j3gm7w.relation: Kinship does not bend justice, testimony or accountability.

tree:1v3qfs00i7g4v6.why: 'They had no ...': protectors besides God (11:20, 42:46) and no defender from God (40:21). Close wording about the helplessness of the deniers.

tree:1via7v40wvgmzy.why: The real pair, 41:52 and 46:10 ('if it is from God and you disbelieve in it', with 'then' vs 'and'), is the one the books compare and should stand as its own card; 4:82 ('from other than God') is a different phrase.

check.why: Drop is right: I checked that the 41:52 with 46:10 pair is in a book card and in kept cards, and 4:82 is a different phrase.

tree:0al9u3b17lealn.why: Lot's wife 'was of those who stayed behind', said of her (7:83, 29:32) and to Lot (29:33, 'your wife'). The pronoun is the trap.

tree:032bfbj1vgxbqb.why: 'They used to reject Our signs' after 'what' (7:51), 'and' (41:15), 'for what' (41:28). Two in Fussilat.

tree:1ukyehg1h6zwe4.why: 'No sign comes to them but they turn away from it' (6:4, 36:46, identical) vs 'We gave them Our signs and they turned away' (15:81).

tree:08mrlz60ys8yc0.why: 'And many of them are defiantly disobedient' closes three ayat of al-Hadid about the people of earlier scripture (57:16, 57:26, 57:27).
tree:08mrlz60ys8yc0.relation: Hearts hardened over time, a warning to the believers.

tree:0uwjfeb0iab5sz.why: 'Those who denied the signs of God' is a common phrase; the three ayat (a warning to the Prophet, the end of evildoers, the donkey parable) share nothing more.

check.why: Drop is right: a common phrase with nothing more shared.

tree:1kdz3yw0yybqrw.why: 'Thus says your Lord: it is easy for Me' to Zakariya (19:9) and Mary (19:21), and 'thus says your Lord: He is the Wise' to Abraham's wife (51:30).
tree:1kdz3yw0yybqrw.relation: Three miraculous births announced in the same words.

tree:1kyo1f71s2h479.why: 'Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers': 'and thus' in 7:41, 'thus' in 12:75 and 21:29.

check.why: Keep is right: 'thus do We recompense the wrongdoers' with and without wa is a real memorizer refrain in three places.

tree:1jpmlye1jktgm0.why: 'Thus God leaves astray ...': the transgressor and doubter (40:34), the disbelievers (40:74), whom He wills (74:31).

tree:0yqmyxp0z2b67h.why: 'My / our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge': Abraham (6:80) and Shu'ayb (7:89), both after 'except what my Lord wills'; and Moses on God (20:98).
tree:0yqmyxp0z2b67h.relation: Prophets entrusting their future to God's all-encompassing knowledge.

tree:0q8o4001izd668.why: 'Which you used to deny': the Fire (34:42, 52:14) and the verses (23:105, 'so you used to deny them').

tree:1ltetrp04pkuch.why: 16:43 and 21:7 are near-identical (with and without 'from' before 'before you'): ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know, a classic memorizer pair. 30:56 ends with the same three words but after 'but' instead of 'if' (a rebuke on the Day). That is arguably a different structure, but its row reads on into 30:57, and rows that read on are not removed while that rule is open.
tree:1ltetrp04pkuch.relation: Ask those who know when you do not know; on the Day, not knowing is no excuse.

tree:00nmaky0qypm7c.why: 'Then there is no sin on him': the one forced by need (2:173), the one who mends a bequest (2:182), the pilgrim who hastens or delays (2:203).

tree:13en6hm10jgl6a.why: 'Do not follow their desires' in judging by what God sent down (5:48, 5:49) and in calling to the religion (42:15).
tree:13en6hm10jgl6a.relation: Revelation, not the desires of others, is the basis of judgment.

tree:1ptxkgx0w4dc8v.why: 'Do not grieve over them': followed by 'lower your wing to the believers' (15:88) and 'do not be distressed by their plotting' (16:127, 27:70, near-identical: 'tak' vs 'takun').
tree:1ptxkgx0w4dc8v.relation: Comfort to the Prophet over the deniers.

tree:1s7dyac1pxe1bo.why: 'You will not be asked about what ...': they did (2:134, 2:141, identical) and 'what we committed' (34:25). Each answers for his own deeds.
tree:1s7dyac1pxe1bo.relation: Personal responsibility, between generations and between believers and deniers.

tree:0wpp29611oym3w.why: 'Do not obey the disbelievers': 'so do not' then strive against them (25:52), 'and do not' with 'and the hypocrites' twice in al-Ahzab (33:1, 33:48).

tree:1fwlvgs0viw1mw.why: All three rows stay. 'So do not be in ...' is the same prohibition in the same structure: in doubt about it (11:17), in doubt about what these worship (11:109), in distress over what they plot (16:127). Only the noun after it changes, which is exactly the memorizer's trap.
tree:1fwlvgs0viw1mw.relation: The Prophet is told not to doubt the truth and not to be distressed by the plotting against it.

tree:12awfjq0ws5yec.why: 'Do not be among ...': the doubters (3:60), the heedless (7:205), the despairing (15:55). One word at the end changes.

tree:076pswf0f53q6r.why: All three rows stay. 'There is no turning it back' has the same words and the same sense in all three: a Day that cannot be turned back from God (30:43, 42:47), and God's will for harm on a people that cannot be turned back (13:11). Different subject, same phrase.
tree:076pswf0f53q6r.relation: What God decrees cannot be repelled: neither His punishment on a people nor His Day.

tree:1sn35ff0g7f0xp.why: 'We do not let the reward of ... be lost': the reformers (7:170), the doers of good (12:56), whoever does good work (18:30).

tree:1g35kat183l0cx.why: 'Nor will they be allowed to make amends' closes three scenes of the Day (16:84, 30:57, 45:35), each with a different lead-in.
tree:1g35kat183l0cx.relation: On the Day no excuse is accepted.

tree:1olrbgk1wpbztq.why: 'And God does not love the wrongdoers' (3:57, 3:140) vs 'indeed He does not love the wrongdoers' (42:40).

tree:0zzm0sb0ril5kp.why: 'Do not transgress; God does not love the transgressors' in fighting (2:190) and in forbidding good things (5:87), and 'indeed He does not love' after supplication (7:55).

tree:09cyjm71lnwyqz.why: 'God does not guide whom ...': whom He leaves astray (16:37), who is a liar and disbeliever (39:3), who is a transgressor and liar (40:28).

tree:1324xdh0msfdap.why: 'If you do not desist': Abraham's father threatens stoning (19:46), Noah's people stoning (26:116), Lot's people expulsion (26:167).
tree:1324xdh0msfdap.relation: Every prophet threatened by those closest to him.

tree:039zthv0e57ht3.why: 'Evil indeed is what they used to ...' closing three ayat of al-Ma'ida with three verbs: do, work, do (5:62, 5:63, 5:79). A classic trap.

tree:1klijys03tpw0y.why: 'That you may warn a people to whom no warner came before you': 28:46 and 32:3 identical except the last word; 36:6 'whose fathers were not warned'.

tree:0wl4svz0x9yd2p.why: 'God's curse is on ...': the disbelievers (2:89) and the wrongdoers (7:44, 11:18), the last two followed by near-identical ayat.

tree:1awu8n016dmm9o.why: 'Followed by a curse in this world and on the Day of Resurrection': 'Ad (11:60), Pharaoh (11:99, without 'world'), Pharaoh's people (28:42).
