tree:18ewtsa0xaq58m.why: The deniers' wonder: 'shall we really be in a new creation?' (13:5, 32:10, 34:7), each followed by a different answer.

tree:0wya6db1nj94fb.why: All three rows stay. 'We have sent to ...' is the same words and structure in all three: to nations before you (6:42, 16:63), to Thamud their brother Salih (27:45). 6:42 and 16:63 are the close pair (nations before you, then hardship / Satan made their deeds fair); 27:45 is where a reciter may branch.
tree:0wya6db1nj94fb.relation: Messengers sent to nations before, and how those nations answered.

tree:1da3p501i51a3a.why: 'You have done a grievous / terrible / unheard-of thing': Moses to al-Khidr twice (18:71, 18:74) and Mary's people (19:27). Three adjectives to keep apart.

tree:1femkzk0tf07vu.why: 'You know well that ...': Lot's people (11:79), Moses to Pharaoh (17:102), Abraham's people about the idols (21:65).

tree:0xpccge1vc64za.why: Night and day for you: subjected (14:33, 16:12) and made (28:73). Signs of mercy with different tails.

tree:05ojp2k0vn3w4m.why: Jesus came to make lawful 'some of what was forbidden to you' (3:50) and to make clear 'some of what you differ about' (43:63), both ending 'so fear God and obey me'. In 27:72 'for you some of what' follows another verb ('may be close behind you'), a different structure.
tree:05ojp2k0vn3w4m.changes: Removed 27:72: the words follow a different governing verb and start a different sentence.
tree:05ojp2k0vn3w4m.relation: Jesus' mission told twice: easing the law and clearing up disputes, with the same call to fear God and obey.

check.why:
27:72 has the same words and structure, 'to you some of what', and was removed only for its subject (the punishment they hasten). I would keep it as a third row; the two Jesus rows still stand out by their shared ending.
لكم بعض الذي

tree:19nwito0cwunf6.why: 2:36 and 7:24 share 'and for you on earth a dwelling and provision for a time' word for word in Adam's story. In 16:13 'for you on earth' is governed by 'what He spread', a different structure.
tree:19nwito0cwunf6.changes: Removed 16:13: a different structure. The rows that read on (2:37, 7:25) are kept as they are.
tree:19nwito0cwunf6.relation: The fall from the Garden told twice: life on earth is a dwelling and provision for a time.

tree:17hclig0wv75z8.why: 'For you in them are benefits': the sacrificial animals till their term (22:33), cattle with milk and food (23:21), cattle to ride (40:80).

tree:0qcvpxx1sw6scr.why: 'He will forgive you of your sins and defer you to a set term' (14:10 the messengers, 71:4 Noah) vs 'and protect you from a painful punishment' (46:31 the jinn).

tree:1e6z7cy0595npq.why: 'I am to you from Him a warner': and a bringer of good news (11:2) vs clear (51:50 and 51:51, two neighbouring ayat with the same ending).

check.why: Keep is right: 'a warner from Him' with two endings. 51:51 shows twice through the run-on, which should be cleaned.

tree:15yu8l80vbpeui.why: 'I am to you a clear warner': Noah in 11:25 and 71:2 ('indeed I'), and the Prophet in 22:49 ('I am only'). Each followed by the call to worship God.

tree:1m91brs1ysy8ho.why: 'For those who do not believe' is a common phrase; the three ayat (devils as allies, work as you will, the evil description) share nothing more.

tree:16ceidb0m2ymxz.why: 'A humiliating punishment for the disbelievers' three times in an-Nisa: 'and We prepared' (4:37, 4:151) vs 'God has prepared' (4:102).

tree:1yr1two1gbhtp2.why: On the Day, life seems to have lasted only an hour of the day (10:45, 46:35, with and without 'the') or an evening or its morning (79:46).
tree:1yr1two1gbhtp2.relation: How short this life will seem when the Day comes.

tree:1vacg1j0t9mvst.why: 'When they saw the punishment': they hid their regret (10:54, 34:33, same clause, different tails), and the wrongdoers ask for a way back (42:44).
tree:1vacg1j0t9mvst.relation: Regret that comes only when the punishment is seen.

check.why: Keep is right: 'they hid their regret when they saw the punishment' is a rare repeated clause, with 42:44 on the same scene.

tree:1n2fy9s0kbxjk4.why: 'If You save us / give us ..., we will surely be among the grateful': at sea (6:63, 10:22) and the couple praying for a child (7:189); each time they break the promise in the next ayah.
tree:1n2fy9s0kbxjk4.relation: Promises made in distress and broken in ease.

tree:1xr75op0ys22rz.why: 'To Him belong the best names': call Him by any (17:110), no god but He (20:8), the Creator, Maker, Fashioner (59:24).

tree:1ml0e2y0jvjb70.why: 'His is the praise in ...': the first and the last (28:70), the heavens and earth (30:18), the Hereafter (34:1).

tree:13cizu50rncd4n.why: The real pair, 30:43 and 42:47 ('a Day that cannot be turned back from God'), is already a card. 5:41 ('you have no power for him against God') is a different phrase, so this card adds only an outsider.

tree:014wf5v0pnepyp.why: Only 'for him, before' is shared, in three unrelated settings (a brother who stole, John's unique name, submit before the punishment).

tree:094pfo8034wshc.why: 'It will have what it earned': a nation that passed (2:134, 2:141, identical) and every soul (2:286, 'and against it what it incurred').
tree:094pfo8034wshc.relation: Each answers for what it earned.

tree:1vvr0111y3az7f.why: Only 'for them; indeed God' is shared, joining three unrelated sentences (treaties, lowering the gaze, the hypocrites).

tree:0amhimb0x06l6h.why: 'They will have whatever they wish with their Lord' (39:34, 42:22) and 'whatever they wish therein' (50:35). The reward of the Garden, with different tails.

tree:07i0y2j1ickb0z.why: 'They have besides Him no ...': protector or intercessor (6:51), defender (13:11), protector (18:26). The noun is the trap.

tree:0c3rdhe040e60c.why: 'Had your Lord willed': they would not have done it (6:112), all on earth would believe (10:99), He would make people one nation (11:118).
tree:0c3rdhe040e60c.relation: God's will behind people's choices and differences.

tree:0ag40d906c7fpj.why: 'Even though the disbelievers dislike it': God perfects His light (9:32, 61:8, near-identical) and worship Him sincerely (40:14).

tree:082p0mp0df271d.why: Only 'if God willed' is shared, in three unrelated settings (guiding all people, feeding the poor, defeating the enemy). The phrase is too general to hold them together.

tree:0ugdhos0og8xee.why: 'Grant me from Yourself': Zakariya asks for good offspring (3:38) and an heir (19:5), and the Prophet for a supporting authority (17:80).
tree:0ugdhos0og8xee.relation: Asking for what only God can give.

tree:1p1wtzj1wh4mx5.why: 'What God has given them of His bounty': hiding it out of stinginess (4:37), envying others for it (4:54), being content with it (9:59).
tree:1p1wtzj1wh4mx5.relation: Three attitudes to God's gifts: hoarding, envy, contentment.

tree:1f18tl61rnts60.why: 'I do not want to ...': Shu'ayb does not want to oppose his own teaching (11:88), the old man of Madyan does not want to burden Moses (28:27), and God wants no provision from people (51:57).
tree:1f18tl61rnts60.relation: Sincerity without self-interest, from prophet, host and Lord.

tree:1dhzyj51d52mld.why: 'I am not a guardian over you' (6:104, 11:86) vs 'not a keeper over you' (10:108). The prophet's role is to convey, not to force.

tree:1u4o88n18f9127.why: Only 'what you are upon' is shared, and the words carry different senses (your present state, what you are doing, you cannot tempt anyone). Different structures, nothing to confuse.

tree:10iiglf0vijysf.why: 'Whatever you spend of ...': good (2:215), expenditure (2:270), anything (34:39), each with a different promise after it.
tree:10iiglf0vijysf.relation: Nothing spent is lost: God knows it and replaces it.

tree:0003rev1u6h7qt.why: 'What was given to Moses': in the believers' creed (2:136, 3:84) and in the deniers' demand for the like of it, though they disbelieved in it before (28:48).
tree:0003rev1u6h7qt.relation: Contrast: believers affirm all revelation; deniers ask for Moses' signs and reject them.

tree:0ycamxa1vm5ham.why: 'He knows what you reveal and what you conceal': 'what you used to conceal' in 2:33, 'what you conceal' in 5:99 and 24:29. A one-word trap.

tree:1t5rkix025jy0n.why: Only 'what you worship' is shared, in three senses: Jacob's question about after him (2:133), the idols are mere names (12:40), the idols as fuel of Hell (21:98). Different structures and subjects.

tree:1qcj3lj1p1wbe9.why: 'After the clear proofs had come to them': they differed out of envy (2:213), they fought each other (2:253), they took the calf (4:153).
tree:1qcj3lj1p1wbe9.relation: Division and disbelief came not from ignorance but after clear proof.

tree:0w7ey8l1ajic57.why: 5:84 (Christians moved to tears) and 20:72 (Pharaoh's magicians) are new believers holding to 'what has come to us of the truth / of clear proofs'. In 5:19 'what' is a negation ('no bringer of good news came to us'), a different word.
tree:0w7ey8l1ajic57.changes: Removed 5:19: its 'what' is a negation, not 'what has come to us'.
tree:0w7ey8l1ajic57.relation: Two groups of new believers stand by what came to them, whatever it costs.

check.why: Removing 5:19 is right, though for a better reason than the agent gave: there the particle is a negation (no bringer of news came to us), while in 5:84 and 20:72 it is a relative ('what came to us'). That is a structural difference.

tree:0zpcgjf0qbhc4f.why: Only 'God has not made' is shared, in three unrelated rulings (no way against neutral people, no invented taboo animals, no two hearts).

tree:103fhl204wtgf4.why: 'We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves' (11:101), 'they used to wrong themselves' (16:118), 'they were the wrongdoers' (43:76). Close wording, three endings.

tree:1skt80g0fwmz9k.why: All three rows stay. 'What is apparent of it' is the same relative and the same words in all three. 6:151 and 7:33 forbid indecencies, apparent and hidden; 24:31 lets women show of their adornment only what is apparent of it. Different subject, same words, and a reciter could add 'and what is hidden' there.
tree:1skt80g0fwmz9k.relation: What is apparent: indecency is forbidden whether open or hidden, adornment is allowed only as far as it shows by itself.

tree:02xgzoc0wfv5yw.why: 'What has already passed' is pardoned: past marriages to a father's wife and to two sisters (4:22, 4:23), and the disbelievers' past if they desist (8:38).
tree:02xgzoc0wfv5yw.relation: God does not hold people to account for what was before the law came.

tree:0e2i1ts0ijao6i.why: All three rows stay. 'Your Lord would never ...' is the same words and structure: never destroy towns unjustly (11:117), never destroy towns until He sends a messenger (28:59), never forgetful (19:64). The first two are the close pair; 19:64 is the same frame with another predicate.
tree:0e2i1ts0ijao6i.relation: God's justice and attention: no town is destroyed unjustly or unwarned, and nothing is forgotten.

tree:0ig9igq197oosm.why: Only 'it was not for you' is shared, in three unrelated settings (the people of the Fire, growing trees, the Prophet's wives).

tree:0nl5vmb0rej3ob.why: 'It was not for us': Joseph refuses to associate (12:38), messengers cannot bring authority except by God's leave (14:11), and the misleaders disown any authority over their followers (37:30).
tree:0nl5vmb0rej3ob.relation: No one, prophet or misleader, holds power of his own.

tree:1s4iret1t2mie5.why: 'And they were not guided' closes three ayat about loss: selling guidance for error (2:16), killing children (6:140), denying the meeting with God (10:45).

tree:0qawqw00k93jeo.why: Only 'it has no ...' is shared, about a rootless tree (14:26), a blast without pause (38:15) and a sky without rifts (50:6). Unrelated images.

tree:1imij2n0rmf063.why: 'What I have no ...': right to say (5:116, Jesus) vs knowledge of (11:47 Noah, 40:42 the believer of Pharaoh's people).
tree:1imij2n0rmf063.relation: Prophets and believers refusing to speak without right or knowledge.

tree:0f7tjkd1uosvth.why: 'There is no creature on earth but ...': they are nations like you (6:38), God provides for it (11:6), He holds its forelock (11:56).
tree:0f7tjkd1uosvth.relation: Every creature known, provided for and held by God.

tree:1i57t4v117ei27.why: 'And we will not be punished': 'Ad's boast (26:138), the rich deniers' boast (34:35), and the people of the Garden in wonder (37:59).
tree:1i57t4v117ei27.relation: Contrast: the deniers' false security and the believers' true security.

tree:0wtt6d31apopxv.why: The 'what' differs: a negation in 7:71 and 67:9 ('God sent down nothing'), a relative in 47:26 ('what God sent down'). Two different structures, and 7:71 / 67:9 alone are not close.

tree:0alayg21cxzh8a.why: 'What is recited to you': about women and orphans (4:127), and cattle made lawful 'except what is recited to you' (5:1, 22:30).

tree:1f0fg271ve1prx.why: 'Follow what is revealed to you' (10:109, 33:2), and 'perhaps you would leave some of what is revealed to you' (11:12).
tree:1f0fg271ve1prx.relation: Holding to the revelation despite pressure.

tree:17dkzdd1gbo4up.why: 'And died while disbelievers': the curse (2:161), no ransom accepted (3:91), no forgiveness (47:34). Close openings, different consequences.

tree:02izjlf18egn6n.why: 'And enjoyment for a time': Adam's descent (2:36, 7:24, identical) and the delay of punishment (21:111).

tree:0cf6dkw0g4u28m.why: 'The like of what was given to ...': the messengers (6:124), Moses (28:48), Qarun (28:79).
tree:0cf6dkw0g4u28m.relation: Envy of what others were given, of prophethood and of wealth.

tree:0ysilrb0is6w2b.why: 'With the wrongdoing people': do not sit with them (6:68), do not place us with them (7:47), do not place me with them (7:150).

tree:16tc47h1y5jnmh.why: Noah saved with those with him in the ark: 'and those with him' (7:64) vs 'and whoever was with him' (10:73, 26:119), with different tails.

tree:05k1q7v1nk98o3.why: 'That is among the signs of God' after clothing (7:26) and the sun turning from the cave (18:17): small things in creation read as signs. In 33:34 the words mean the verses recited in the Prophet's houses, a different sense of the word.
tree:05k1q7v1nk98o3.changes: Removed 33:34: 'signs' there means recited verses, not signs in creation.
tree:05k1q7v1nk98o3.relation: Garments and shade in the cave: everyday mercies counted as signs.

check.why: In 33:34, 'God's ayat' means the recited verses, not a sign in creation. A different word sense, so removing it is right.

tree:0bmjkct0zthd4n.why: Lot's rebuke 'no one in the worlds preceded you in it' in 7:80 and 29:28, which differ in the opening (a question / an assertion). In 35:41 the words go on 'after Him', a different structure.
tree:0bmjkct0zthd4n.changes: Removed 35:41: a different structure. The rows that read on (7:81, 29:29) are kept as they are.
tree:0bmjkct0zthd4n.relation: Lot's charge told twice, once as a question and once as a statement.

tree:0n26sjs1sldjn4.why: 'Who is more astray than one who ...': follows his desire (28:50), is in far dissension (41:52), calls on what will not answer (46:5).
tree:0n26sjs1sldjn4.relation: Three faces of the worst error: desire, opposition, false worship.

tree:0p3tyn802t2jdy.why: Houses cut from the mountains: Thamud 'used to carve' (15:82) and 'you carve' (26:149), and the bee told to take homes in the mountains (16:68).
tree:0p3tyn802t2jdy.relation: Contrast: the bee builds as inspired and gives healing; Thamud built proudly and perished.

tree:1at9t8414ztgkq.why: 'I will fill Hell with jinn and men all together' (11:119, 32:13, identical), and the last ayah of the Quran naming the whisperers 'of the jinn and men' (114:6).

check.why: Keep is right: 11:119 and 32:13 are identical, and 114:6 has the same words and structure, so under the Clarifications it stays.

tree:0hwume80uyn0nu.why: Two charges in an-Nisa opening 'of those who are Jews': distorting words (4:46) and the wrong for which good things were forbidden (4:160).
tree:0hwume80uyn0nu.relation: The wrongs of some of the Jews and their consequence.

tree:0xoxszh0ud9mll.why: All three rows stay. 'Sends down from the sky, of ...' is the same verb and structure in all three: of water (2:164), of provision (45:5), of mountains of hail (24:43). Different subject, same words; the reader must remember what comes after.
tree:0xoxszh0ud9mll.relation: What comes down from the sky can be life (water, provision) or a striking hail.

tree:18tfzmi06kkxz6.why: 34:2 and 57:4 share a whole clause: He knows what enters the earth and what comes out, what descends from the sky and what ascends, then different tails. In 36:28 'and what' is a negation ('and We were not sending down'), a different word.
tree:18tfzmi06kkxz6.changes: Removed 36:28: its 'and what' is a negation.
tree:18tfzmi06kkxz6.relation: God's knowledge of all that moves between earth and sky, then mercy (34:2) and His being with you (57:4).

check.why: 36:28 is unrelated: 'from the sky' follows a different verb (no army sent down). Removing it leaves the true pair 34:2 and 57:4.

tree:04ew8kx029o1w9.why: 2:120 and 13:37: if you followed their desires after the knowledge that came to you, you would have no protector from God, nor helper / defender. In 19:43 'what' is a relative ('what did not come to you'), while in the pair it is a negation: a different word.
tree:04ew8kx029o1w9.changes: Removed 19:43: its 'what' is a relative, not the negation.
tree:04ew8kx029o1w9.relation: Knowledge brings responsibility: following desires after it leaves one without protection.

tree:0o5d4rb0zqsusf.why: 'Saved from the great distress': Noah and his family (21:76, 37:76) and Moses and Aaron with their people (37:115).

tree:0d1truv12fojhx.why: 'Who would help me against God if ...': Noah if he drove the poor away (11:30), Salih if he disobeyed (11:63), and 'who can protect you from God if He wills' (33:17).
tree:0d1truv12fojhx.relation: No one can protect from God.

tree:1ef5fnt1gfmlp1.why: 'God has been gracious to us': Joseph reunited (12:90), those who envied Qarun (28:82), the people of the Garden (52:27).
tree:1ef5fnt1gfmlp1.relation: Recognising God's favour: after trial, after a near escape, and in Paradise.

tree:1it528908zgcpb.why: Only 'from the command of God' is shared, in three different senses (no refuge from it, wonder at it, guarding by it).

tree:1vblmw11uat6in.why: 'That is of the news of the unseen, which We reveal to you': Mary (3:44), Noah ('those' in 11:49), Joseph (12:102).

tree:0vp8zwd106tbp7.why: Only 'after' is shared, in three unrelated sentences (Satan's discord, victory at Mecca, intercession by God's leave).

tree:0hkt2ys09d7n24.why: 'From before them and behind them': Satan's attack from every side (7:17), the barrier around the deniers (36:9), messengers coming from all sides (41:14).
tree:0hkt2ys09d7n24.relation: Surrounded on every side: by Satan, by blindness, and by the call of the messengers.

tree:13q7r0a1r2et8a.why: 'The interpretation of events' three times in Yusuf: promised (12:6), begun in Egypt (12:21), and acknowledged by Joseph at the end (12:101).

tree:1p6wdy31t0ey0b.why: 'Whoever's scales are heavy': 7:8 and 23:102 identical, 101:6 with 'as for'. Followed by the light scales in the next ayah.

tree:1lq5rsb1qi35nf.why: 'Whoever brings an evil deed': only its like (6:160), thrown face-first (27:90), recompensed only for what they did (28:84).

tree:1oztqvl03xx8jn.why: 'Whoever's scales are light': 7:9 and 23:103 share the start and end differently, 101:8 'as for'. The pair of the previous card.

tree:0yvmyqw0vg5mf0.why: 'Those they call upon besides Him cannot ...': help (7:197), answer (13:14), judge (40:20).

check.why: Keep is right: 'those they call upon besides Him cannot' help, answer or judge, in the same structure on one theme.

tree:0f7qfzf1ai1p85.why: 'Nor smaller than that nor greater, but in a clear Book' (10:61, 34:3, with earth and heaven in reverse order) and 'nor less than that nor more' (58:7).

tree:0yer55a12fkeas.why: 'From your Lord; so whoever ...': sees (6:104), is guided (10:108), wills (18:29). The choice given after the message.

tree:08gmczw1q5leee.why: The demand 'why is a sign not sent down to him from his Lord? Say ...' with three answers (6:37, 13:27, 29:50).

tree:1oz5fcq0ngy9ky.why: 15:21 and 17:44: 'there is nothing but' its treasuries are with Us / it glorifies His praise, both in the same frame. 12:68 has the words inside 'it did not avail them anything against God, except a need', a different governing verb and an exception of another kind.
tree:1oz5fcq0ngy9ky.changes: Removed 12:68: different governing verb and structure.
tree:1oz5fcq0ngy9ky.relation: Everything has its store with God, and everything glorifies Him.

tree:16uc2oj1bfnry5.why: All three rows stay. All three have the same structure: a negation with 'anything', then 'nothing but ...' with the negative particle. The deniers say God sent down nothing and you only lie / are in error (36:15, 67:9); Jacob says he cannot avail his sons anything, judgment is only God's (12:67). Same words and structure, different speaker.
tree:16uc2oj1bfnry5.relation: Contrast: deniers deny revelation outright, while Jacob denies only his own power and leaves judgment to God.

tree:1i1w9u41x04ey2.why: Nothing escapes God in the earth or in the heaven (14:38), nothing can frustrate Him in the heavens or the earth (35:44): the order is reversed, a memorizer's point. In 8:60 'what' is conditional ('whatever you spend of anything'), a different word.
tree:1i1w9u41x04ey2.changes: Removed 8:60: its 'what' is conditional, not the negation.
tree:1i1w9u41x04ey2.relation: God's knowledge and power reach all of heaven and earth.

tree:075cwh81h0i60g.why: 'When the truth came to them from Us, they said ...': this is clear magic (10:76), why was he not given like Moses (28:48), kill the sons of the believers (40:25).
tree:075cwh81h0i60g.relation: Three reactions of deniers to the truth: slander, excuse, persecution.

tree:0fhyfiz0ipghkf.why: 'Of His bounty; indeed He ...' with three closings: is ever merciful to you (17:66), does not love the disbelievers (30:45), is Forgiving, Appreciative (35:30).

tree:1kxzy4z11b3uyt.why: 23:83 and 27:68: 'we and our fathers were promised this before', with the words in a different order, a classic memorizer point. In 2:91 the 'if' is conditional ('if you are believers'), while in the pair it is the negation ('this is nothing but'): a different word.
tree:1kxzy4z11b3uyt.changes: Removed 2:91: a different particle. The rows that read on (23:84, 27:69) are kept as they are.
tree:1kxzy4z11b3uyt.relation: The deniers' same dismissal in two surahs: old tales of the ancients.

tree:1ywbx3c0rgabqa.why: 'Have they not travelled ... those before them were stronger than them': 30:9, 40:21 ('they were, they'), 40:82 ('more numerous and stronger'). A well-known trap.
tree:1ywbx3c0rgabqa.relation: Past nations were stronger, and it did not save them.

tree:0o553is1q8rtmc.why: 'We never destroyed a town but ...' (15:4, 26:208) and 'there is no town but We will destroy it' (17:58). Same theme of God's decree on towns.

tree:19kzm8c1pcos2q.why: 'Town that We destroyed': how many (7:4), none of them believed (21:6), how many, while it was wrong-doing (22:45).

tree:0aqok0n0jcaftj.why: 'Whoever of you is ill' opens a concession in fasting (2:184) and in pilgrimage (2:196), each with a different remedy. In 2:232 'whoever' is a relative (the one among you who believes is admonished), not the conditional: a different word and structure.
tree:0aqok0n0jcaftj.changes: Removed 2:232: its 'whoever' is a relative, not a condition.
tree:0aqok0n0jcaftj.relation: Illness eases two acts of worship, each with its own make-up.

tree:19a0fgt0ymlvl1.why: 'And whoever disbelieves, then indeed God / my Lord is Free of need': of the worlds (3:97), Generous (27:40), Praiseworthy (31:12).

tree:1nymreg1u41lim.why: Only 'from every place' is shared: waves at sea, death in Hell, a town's provision. Unrelated images, nothing to confuse.

tree:00foapl1xz0bwb.why: 'Who provides for you from the sky (10:31, 27:64) / the heavens (34:24) and the earth?' with three different follow-ups.

tree:0u1tvsz1s0hcrf.why: Only 'whom He wills, and' is shared: guidance and spending (2:272), the dead not hearing (35:22). Unrelated.

tree:116zfth1ayhefb.why: 6:10 and 21:41 are identical: messengers were mocked, and what they mocked encompassed the mockers. 28:6 (Pharaoh shown what he feared from them) has the same relative and words, but its 'from them' belongs to another verb. Its row does not read on, but the two that do are kept whole, and 28:6 stays for the owner to judge.
tree:116zfth1ayhefb.relation: What the mockers mocked, and what Pharaoh feared, is what came upon them.

tree:0mynd5e1i1u9hm.why: 'Among them is one who says': the prayer for both worlds (2:201), 'excuse me' (9:49), 'which of you did this increase in faith?' (9:124).
tree:0mynd5e1i1u9hm.relation: What people say reveals what they want.

tree:06wufev1g235pn.why: The covenant of the Children of Israel: its terms (2:83), the twelve chiefs (5:12), the messengers they denied or killed (5:70).

tree:04wkhuk02x2jmi.why: 'Excellent is the reward of the workers': 'and excellent' (3:136), 'excellent' (29:58), 'so excellent' (39:74). The particle is the trap.

tree:1neinxt1nb78tp.why: 2:48 and 2:123: fear a Day when no soul will avail another, with intercession and ransom in reverse order, a classic pair. 36:54 has a different verb ('no soul will be wronged at all').
tree:1neinxt1nb78tp.relation: The Day when no one can help another, told twice with the order changed.

tree:1dvyfkl0rbsf5f.why: 'Benefit or harm': the Prophet has none for himself (7:188), the idols have none even for themselves (13:16), and on the Day no one has any for another (34:42).
tree:1dvyfkl0rbsf5f.relation: No one owns benefit or harm but God.

tree:1rimhj5161p1qb.why: 'We relate to you of the news of ...': the towns (7:101), the messengers (11:120), what has passed (20:99).

tree:14qypgb10mqkol.why: Wishes to be among the believers: 'and be' (6:27, 28:47) vs 'so be' (26:102). Each wish comes too late or is false.

tree:1mzx9nm00w3vsm.why: 'Grant me from ...': Zakariya twice 'from Yourself' (3:38, 19:5), Abraham 'of the righteous' (37:100).

tree:1shz78411wb81c.why: 'This is clear magic' said of Moses' signs (27:13), the Quran (46:7), Jesus' proofs (61:6). Same slander, three messengers.

tree:07812m70cjl6z7.why: All three rows stay. 'Shall I show you ...' is the same words and structure: Moses' sister offering a nurse in two tellings (20:40, 28:12), and the call to a trade that saves from punishment (61:10). Different subject, same opening.
tree:07812m70cjl6z7.relation: A guide to what saves: a nurse for the infant Moses, and faith and striving for the believers.

tree:07b3kyj13lxdcz.why: 'Those who guard their prayer' (6:92, 70:34) vs 'those constant in their prayer' (70:23). Two in al-Ma'arij.

tree:1bmygms0ro284e.why: 'So they do not hear' (7:100, 41:4) vs 'while they do not hear' (8:21).

tree:1oxis2a0ddy8nw.why: 'It is the truth from ...': the deniers' defiant prayer 'if this is the truth from You' (8:32), 'rather it is the truth from your Lord' (32:3), and the believers who believe in it as the truth from their Lord (47:2).
tree:1oxis2a0ddy8nw.relation: Contrast: the same truth challenged by deniers and accepted by believers.

tree:0f06rhn01dhk0d.why: 'And He is the Wise, the Aware' closes three ayat with different lead-ins: the Subduer (6:18), Knower of the unseen (6:73), praise in the Hereafter (34:1).

tree:0s82ths1ghl7oe.why: 22:62 and 31:30 are near-identical ('that is because God is the Truth', with 'it is' falsehood only in 22:62); 34:23 ends 'and He is the Most High, the Great'.

tree:00u4hw5003yy17.why: 'Indeed He is the Knowing, the Wise': Jacob's hope (12:83) and Joseph's thanks (12:100), father and son in one surah; 66:2 with 'and He is'.
tree:00u4hw5003yy17.relation: Jacob trusts God's wisdom in loss, Joseph praises it in reunion.

tree:0nwkghh0epzuxb.why: 'He is only one God': I am free of what you associate (6:19), so that people of understanding remember (14:52), so fear Me (16:51).

tree:0g5j8051eerbsd.why: 'Until God judges, and He is the best of judges': Shu'ayb (7:87), the Prophet (10:109), Joseph's eldest brother (12:80).

tree:1kbjzl60zkf9bc.why: 'Lord of the Throne': the Great (9:129, 27:26) vs the Noble (23:116). One word.

tree:08khule16hyoxm.why: All three rows stay. 'He, in the Hereafter, is ...' is the same structure: among the losers (3:85, 5:5) and blind (17:72). The first two close the same way; 17:72 is the same frame with another predicate. The rows of 3:85 and 5:5 read on and stay as they are.
tree:08khule16hyoxm.relation: Loss in the Hereafter for whoever rejects faith or was blind here.

tree:1lbenex1nge2ob.why: 'While he is a believer, those ...': will enter the Garden (4:124, 40:40, with 'male or female') and their effort is appreciated (17:19).
tree:1lbenex1nge2ob.relation: Faith is the condition for deeds to count.

tree:16oytsy0fz0fjc.why: 'He gives life and causes death' after 'no god but He' with three tails: believe in His Messenger (7:158), to Him you return (10:56), your Lord and your fathers' Lord (44:8).

tree:0zopmhp0mnesex.why: 'Jews or Christians' three times in al-Baqara: only they enter the Garden (2:111), be them to be guided (2:135), Abraham and his sons were (2:140).
tree:0zopmhp0mnesex.relation: Exclusive claims answered with Abraham's pure faith.

tree:13600310z200qn.why: 'What we found our fathers upon': 'even if their fathers ...' (5:104, 31:21) and Pharaoh's people to Moses (10:78).
tree:13600310z200qn.relation: Blind following of forefathers against every messenger.

tree:1ixfkdv0wsh66v.why: 'Only one blast, and then they ...': extinguished (36:29), all brought before Us (36:53), looking on (37:19).

tree:0bbmeu000dywke.why: 'The promise of God is true' with three tails: who is truer in speech (4:122), He begins creation (10:4), He is the Mighty (31:9).

tree:1cclkk80zzdz3e.why: 'No protector and no intercessor besides Him': 6:51 and 6:70 in one surah ('Him' vs 'God'), and 32:4 'you have'.

tree:0p7pbs20n180l2.why: The angels glorify their Lord's praise around the Throne (39:75), bearing it and asking forgiveness for believers (40:7), and for those on earth (42:5).
tree:0p7pbs20n180l2.relation: The angels' worship includes praying for us.

tree:0ppf7e518q5o69.why: 'They hasten to good deeds': the righteous People of the Book (3:114), Zakariya's family (21:90), the believers who fear their Lord (23:61).

tree:1qgpg4u16c7dec.why: 'God leaves astray whom He wills' (14:4, 74:31) vs 'whoever is a transgressor and doubter' (40:34).

tree:1l2jmon1swhnfj.why: All three rows stay. 'God knows those who ...' is the same verb and structure. 3:142 and 9:16 are the close pair (did you think ... while God has not yet made evident those who strive); 24:63 says God knows those who slip away. Different subject, same words.
tree:1l2jmon1swhnfj.relation: God makes known the strivers and the deserters alike.

tree:0rt2gv51wla7kx.why: 'Do they not know that God ...': knows their secret (9:78), accepts repentance (9:104), extends provision (39:52, 'have they not').

tree:04fq1tr0oiyyfr.why: 'O Jesus son of Mary' three times in the last part of al-Ma'ida: God reminds him of His favours (5:110), the disciples ask for the table (5:112), God asks about worship of him (5:116).

tree:1nxvxyz0a78uf1.why: 'He will forgive you your sins': for following the Prophet (3:31), for upright speech (33:71), for faith and striving (61:12), each with a different tail.

tree:1izjpnw0tg41yw.why: 'How will I have a boy?': Zakariya in 3:40 and 19:8 (old age and barren wife in reverse order), Mary in 19:20.

tree:1cjlbtm1nmvy6w.why: 'He will inform them of what they did': 24:64, 58:6 and 58:7, each with a different closing. Two neighbouring ayat in al-Mujadila.

tree:0ab0jjk19rh14k.why: All three rows stay. 'Those who disbelieve wish' is the same verb and words. 4:42 and 15:2 are their wishes on the Day; 2:105 has the verb negated (they do not wish good for you). Same words, different subject.
tree:0ab0jjk19rh14k.relation: What the deniers wish: now they begrudge the believers good, then they wish they had been Muslims.

tree:1kr7wdt1ovaw3r.why: 'The day the two armies met': those who fled at Uhud (3:155), what struck you at Uhud was by God's leave (3:166), and the Day of Criterion at Badr (8:41).
tree:1kr7wdt1ovaw3r.relation: Victory and setback both by God's will.

tree:0o2adjz1kuv15f.why: All three rows stay. 39:15 and 42:45 share 'the losers are those who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection', then a warning opening 'truly'. 11:60 has the same words and structure: 'and on the Day of Resurrection; truly, Aad denied their Lord'. Different subject, same words, so it is the reciter's slip, not a reason to remove.
tree:0o2adjz1kuv15f.relation: Who the true losers are, and a people (Aad) who became an example of it.

tree:1n4iko701gahlr.why: 'Leave them to plunge and play until they meet their Day which they are promised' (43:83, 70:42, identical) and 'woe from their Day which they are promised' (51:60).

tree:0c73h040l6pi9a.why: 'Woe to us, we were wrongdoers' (21:14, 21:46) vs 'we were transgressors' (68:31).

tree:1s1tz4x1cn8afp.why: Two different words share one spelling: the command 'believe in God and His Messenger' (4:136, 57:7) and the description 'the believers are only those who believed in God and His Messenger' (24:62, 49:15). Each pair is its own memorizer card: two commands, and two definitions of the true believer.
tree:1s1tz4x1cn8afp.changes: Split: the command (4:136, 57:7) is a different word from the past-tense description (24:62, 49:15).
tree:1s1tz4x1cn8afp.relation: The command to believe, and what true belief looks like: staying with the Prophet, not doubting, striving.

check.why: Right split: the command 'believe' (4:136, 57:7) and the past tense 'those who believed' (24:62, 49:15) are different words in the same spelling.

tree:167ifpl0t13q0z.why: 'Those who believed and were mindful' closing four ayat: the friends of God (10:63), Joseph's reward (12:57), saved with 'We saved' (27:53) vs 'and We rescued' (41:18).

tree:0ba3ctx1c3c3ql.why: 'And revived the earth with it after its death' in four lists of signs; 29:63 has 'from after' and comes as a question to the deniers.

tree:04bylgm1abre8k.why: 'When he called out to his Lord': Zakariya (19:3, 21:89) and Job (21:83, 38:41, 'harm' vs 'Satan has touched me').
tree:04bylgm1abre8k.relation: Prophets' private calls to God in need.

tree:0eur0ay1si944c.why: 'When their term comes': they cannot delay or advance it (7:34, 10:49, 16:61), and 35:45 (twin of 16:61) ends 'then God sees His servants'.

tree:1dkgexu079la5y.why: 'When the promise of ... comes': the first and last of the two (17:5, 17:7), the last (17:104), and Dhul-Qarnayn's 'my Lord' (18:98).

tree:1dxwjf1155gpvr.why: Mentioning God's name over food: on game (5:4), and three neighbouring ayat of al-An'am (6:118, 6:119 allowed, 6:121 forbidden when not mentioned).

tree:1mfl3y60rz5e8s.why: 'Stronger than them in power': three 'have they not travelled' ayat (30:9, 35:44, 40:21) and 'Ad's boast answered (41:15).
tree:1mfl3y60rz5e8s.relation: Strength did not save the nations before.

tree:0sbbdwd0vp0n39.why: 'Obey God and His Messenger' three times in al-Anfal (8:1, 8:20, 8:46) and in 58:13, each with a different tail.

tree:1hjctgw0gbvwre.why: 'God has prepared for them': gardens (9:89), forgiveness and great reward (33:35), and a severe punishment (58:15, 65:10).
tree:1hjctgw0gbvwre.relation: Contrast: what God prepares for the obedient and for the hypocrites.

tree:0ihxe0a15lwi1c.why: 'Work according to your position': 'I am working, so you will know' (6:135, 39:39), 'you will know' (11:93), 'we are working' (11:121).

tree:06ktmpl0psweqt.why: 'Only the clear conveying': on the messengers (16:35), on the Messenger (24:54, 29:18), on us (36:17).

tree:122u5iu1bl2ek2.why: 'They deceive / mislead / destroy only themselves, and they do not perceive' (2:9, 3:69, 6:26) and 'they do not harm you' (4:113).
tree:122u5iu1bl2ek2.relation: Evil plots harm only their makers.

tree:0ilddw610q9aak.why: 'A human like you': the messengers' own answer (14:11) and the deniers' charge (21:3, 23:24, 23:33), with different tails.

tree:0h7843z1gzagsh.why: 'A human like us': the deniers' charge against the messengers (14:10, 26:154, 26:186, 36:15), each with a different tail.

tree:1i60jdj0i8h547.why: 'Only one blast': three times in Ya-Sin (36:29, 36:49, 36:53) and once in Sad (38:15), with different tails.

tree:0ierlx21pidsce.why: All four rows stay. 'Only upon God' is the same restriction in the same structure in all: my reward is only upon God (Noah in 10:72 and 11:29, the Prophet in 34:47), and every creature's provision is only upon God (11:6). Different subject, same words and structure.
tree:0ierlx21pidsce.relation: Who pays: the messengers ask no wage because their reward is on God, as is every creature's provision.

tree:1d1tizz1tny2oz.why: 'The home of the Hereafter is better for those who are mindful; do you not reason?' (6:32, 7:169, 12:109 with small differences), and 12:57 'the reward of the Hereafter'.

tree:1cf2rl81awhdfw.why: 'We detail the signs for a people who know' with four verb forms: We have detailed (6:97), thus We detail (7:32), and We detail (9:11), He details (10:5).

tree:05pn55m1i1qepu.why: 'The land which We blessed': inherited by the Children of Israel (7:137), Abraham and Lot (21:71), Solomon's wind (21:81), Sheba's route (34:18).

tree:0pc0vgp069hxdn.why: 'The truth from their Lord': known by believers and People of the Book (2:26, 2:144), and followed by believers (47:2, 47:3).

tree:139h7n30morifh.why: 'The life of this world is only ...': the enjoyment of delusion (3:185), play and amusement (6:32), amusement and play in reverse order (29:64).

tree:0xbjicd1pytaq9.why: 'What We revealed to you': to recite it (13:30), they nearly tempted you from it (17:73), it is the truth (35:31), the same religion given to Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus (42:13).
tree:0xbjicd1pytaq9.relation: The revelation as one message across all prophets.

tree:07fbe6m161han8.why: 'Those who took besides God / besides Him': protectors like the spider's house (29:41), 'only to bring us near' (39:3), God watches them (42:6), gods that abandoned them (46:28).
tree:07fbe6m161han8.relation: The weakness of every protector other than God.

tree:1s2nzp510ieyfl.why: All three rows stay. 'Those of them who disbelieved' is the same words and structure in all three. 5:73 and 9:90 threaten them with a painful punishment; in 5:110 those of them who disbelieved said 'this is plain magic'. Different subject, same phrase. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:1s2nzp510ieyfl.relation: Those among them who refuse: their word against the signs, and the punishment promised them.

tree:18yqqxp0zsfpfr.why: 'Those who dispute about the signs of God' three times in Ghafir (40:35, 40:56, 40:69) and 'about Our signs' in 42:35.

tree:1t3o9170q1r18h.why: 'Those who fear their Lord unseen': (21:49, 35:18, 67:12) and those whose skins shiver at the Book (39:23).
tree:1t3o9170q1r18h.relation: Fear of the unseen Lord as the mark of the believer.

tree:0zdfxm91pir7ah.why: 'Those who say: our Lord ...': forgive us (3:16), take us out of this town (4:75), avert Hell (25:65), grant us comfort in spouses (25:74).
tree:0zdfxm91pir7ah.relation: The believers' prayers for themselves, the oppressed and their families.

tree:0ulq2af0ntkv99.why: 'Those who establish prayer': with zakat while bowing (5:55), and spending (8:3); 27:3 and 31:4 identical with certainty in the Hereafter.

tree:0f0kbwm0lyvn06.why: 'The heavens and the earth; and God is ...' with four closings: aware (3:180), able (3:189), sees (49:18), witness (85:9). A memorizer's trap.

tree:14uh0sw067vvu6.why: 'God sees what they do' (2:96, 3:163, 5:71) vs 'what you do' (49:18).

tree:0xynzy31mldcfj.why: 'Among people is one who disputes about God without knowledge': 22:3 'and follows every devil', 22:8 and 31:20 identical 'without guidance or an enlightening Book'. In 31:6 'without knowledge' follows 'to lead astray from God's way', a different governing verb.
tree:0xynzy31mldcfj.changes: Removed 31:6: a different governing verb. The rows that read on (22:9, 31:21) are kept as they are.
tree:0xynzy31mldcfj.relation: Arguing about God without knowledge, guidance or a Book: what it leads to.

tree:002or0l1850s97.why: 'God encompasses what they do' (3:120, 8:47; 4:108 'ever encompassing') vs 'sees what they do' (8:39).

tree:1igy0ki0if83uy.why: God sealed (2:7) and set a seal (9:93, 16:108, 47:16) upon their hearts, each continuing differently.
tree:1igy0ki0if83uy.relation: Hearts sealed as the end of stubborn refusal.

tree:142pk3g10ova0s.why: 'And God knows the wrongdoers': 2:95 and 62:7 nearly identical (never / will not wish for death), plus 2:246 and 9:47.

tree:1a6vc0t1bq2rcj.why: 'Exalted is God above what they associate' (7:190 'so exalted', 27:63) vs 'glory be to God above what they associate' (52:43, 59:23).

tree:003clkk1g2yggy.why: 'God is Forgiving, Forbearing' after four lead-ins: 'and God' (2:225, 5:101), 'know that God' (2:235), 'indeed God' (3:155).

tree:0iqiwyh0kmf72n.why: 'God does not fail His promise': 'indeed God does not fail the appointment' (3:9, 13:31), 'God does not fail His promise' (30:6), 'God does not fail the appointment' (39:20).

tree:1q5h6vp0cc7e55.why: 'And fear God that you may succeed' (2:189, 3:130, 3:200) vs 'remember the favours of God that you may succeed' (7:69).

tree:1p2yt911g9m2hd.why: 'God is with the patient': 'indeed God' (2:153, 8:46) vs 'and God' (2:249, 8:66), each in a call to patience or a battle.

tree:1df2ud000ktz3e.why: Only 'God, before' is shared, in four unrelated sentences (killing prophets, betrayal, broken pledge, God's earlier word).

tree:1r76dzz0nuzk6t.why: 'That is because God is the Truth': 22:6, 22:62 and 31:30 (with 'it is' only in 22:62), and 'they will know that God is the clear Truth' (24:25).

tree:0vr6wa815gbtsy.why: 'And those are the ...' is a stock closing; these four (winners, liars, successful, people of understanding) have unrelated subjects and nothing more in common.

tree:0g46cqs1bwe0wc.why: 18:43 and 28:81: no party to help him besides God, and he could not help himself: the garden owner and Qarun, both ruined by their wealth. 2:143 has the same words and structure (a negation starting a new clause after God's name), so it stays. In 6:136 'what was for God' uses a relative, a different word.
tree:0g46cqs1bwe0wc.changes: Removed only 6:136: its 'what' is a relative, not the negation. 2:143 stays: same words and structure, only a different subject.
tree:0g46cqs1bwe0wc.relation: Two men ruined by wealth, with no one to help them besides God.

tree:1yct2jz0e5tl3z.why: 'God does what He wills' with two verbs for willing (2:253, 22:14 vs 3:40, 22:18), the last two close together in al-Hajj.

tree:19teaw01yghuto.why: 'The Messiah son of Mary': 5:17 and 5:72 identical claims answered differently, 5:75 he was only a messenger, 9:31 they took him as lord.
tree:19teaw01yghuto.relation: Every claim of divinity for Jesus answered in the Quran.

tree:0cmp4ux0wl2ea9.why: Two phrasings: 'and there is no god but God' with the emphatic negation (3:62, 38:65), and the testimony itself 'no god but God' (37:35, 47:19), its only two places. The negations are different words, so each pair is its own memorizer card.
tree:0cmp4ux0wl2ea9.changes: Split by the two negations: 3:62 and 38:65; 37:35 and 47:19.
tree:0cmp4ux0wl2ea9.relation: The testimony refused by the arrogant (37:35) and the command to know it (47:19).

check.why: Right split: 'and there is no god but God' and 'there is no god but God' are different words.

tree:1dx8jf41taoyze.why: 'What god other than God would bring you ...?': your hearing and sight back (6:46), light (28:71), night (28:72). A clear set for memorizers and for pondering God's blessings. In 52:43 the words follow 'or have they', a different structure with no 'who would bring you'.
tree:1dx8jf41taoyze.relation: Hearing, sight, light and night: none but God could give them back.

tree:1i8hfgi0vndo36.why: 'I have been commanded to be ...': the first to submit (6:14), of the Muslims (10:72), of the believers (10:104).

tree:1hclcgg03av1t6.why: 'Their wealth and children will not avail them against God' (3:10, 3:116, 58:17) and 'let not their wealth and children impress you' (9:55).
tree:1hclcgg03av1t6.relation: Wealth and children: no protection from God, and a means of punishment.

tree:00wds250yctrqh.why: 'And I was commanded to be of the Muslims' (10:72, 27:91) vs 'of the believers' (10:104), a memorizer's trap. In 2:67 the words follow a different governing verb ('I seek refuge in God from being of the ignorant').
tree:00wds250yctrqh.changes: Removed 2:67: a different governing verb. The rows that read on (10:73, 27:92) are kept as they are.
tree:00wds250yctrqh.relation: The messenger's own submission, stated by Noah and by the Prophet.

tree:179w26b1985ejv.why: 'God is Free of need': Praiseworthy (2:267, 31:12), of the worlds (3:97), of you (39:7).

tree:18dixba0y58sto.why: Only 'indeed God has' is shared, before three unrelated verbs (sent Talut, destroyed earlier generations, judged between servants).

tree:0hhdw7c06b9hg2.why: 'If evil befalls them': they blame the Prophet (4:78), they see Moses as a bad omen (7:131), they despair (30:36), man is ungrateful (42:48).
tree:0hhdw7c06b9hg2.relation: How people react to hardship: blaming others, despair, ingratitude.

tree:1r0ekyj0vbvbup.why: 'If they turn away, then only ...': they are in dissension (2:137), your duty is to convey (3:20, 16:82), on him is what he was charged with (24:54).

tree:076xhp713jx563.why: 'You stayed only ...': a little (17:52, 23:114), ten (20:103), a day (20:104).
tree:076xhp713jx563.relation: How short life will seem on the Day.

tree:10ekrs21dwmd8a.why: 'If He wills, He can remove you and bring ...': others (4:133), successors (6:133), a new creation (14:19, 35:16, identical with the same next ayah).

tree:1rhi6le1472zre.why: 'To our Lord we will return': Pharaoh's magicians twice (7:125, 26:50), the riders (43:14 'surely return'), and 'to our Lord we turn in hope' (68:32).

tree:08u7pwz00sy3ov.why: 'We were wrongdoers': the destroyed towns (7:5), 'woe to us' (21:14, 21:46), 'glory to our Lord' from the garden owners (68:29).

tree:0i7x6h20qc3zo4.why: Two different senses of 'what God sent down from': rain from the sky (2:164, 45:5, a pair already in its own card) and the Book (2:174, 42:15). Mixed together they make no single point.

tree:1tly0lc1ytq4yu.why: 'We sent down to you the Book': in truth to judge (4:105), confirming (5:48), and thus (29:47), in truth so worship God (39:2).

tree:1skfxf417bwcdi.why: 'He was of Our servants': the sincere (12:24, Joseph) and the believers, three times in as-Saffat (37:81, 37:111, 37:132).

tree:1wyp2bo0m0p5vo.why: 'I fear that ...': Abraham for his father (19:45), Moses that they will deny him (26:12, 28:34), and Pharaoh that Moses will change their religion (40:26).
tree:1wyp2bo0m0p5vo.relation: Contrast: the prophets fear for others; Pharaoh fears for his power.

tree:1kuq32o05utqne.why: 'So wait, I am with you among those who wait' (7:71, 10:20, 10:102) vs 'wait, I am with you among the waiting' with another verb (52:31).

tree:0qqxxxg01nlms6.why: 'How can I have a boy / child?': Zakariya (3:40, 19:8) and Mary (3:47 'child', 19:20 'boy').

tree:0izq9ge08gny9i.why: 'Or on a journey' in fasting (2:184, 2:185) and in purification (4:43, 5:6), each pair with near-identical wording.
tree:0izq9ge08gny9i.relation: The same concession for travellers in fasting and prayer.

tree:08048110029s1n.why: All four rows stay. 'Or what their right hands possess' is the same relative and the same words in all four. 23:6 and 70:30 are identical, with matching runs after them; 4:3 and 24:31 use the same phrase in other rulings. Different subject, same words. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:08048110029s1n.relation: The same phrase across marriage, chastity and modesty rulings.

tree:1gtd4z51hsxccn.why: 'Those are the companions of Hellfire': after 'disbelieved and denied Our signs' (5:10, 5:86, 57:19) and after 'strove against Our signs' (22:51).

tree:12gzd0d0sqfdff.why: All four rows stay. 'Allies instead of ...' is the same words and structure. Three ayat forbid or condemn taking the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers (3:28, 4:139, 4:144); 7:30 says the astray took devils as allies instead of God. Different subject, same phrase.
tree:12gzd0d0sqfdff.relation: Whom one takes as ally: the disbelievers instead of the believers, the devils instead of God.

tree:0sdybuy0hutioe.why: 'Where is what you used to ...?': call upon (7:37), worship (26:92), associate (40:73), one question with three verbs. In 57:4 'wherever you are' has a different 'what' (He is with you wherever you are), a different structure.
tree:0sdybuy0hutioe.changes: Removed 57:4: a different word and structure.
tree:0sdybuy0hutioe.relation: The question put to idolaters at death and on the Day: where are your gods now?

tree:1ly60j01pmvjx6.why: 'We believe in God and what was sent down': to us (2:136, 5:59), upon us (3:84), and the believing People of the Book (3:199).

tree:1gbtlt30txgql3.why: Only 'some of them to others' is shared, with four different verbs (alone with, inspire, look at, throw back words). Unrelated settings.

tree:0n4pegc17xhb1e.why: 'God is ever Knowing of all things' is a stock closing found in many places; these four (inheritance shares, the Seal of the Prophets, hidden thoughts, Hudaybiya) share nothing more.

check.why: Drop is right: a stock closing with nothing more shared.

tree:1io07ob1675p1h.why: 'Rather they are in doubt' (27:66, 38:8, 44:9) vs 'in confusion' (50:15). The deniers' state described four times.

tree:1xw6kmy1mvskrg.why: 'We disbelieve in what you were sent with': said to many messengers (14:9 with doubt, 34:34, 41:14, 43:24 with 'disbelievers').
tree:1xw6kmy1mvskrg.relation: The same answer from every nation that denied.

tree:0e3iudu1fwmzj4.why: 'Whoever repents, believes and does good': enter the Garden (19:60), forgiven (20:82), evil turned to good (25:70 'a righteous deed'), among the successful (28:67).
tree:0e3iudu1fwmzj4.relation: Repentance with faith and deeds opens every door.

tree:0wpfzx11rdeat7.why: 'Rivers flowing beneath them': in the Garden (7:43, 10:9, 18:31), and beneath the earlier nations who were destroyed despite them (6:6).
tree:0wpfzx11rdeat7.relation: Contrast: rivers as worldly comfort that did not save, and as reward that lasts.

tree:1x345nr0gxh4ff.why: 'That you worship none but God': 11:26 (Noah) and 46:21 (Hud) end 'I fear for you the punishment of a painful / great day'; 11:2 and 41:14 give the same call.

tree:11sw5oa10az7f8.why: 'Do not spread corruption on earth': after its reform (7:56, 7:85), the hypocrites' answer (2:11), and 'would you spread corruption if you turned away' (47:22).

tree:0b20kai0ch42re.why: 'Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you ...': differ (6:164) vs do (39:7), both after 'no bearer bears another's burden'; and 'then to your Lord you will be returned' (32:11, 45:15).

tree:0v0dwnh0g3f441.why: 'Seek forgiveness of your Lord, then repent to Him' four times in Hud: the Prophet, Hud, Salih, Shu'ayb, each with a different promise.
tree:0v0dwnh0g3f441.relation: Every prophet's call: forgiveness and repentance bring blessing.

tree:1kjbtnj1gtuyon.why: 'Then He causes you to die, then gives you life' (2:28, 22:66, 30:40) vs 'He gives you life, then causes you to die, then gathers you' (45:26).

tree:1eb8bjn0rrxd6x.why: 'After the knowledge that has come to you': warnings against following their desires (2:120, 2:145, 13:37) and the challenge of mutual cursing (3:61).
tree:1eb8bjn0rrxd6x.relation: Once knowledge has come, no compromise with desires.

tree:1h93rtm1ns3p8m.why: 'He made for you the night': to rest and the day to see (10:67, 40:61, near-identical), as a garment (25:47), night and day (28:73).

tree:1v6ewk511ac3hl.why: All four rows stay. 'Until, when he reached ...' is the same words and structure: Dhul-Qarnayn's three journeys (18:86, 18:90, 18:93) and a man reaching his full strength and forty years (46:15). Different subject, same opening.
tree:1v6ewk511ac3hl.relation: Reaching: the ends of the earth for a king, maturity for a man, and both turn to thanks.

tree:0oy1pmd1fteb0b.why: 'Abiding therein, and that is ...': the great success (4:13), the reward of the doers of good (5:85), of who purifies himself (20:76), and of the wrongdoers in the Fire (59:17).
tree:0oy1pmd1fteb0b.relation: Contrast: the same eternal abiding in the Garden and in the Fire.

tree:0kptien11hd1gb.why: 'Creator of all things' in four declarations, with the order of 'no god but He' and the tails changing (6:102, 13:16, 39:62, 40:62).

tree:0o7omo003vwgj2.why: 'That is because they said': trade is like usury (2:275), the Fire will touch us only briefly (3:24), no blame toward the gentiles (3:75), we will obey you in part (47:26).

tree:0bzgld31qhgr49.why: 'Evil is what they judge' closing four ayat, with 'truly' only in 16:59; two begin 'or do they think' (29:4, 45:21).

tree:1km0l160139xgy.why: 'Glory be to God above what they describe' (23:91, 37:159) vs 'above what they associate' (52:43, 59:23).

tree:0cpd5st0hm5bx5.why: All four rows stay. In all four 'God's way, and those' ends a clause and opens a new group. 8:72 and 8:74 are the close pair (believed, emigrated, strove, and those who sheltered and helped); 4:76 contrasts believers fighting in God's way with the disbelievers; 9:34 turns to the hoarders. Same words and structure, different subjects.
tree:0cpd5st0hm5bx5.relation: Who fights and spends in God's way, and who fights against it or hoards.

tree:1wjc27l0m17k1z.why: Only 'anything; indeed God' is shared, joining the end of one clause to an unrelated closing name in four different ayat.

tree:1j169ps0448m10.why: 'No power to harm or benefit': the idols for you (5:76), the Prophet for himself (10:49), the calf (20:89), the gods for themselves (25:3).
tree:1j169ps0448m10.relation: Nothing worshipped besides God owns harm or benefit.

tree:0dg0h4h1ffy9id.why: All four rows stay. 'Perhaps it will be' is the same words and structure in all four: perhaps their term has drawn near (7:185), perhaps it is near (17:51), perhaps it is close behind you (27:72), perhaps he will be among the successful (28:67). Different subject, same phrase.
tree:0dg0h4h1ffy9id.relation: Perhaps: a warning that the end may be near, and a hope for the one who repents.

tree:0p08pqr1aahysf.why: The three prayers 'give us victory over the disbelieving people' (2:250, 2:286, 3:147) are already a card of their own; 5:68 ('do not grieve over the disbelieving people') is a different subject.

tree:1n6cqdk1hsr636.why: 'Those who believe and do good, those ...': companions of the Garden (2:82), forgiveness and great reward (11:11), forgiveness and noble provision (34:4), best of creatures (98:7).

tree:1nfhfjx06r5uah.why: Disputing about the signs of God, four times in Ghafir: none but disbelievers (40:4), without authority (40:35, 40:56), how are they turned away (40:69).
tree:1nfhfjx06r5uah.relation: Ghafir's recurring theme: arguing against God's signs from pride.

tree:19nmsyt0p8qudf.why: 27:87 and 39:68 describe the Trumpet: all in the heavens and earth terrified / swoon, except whom God wills. In 11:6 and 11:116 the 'except' closes a negation ('no creature ... except', 'forbidding corruption ... except a few'), a different structure from the exception out of 'all in the earth'.
tree:19nmsyt0p8qudf.changes: Removed 11:6 and 11:116: their 'except' belongs to a negation, a different structure.
tree:19nmsyt0p8qudf.relation: The Trumpet told twice: terror and swooning, with God's exception in both.

check.why: Removing 11:6 and 11:116 is right: their 'except' begins unrelated clauses, a different structure.

tree:0739w220t1ry1c.why: Only 'on earth, of' is shared, joining four unrelated clauses (no protector, successors, creatures prostrating, trees as pens).

tree:1622pz81yaea92.why: 'On land and sea': God knows all in it (6:59), He makes you travel (10:22), He carries the children of Adam (17:70), and corruption appears in it because of people (30:41).
tree:1622pz81yaea92.relation: God's care over land and sea, and man's corruption of it.

check.why: I would drop it. 'On land and sea' is a common phrase here across four unrelated subjects (God's knowledge, travel, honour, corruption). The 'God's care' relation is read into them, and a stock phrase with different subjects leans to a drop under the brief.

tree:06yt0is15fyisq.why: 'In the Gardens of Bliss' with different lead-ins: those who believe and do good (10:9, 22:56), and alone as a short ayah (37:43, 56:12).

tree:0ix9wab1veitaz.why: 'In gardens and springs': 'the mindful are in' (15:45, 51:15) and alone (26:147 Thamud's worldly gardens, 44:52 the Garden).
tree:0ix9wab1veitaz.relation: Contrast: Thamud's gardens in this world (26:147) and the gardens of the mindful.

tree:00m2h4m1y78ju4.why: All four rows stay. 'In the Book of God' has the same words and sense (God's decree and record) in all four: blood relatives are closer in it (8:75, 33:6), twelve months are in it (9:36), the dead stayed in it until the Day (30:56). Different subject, same phrase.
tree:00m2h4m1y78ju4.relation: What God has written: kinship, the months, and the term of the dead.

tree:00bzyef0qhvz49.why: All four rows stay as one card. 'Those who do not ... said' is the same words and structure in all four, and the trap is exactly which verb follows: 'do not know' (2:113, 2:118) or 'do not hope to meet Us' (10:15, 25:21). 2:118 and 25:21 both demand that God speak or angels come. Splitting would hide that.
tree:00bzyef0qhvz49.relation: The same demands from those without knowledge and those who do not expect to meet God.

tree:010vj7x0qxxvkx.why: 'Did I not tell you': to the angels (2:33) and Jacob (12:96) with 'to you (plural)'; al-Khidr to Moses twice, without and with 'to you' (18:72, 18:75). A famous trap.

tree:027fllw0ltiqlq.why: 'They said: do not fear': the angels to Abraham (11:70, 51:28), to Lot (29:33), the litigants to David (38:22).

tree:1wmil5z19zla77.why: 'Say: I am only ...': a human like you (18:110, 41:6, same opening, different tails), a warner (38:65), one of the warners (27:92).

tree:09l30nu0iddu0u.why: 'Little do you give thanks' after hearing, sight and hearts (23:78, 32:9, 67:23) and after livelihoods (7:10).
tree:09l30nu0iddu0u.relation: God's gifts to man and his little gratitude.

tree:09i4l951jrbymj.why: 'When it is said to them: come': to what God sent down and to the Messenger (4:61, 5:104, identical start), to fight (3:167), for the Messenger to ask forgiveness for you (63:5).
tree:09i4l951jrbymj.relation: Hypocrites and deniers turning away from the call.

tree:0r1lse305pwzsp.why: 'God is ever, of what they / you do, ...': encompassing (4:108), seeing (33:9, 48:24), aware (48:11).

tree:0k3v1aa0qq2d6e.why: All four rows stay. 3:164 and 62:2 are near-identical (a messenger who recites, purifies, teaches, though they were before in clear error). 30:49 has the same structure, 'though they were before ... surely in despair', and 2:89 'and they were before' with another verb. Same words and structure, different subjects. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:0k3v1aa0qq2d6e.relation: What people were before: in error before the Prophet, in despair before the rain, seeking victory before the Book came.

tree:095ejw60z1ogu6.why: 'Indeed many of the people are ...': defiantly disobedient (5:49), heedless of Our signs (10:92), deniers of the meeting with their Lord (30:8), one frame with three endings. In 14:36 'many of the people' is the object of 'they led astray', a different governing verb.
tree:095ejw60z1ogu6.relation: What most people are: disobedient, heedless of signs, denying the meeting.

tree:1inr8mf1q8nd39.why: 'Those who disbelieved in the signs of God': severe punishment (3:4), seized for sins (8:52), despair of My mercy (29:23), the losers (39:63).

tree:1t7n5gq00tq5s2.why: 'Which you used to deny': the Fire (32:20), the Day of Decision (37:21), 'go to what you denied' (77:29), 'this is what you denied' (83:17).

tree:0gmhqn60qp6uds.why: 'So how was My reproach' closing four ayat about earlier deniers (22:44, 34:45, 35:26, 67:18).

tree:116aqxt1e21jzh.why: 'I ask you no reward / wealth for it': the Prophet (6:90, 42:23), Noah (11:29, 'wealth'), Hud (11:51). Each with a different tail.

tree:191hd9q15lqa70.why: 'No blame on the two of them' in family rulings: ransom (2:229), remarriage (2:230), weaning (2:233), reconciliation (4:128).

tree:0eytwh81duyvx2.why: 'The Hour, no doubt about it': the cave sleepers as proof (18:21), it is coming (22:7, 40:59), and the deniers' answer (45:32).

tree:0oeeuj40wvg3q2.why: 'God does not love every ...': sinful disbeliever (2:276), treacherous ingrate (22:38), arrogant boaster (31:18, 57:23).

tree:10y46wh1qqkc5t.why: 'Those who do not hope to meet Us': content with this life (10:7), left to wander (10:11), demand another Quran (10:15), demand angels (25:21). Three in Yunus.

tree:0e0wqd513g8dnx.why: 'God does not let the reward of ... be lost': the believers (3:171) vs the doers of good (9:120, 11:115, 12:90).

tree:0r2v7jw06tdpem.why: Two pairs share 'does not avail against': conjecture does not avail against the truth (10:36, 53:28, near-identical), and Hell's shade and food do not avail against flame or hunger (77:31, 88:7). The subjects are two different things, so the split is fair.
tree:0r2v7jw06tdpem.changes: Split into conjecture and truth (10:36, 53:28) and what avails nothing in Hell (77:31, 88:7). The row of 53:28 that reads on into 53:29 is kept as it is.
tree:0r2v7jw06tdpem.relation: Conjecture cannot replace truth; the shade and food of Hell give no relief.

tree:1m6j0bh07wth83.why: 'They are in doubt about it': 11:110 and 41:45 identical about Moses' Book, 42:14 about the heirs of the Book, and 4:157 about killing Jesus.

tree:0mq7yf90e1ju0d.why: 'The meeting of this Day of yours': warned of it (6:130, 39:71, then 'they said') and forgot it (32:14, 45:34).
tree:0mq7yf90e1ju0d.relation: Warned of the Day, they forgot it, and now they are forgotten.

tree:0wlv6170w38mbd.why: 'Thus God makes clear to you the signs, that you may ...': reflect (2:219, 2:266) vs reason (24:61, 57:17 'We have made clear').

tree:0hldxu80yyynma.why: 'He created / subjected for you what is in ...': the earth (2:29, 22:65), the heavens and earth (31:20, 45:13).

tree:1c04ux21k8kvag.why: All four rows stay. 'And there is not for him' in the same words and structure: no partner in dominion (17:111, 25:2), none equal to Him (112:4), and in the inheritance law, if he has no child (4:11). Different subject, same words.
tree:1c04ux21k8kvag.relation: God has no son, partner or equal.

tree:06ppa8r1ymune7.why: 'You will never find for him ...': a helper (4:52), a way (4:88, 4:143), a guiding protector (18:17).

tree:0rymilt08ah1qf.why: 'Whoever is guided is guided for himself, whoever strays ...': four tails (10:108, 17:15, 27:92, 39:41).

tree:1ibe2tf0l25cat.why: 'Satan made their deeds fair-seeming to them': and said none can overcome you (8:48), he is their ally (16:63), and barred them from the way (27:24, 29:38).

tree:07unbp711gvsg1.why: 'A painful punishment for them': We have prepared (4:18, 17:10), tidings to the hypocrites (4:138), He has prepared (76:31).

tree:1jizojt0ecnoip.why: 'We sent you only as ...': a bringer of good news and a warner (17:105, 25:56), a mercy to the worlds (21:107), to all people (34:28).
tree:1jizojt0ecnoip.relation: The Prophet's mission in four descriptions.

tree:1q6bknd0r7vh9l.why: 'The life of this world is only ...': enjoyment of delusion (3:185, 57:20), play and amusement (6:32), a passing enjoyment compared to the Hereafter (13:26).

tree:0gagrlk0izsvoi.why: 'And I am not of ...': the guided (6:56), the polytheists (6:79 Abraham, 12:108 the Prophet), those who pretend (38:86).

tree:166u3ii0dj81jo.why: 'You are not over them a guardian' (6:107, 39:41, 42:6) vs 'a tyrant' (50:45).

tree:0m56cqa13zpnkg.why: 'What was sent down to you from your Lord': believed by some of the People of the Book (3:199), to be upheld (5:68), to be followed (7:3, 39:55 'the best of').

tree:0lcu9q708mnx4b.why: 'What was sent down to you and what was sent down before you': the believers (2:4, 4:162), the hypocrites' claim (4:60), and 5:59.

tree:1sop8bv0xes5a5.why: 'After it had become clear to them': the truth (2:109), that they are people of Hell (9:113), the guidance (47:25, 47:32).
tree:1sop8bv0xes5a5.relation: Turning away after clear knowledge is the gravest kind.

tree:0f28nt500i928l.why: 'Whatever you spend of good / anything': it is for yourselves (2:272), God knows it (2:273, 3:92), it will be repaid to you (8:60).

tree:05wwl6h1gzuh75.why: 'They would not believe': even with angels and the dead speaking (6:111), what they denied before (7:101, 10:74 near-identical), and the destroyed generations (10:13).

tree:1qbr7ap0q1myv3.why: 'What they used to earn did not avail them' (15:84, 39:50, 40:82), and 'what they earned covered their hearts' (83:14).

tree:15z0neh1w0dio7.why: The real pair, 23:6 and 70:30, is already another card (as proposed for tree:08048110029s1n); 16:71 uses 'what their right hands possess' about sharing provision, a different subject.

tree:02uy1bu1i76cui.why: 'I only follow what is revealed to me': four replies to the deniers' demands (6:50, 7:203, 10:15, 46:9).

tree:0bkqc26159e5d8.why: 'Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is ...': the resting place (3:197, 13:18) vs the destination (9:73, 66:9, identical ayat).

tree:138bgjs13f86to.why: 'We saved him and those with him by mercy from Us': Hud (7:72, 11:58), Salih (11:66), Shu'ayb (11:94).

tree:0ipbode07nh12q.why: 'The religion of Abraham, upright': 'and he was not of the polytheists' (3:95, 6:161, 16:123) vs 'and God took Abraham as a friend' (4:125).

tree:1w4lp8e1pqek96.why: The rescue from Pharaoh's people is told three times with one changed verb (We saved, We delivered, He delivered you) and one changed verb for the killing of sons. A classic memorizer set. In 40:28 'from' marks a member of Pharaoh's family (a believing man from them), a different sense and governing word.
tree:1w4lp8e1pqek96.changes: Removed 40:28: 'from' there means 'one of', not rescue from.
tree:1w4lp8e1pqek96.relation: The same blessing recalled three times, to remember the rescue.

check.why: In 40:28 'from the family of Pharaoh' says which family the believing man belongs to. In the rescue rows it means 'saved from'. A different use of the preposition, so removing it is right.

tree:0xq5tsl0jn0wvr.why: 2:212 and 83:29 show the same scene: the deniers mock and laugh at the believers, then the reversal on the Day. In 4:51 'than those who believed' is a comparison, and in 90:17 'of those who believed' means being one of them: different senses of the same particle.
tree:0xq5tsl0jn0wvr.changes: Removed 4:51 and 90:17: there the particle compares or counts in, not the object of mockery.
tree:0xq5tsl0jn0wvr.relation: Mockery of the believers in this life, and the reversal when the Day comes.

tree:0xqzcqm1qzmaho.why: The shared words are a plain preposition phrase in four unrelated settings: Jesus purified from the deniers, a battle at Uhud, the ratio of fighters, and ransom refused on the Last Day. Nothing to compare or ponder.

tree:0mk9err0caajg1.why: Prayers for rescue from the wrongdoing people, in the mouths of Noah, Moses (twice) and Pharaoh's wife. The memorizer sees the same closing with different forms of the verb; the reader sees the believers' recurring plea.
tree:0mk9err0caajg1.relation: The same plea for deliverance from oppressors, said by prophets and by Pharaoh's believing wife.

tree:1p3ybci10mgyms.why: Each ayah names something as coming from God and then closes with different divine names: a bequest (Knowing, Forbearing), a deterrent punishment (Mighty, Wise), an obligation in zakat (Knowing, Wise), and His pleasure (Seeing). Easy to mix the closings when memorizing.
tree:1p3ybci10mgyms.relation: Each ruling ends with names that fit it: forbearance after inheritance shares, might after the punishment for theft.

tree:1gh68uk0bpxt9s.why: The real pair, the disavowal and the proclamation from God and His Messenger (9:1, 9:3), is its own card. Here it is mixed with 2:279 (war from God) and 9:24 (dearer than God and His Messenger, a comparative), so the group adds nothing new.

check.why: Drop is right: I checked that the 9:1 with 9:3 pair is kept in W1 (tree:0kibisj0md83pp), and the other rows add nothing.

tree:1rv70au0lesx6e.why: The name of the Children of Israel joins four unrelated scenes: asking for a king, the curse by David and Jesus, a witness to the Quran, and the disciples. Only the name is shared, not a story or a wording to memorize.

tree:1lqw4z31w0tlgj.why: Before and behind as an image of full protection: angels guarding a person (13:11), falsehood unable to reach the Book (41:42), guards around the Messenger (72:27). 46:21 uses it in time, warners before and after Hud, which a memorizer must still keep apart.
tree:1lqw4z31w0tlgj.relation: God's guarding from every side: of each person, of His Book and of His messengers.

tree:12hpw1t0ylw7bp.why: Three warnings against taking the deniers as allies instead of the believers, each with a different follow-up question, a strong memorizer set. In 33:50 the same words mean 'apart from the believers' (a permission special to the Prophet), a different sense.
tree:12hpw1t0ylw7bp.changes: Removed 33:50: a different sense of the words.
tree:12hpw1t0ylw7bp.relation: Seeking honour or protection with the deniers instead of the believers.

check.why: Removing 33:50 is right: there 'apart from the believers' means 'exclusive to you', a different sense of the phrase.

tree:1n1w7bh01j9bqv.why: Taking other gods besides Him, answered four ways: why no clear proof (18:15), bring your evidence (21:24), they create nothing (25:3), their intercession is worthless (36:23). Same opening, different replies.
tree:1n1w7bh01j9bqv.relation: Four arguments against the same act of taking gods besides God.

tree:1srpfq71c4cdfp.why: The truth from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters, in three places with small differences (with and without the emphatic ending), and 28:86 where the same lead-in ends with a supporter of the deniers. Classic memorizer traps.
tree:1srpfq71c4cdfp.relation: The Prophet is told twice not to doubt and once not to back the deniers, each after a reminder that the revelation is from his Lord.

tree:0ks93060v7ocl2.why: The refrain in As-Saffat closing the stories of Noah, Abraham, Moses with Aaron, and Ilyas. The memorizer must know which story each closes and where it is in the dual.
tree:0ks93060v7ocl2.relation: Each prophet's story ends with the same praise: he was one of Our believing servants.

tree:112vph21vt3no8.why: All four rows stay. Who saves from a painful punishment: answering God's caller (46:31), the trade of faith and striving (61:10), and none can protect the deniers (67:28). 22:25 has the same closing words after another verb ('We will make him taste'). That is arguably a different governing verb, but its row reads on and rows that read on are not removed while that rule is open.
tree:112vph21vt3no8.relation: Contrast: what rescues from the painful punishment, and who is made to taste it.

tree:0zhwxt009tn4p4.why: The deniers have no knowledge of it, they only guess or follow conjecture: about the angels (43:20, 53:28) and about death (45:24), close wording with different endings. In 46:4 the particle after 'knowledge' is conditional ('if you are truthful'), not the negation ('they only'): a different word.
tree:0zhwxt009tn4p4.changes: Removed 46:4: its particle is conditional, not the negation.
tree:0zhwxt009tn4p4.relation: Claims about the unseen without knowledge are only guessing.

tree:1xv1vms197e1zu.why: Seeking God's bounty as earning a living: after the Friday prayer (62:10) and travellers for trade excused from long night prayer (73:20), both with the verb 'seek'. In 12:38 and 57:29 the phrase follows other governing words (that is from God's favour, they have no power over any of it).
tree:1xv1vms197e1zu.changes: Removed 12:38 and 57:29: a different governing word, not 'seek'.
tree:1xv1vms197e1zu.relation: Earning a living is seeking God's bounty, and it sits beside prayer.

check.why: In 12:38 and 57:29, 'of God's bounty' depends on a different construction ('that is of', 'any of'), not on 'seek'. A different construction, so the 62:10 with 73:20 pair is right.

tree:1wd0acw02rwf8q.why: All four rows stay. 'Whoever is in ...' is the same relative and structure in all four: blind here (17:72), in error (19:75, 43:40), and in the cradle (19:29). Different subject, same words.
tree:1wd0acw02rwf8q.relation: Blindness of heart and error: given respite, beyond the Prophet's power to guide.

tree:1othqzn1fn1i6v.why: Judgment scenes in which God brings out from every nation a witness (4:41, 16:84, 28:75) or a troop of deniers (27:83). Same frame with changed verbs and objects.
tree:1othqzn1fn1i6v.relation: Every nation is called to account with its witness on the Last Day.

tree:09uz3970292pc5.why: Plants of every kind brought out of the earth, as a sign of resurrection, with different adjectives (beautiful in 22:5 and 50:7, noble in 26:7). A neat memorizer set.
tree:09uz3970292pc5.relation: The living earth as evidence of revival.

tree:12x0g85057k2qp.why: We have set forth every kind of example in this Quran, four times with changed verb, changed word order and four different endings. A model memorizer card.
tree:12x0g85057k2qp.relation: Every example has been given, yet most people refuse, argue, or reject.

tree:00bsc6r0liglwn.why: From a far place as an image of the deniers' distance: Hell sees them from afar (25:12), faith is out of reach (34:52), they throw guesses from afar (34:53), they are called from afar (41:44). Shared ending with clear meaning.
tree:00bsc6r0liglwn.relation: Distance from the truth in this life becomes distance from salvation in the next.

tree:0l0izvw1loqpxo.why: Created from one soul, with four continuations (He created its mate, a dwelling and a deposit, He made its mate, then He made its mate). A strong memorizer set on one theme.
tree:0l0izvw1loqpxo.relation: The single origin of humanity and of the pair, as a reason for piety and gratitude.

tree:19yzd90144b760.why: Whoever believes in God: his sins removed and gardens (64:9, 65:11, almost identical), his heart guided (64:11). In 9:99 'whoever' is a relative ('among the Bedouins is one who believes'), not the conditional: a different word.
tree:19yzd90144b760.changes: Removed 9:99: its 'whoever' is a relative, not the condition.
tree:19yzd90144b760.relation: What belief in God brings: forgiveness, gardens, a guided heart.

tree:0bce9en1wuai3j.why: God guides, helps and provides for whom He wills, each closing with a fitting pair of names. Short, similar endings a memorizer can mix up.
tree:0bce9en1wuai3j.relation: Each act of God is sealed with the names that fit it: knowledge after guidance, might after victory, strength after provision.

check.why: Keep is right: 'whom He wills, and He is' is followed by different names, an easy slip.

tree:0uzpyl41xx031e.why: Whoever associates partners with God, with four consequences: a great sin (4:48), far astray (4:116), paradise forbidden (5:72), falling from the sky (22:31). 4:48 and 4:116 differ in one ending, a classic trap.
tree:0uzpyl41xx031e.relation: The gravity of shirk shown four ways.

tree:1hj58g91yjl28b.why: Whom God guides is truly guided, then four different endings for whom He leaves astray. Classic mutashabih with spelling and ending differences.
tree:1hj58g91yjl28b.relation: Guidance and misguidance are in God's hand, said four ways.

tree:1eprgp11kwnd2v.why: We know best what they say, listen to, or describe: God reassuring the Prophet about the deniers' words, four times with changed verbs. 20:104 and 50:45 share the same verb, which a memorizer must place.
tree:1eprgp11kwnd2v.relation: God's knowledge of the deniers' words as comfort for the Prophet.

tree:0tazawf0msj71b.why: The declaration and to Him we submit closes Jacob's sons' answer, two creeds of faith in all the prophets (2:136, 3:84, nearly identical) and the call to the People of the Book. The 2:136 and 3:84 pair differs in small words, a classic trap.
tree:0tazawf0msj71b.relation: One religion of submission, confessed by Jacob's sons and by the believers toward the People of the Book.

tree:15uvwx109msk0l.why: No soul is burdened beyond its capacity, said in the third person (2:286) and in the first person three times, each followed by something else: a prayer, fair measure, the people of paradise, the speaking record.
tree:15uvwx109msk0l.relation: God's mercy in the limits of obligation, set beside different duties.

tree:0jr29pm10rk2fs.why: Thus We detail the signs for a people who know, reflect, or reason, each after a different lesson. The memorizer must match the ending to its ayah (7:32 and 9:11 share one ending).
tree:0jr29pm10rk2fs.relation: Each kind of sign is matched to the faculty it calls on: knowledge, reflection, reason.

tree:18mf2e70yuun45.why: This worldly life described as passing: only play (29:64), only enjoyment (40:39), all Pharaoh can rule over (20:72), and what the deniers spend in it (3:117). Same phrase, contrasted with the lasting hereafter.
tree:18mf2e70yuun45.relation: The smallness of this life against the next, said by God, by the believing man, and by Pharaoh's magicians.

tree:1gooldy0qi9zac.why: And He knows best the rightly guided, closing four ayat; 6:117, 16:125 and 68:7 also share the first half with small differences. A strong memorizer set.
tree:1gooldy0qi9zac.relation: Guidance is God's to know and give, said to the Prophet in different situations.

tree:1vy4tsm0z3u07k.why: Your Lord knows best who strays and who is guided, with the variant who is guided in 53:30 and who is God-fearing in 53:32. Fine differences a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:1vy4tsm0z3u07k.relation: Only God knows who is truly guided or pious, so do not claim purity for yourselves.

tree:01773qt0631mt3.why: He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful, closing the repentance of Adam, of the calf worshippers, of the givers of charity and of the three who stayed behind. Two openings to keep apart.
tree:01773qt0631mt3.relation: God's acceptance of repentance across the stories of Adam, Israel, and the companions.

tree:06szqsf1lm9dhh.why: All four rows stay. 'He it is who sent' is the same words and structure in all four. 9:33, 48:28 and 61:9 send His Messenger with guidance and the true religion, with two different endings; 25:48 sends the winds as good news. Different subject, same opening. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:06szqsf1lm9dhh.relation: He sends the Messenger with guidance as He sends the winds before His mercy.

tree:18a7w5e1ncn62m.why: He is the All-Hearing, All-Seeing, after three different openings (indeed He, indeed God, and He). The memorizer must know which form closes which ayah.
tree:18a7w5e1ncn62m.relation: Hearing and seeing set after the Night Journey, true judgment, refuge from the arrogant, and His incomparability.
