tree:02bptq614wyuok.why: Only I had is shared; Satan's speech, the companion in Paradise and the Prophet's knowledge are unrelated.

tree:0gxmrv1101fx6f.why: 2:184 and 2:196 share 'whoever of you is ill', in fasting and in Hajj. In 2:232 'whoever' is a relative (the one among you who believes is admonished), not the condition: a different word.
tree:0gxmrv1101fx6f.changes: Removed 2:232: its 'whoever' is a relative, not a condition.
tree:0gxmrv1101fx6f.relation: Illness eases two acts of worship.

check.why: Removing 2:232 is right: there 'whoever of you' is a relative clause after a verb, not the conditional. The resulting pair is already kept in W1 (tree:1p0u1o00r69j44) and in an A1 book card, so it should be de-duplicated at merge.

tree:05kvn9x0kwd351.why: What our fathers worshipped: Ad's objection (7:70), the peoples to their messengers (14:10), and Quraysh (34:43). Same excuse across nations.
tree:05kvn9x0kwd351.relation: Ancestral custom, the common excuse for rejecting the messengers.

tree:1dbdsll0c3spq7.why: They were stronger than you or them: 9:69, 30:9 and 35:44. Same reminder of past nations, close wording.
tree:1dbdsll0c3spq7.relation: Past nations were stronger and still perished.

tree:1az7j550rqptfz.why: They were wrongdoers, closing the calf story (7:148), Pharaoh's people (8:54), and Lut's town (29:31). A memorizer closing set.
tree:1az7j550rqptfz.relation: Wrongdoing brings destruction, whoever commits it.

tree:1vkp56g153id3u.why: They were criminals, closing 9:66, 11:116 and 44:37. A memorizer closing set.
tree:1vkp56g153id3u.relation: The criminals among hypocrites and past nations meet the same end.

tree:10q0eto1xp1qys.why: What they used to do, closing 5:14, 5:63 and 16:112. A memorizer closing set.
tree:10q0eto1xp1qys.relation: God will inform them of, and repay, what they did.

tree:1hz1xgx0whfe2r.why: What they used to worship, on the Day: the angels asked if they were worshipped (34:40), and the wrongdoers gathered with what they worshipped (37:22).
tree:1hz1xgx0whfe2r.relation: Worshippers and their objects of worship face each other on the Day.

tree:1mcb6v70m0js6f.why: What they were promised: punishment came (26:206), the true promise of Paradise (46:16), and the Day (70:44). The run-on from 70:44 crosses into surah Nuh and adds nothing.
tree:1mcb6v70m0js6f.relation: The promise comes true, as reward or as punishment.

tree:06oxtaw0ygvhho.why: All three rows stay. 'Was prescribed for them' is the same passive verb in all three: fighting prescribed, then they turned away (2:246) or feared people (4:77), and those for whom being killed was decreed (3:154). The trap is one letter: fighting / killing. Same words, different subject.
tree:06oxtaw0ygvhho.relation: Fighting prescribed and death decreed: neither can be fled.

tree:0xep5580853zde.why: Only a book from is shared; the Quran's arrival, a prior decree and the written record of calamities are different sentences.

tree:19ztsyb1to5atd.why: Whoever is given his book in his right hand: 17:71, 69:19 and 84:7, each followed by a different result. A memorizer set.
tree:19ztsyb1to5atd.relation: The joy of receiving one's record in the right hand.

tree:1q34qvj0yct3ir.why: The people of Nuh and Lut denied the messengers (26:105, 26:160), and Lut's people denied the warnings (54:33). Short ayat a memorizer mixes.
tree:1q34qvj0yct3ir.relation: Every people that denied one messenger denied them all.

tree:17yr25o0g2e8lo.why: Those who denied the meeting with God are lost (6:31, 10:45), and the chiefs who denied the meeting of the Hereafter (23:33).
tree:17yr25o0g2e8lo.relation: Denying the meeting with God is the root of loss.

tree:07n60vg0mrbtj4.why: They lied against themselves (6:24), against their Lord (11:18), against God (39:60): the liars exposed on the Day.
tree:07n60vg0mrbtj4.relation: Lying about God is lying against oneself.

tree:0pktrap0uxwpb5.why: Thus We sent it down: an Arabic judgement (13:37), an Arabic Quran (20:113), clear signs (22:16). A memorizer set.
tree:0pktrap0uxwpb5.relation: The Quran as law, as recitation and as clear signs.

tree:1e0fx2y1wun3ue.why: Thus We made for every prophet an enemy: devils of men and jinn (6:112), criminals (25:31), and the great criminals in every town (6:123).
tree:1e0fx2y1wun3ue.relation: Every prophet faces enemies; this is God's way.

tree:1rf4azf1uyp4r7.why: When We removed the punishment from them: Pharaoh's people broke their word (7:135, 43:50), while Yunus's people believed and were spared (10:98).
tree:1rf4azf1uyp4r7.relation: Contrast: relief brought broken promises from Pharaoh's people and lasting faith from Yunus's.

tree:1fzj61g0sf7hds.why: Those who disbelieve in Our signs is a stock phrase; the punishments described (skins, resurrection, the left hand) are separate scenes with no closer wording.

tree:0tec0v31dbfmhf.why: They disbelieved after their faith (3:86, 3:90) or after their Islam (9:74). Close wording on apostasy.
tree:0tec0v31dbfmhf.relation: Disbelief after faith, and the door of repentance left open in 9:74.

tree:1tk0vop1cmci25.why: Only much of what is shared; the Messenger revealing hidden scripture, Shuayb's people not understanding and the limbs testifying are unrelated.

tree:0nrbqnd1j5edu9.why: They disbelieved in it: the People of the Book when the Book they knew came (2:89), Quraysh after wishing for a reminder (37:167-170), and those who disbelieved in it before, on the Day (34:53). Same words and structure in all three. 37:170 alone is only the phrase, so the wish before it is added.
tree:0nrbqnd1j5edu9.changes: 34:53 stays: same words, different scene. 37:167-169 are added before 37:170 so the wish is visible.
tree:0nrbqnd1j5edu9.relation: Longing for a Book, then denying it when it comes.

tree:0cq8dwd02m5eot.why: Your Lord suffices: as aware of His servants' sins (17:17), as guardian (17:65), as guide and helper (25:31). A memorizer set.
tree:0cq8dwd02m5eot.relation: God is enough as witness, guardian and helper.

tree:1jey7nz1qm3g8b.why: Enough is it: as a clear sin (4:50), He is enough as aware of sins (25:58), as witness between me and you (46:8). A memorizer set.
tree:1jey7nz1qm3g8b.relation: God's knowledge and witness are enough.

tree:1pm7e8f0xrjir3.why: 6:25 and 7:146 share: if they see every sign they will not believe in it; 10:97 adds even if every sign came to them. One theme in close wording.
tree:1pm7e8f0xrjir3.relation: Signs do not convince the stubborn.

tree:107iptj0j700ht.why: Every matter: decided wisely on the blessed night (44:4), settled (54:3), and the angels descend with every matter on the Night of Decree (97:4).
tree:107iptj0j700ht.relation: Every matter is decreed and settled by God.

tree:0hzl99v1jaqs6x.why: 70:38 and 74:52 share: does every one of them hope or want...? 52:21 says every person is pledged to what he earned.
tree:0hzl99v1jaqs6x.relation: The deniers hope for Paradise and scrolls, but each is held by his own deeds.

tree:1lj5n770kqdx8l.why: All three rows stay. 'Every people' is the same rare phrase in all three: each people knew its drinking place (2:60, 7:160), and on the Day We call every people by their leader (17:71). Same words, different subject.
tree:1lj5n770kqdx8l.relation: Each people has its share now and its record then.

tree:1j8vsbg04kdods.why: Every creature spread on earth: among the signs (2:164, 31:10), and created from water (24:45). A memorizer set.
tree:1j8vsbg04kdods.relation: The variety of creatures is a sign of the Creator.

tree:0rry4pq1bc2n4a.why: Every possessor of is shared in three different senses: claws, merit and knowledge.

tree:0nbqfju146376w.why: Every devil: rejected (15:17), rebellious (22:3, 37:7). Short phrase a memorizer mixes, with the sky guarded from them.
tree:0nbqfju146376w.relation: Guarded from devils, yet some people follow them.

tree:0wfcrz115sjhwt.why: All three rows stay. 'Each in ...' is the same words and structure: each swims in an orbit (21:33, 36:40), and each is in a clear record (11:6). Same words, different subject. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:0wfcrz115sjhwt.relation: Order in creation: each body in its orbit, each creature in the record.

tree:0chrqtz0wxkaet.why: All are devoutly obedient to Him (2:116, 30:26), and the birds all turn to Him with Dawud (38:19). Close wording on submission.
tree:0chrqtz0wxkaet.relation: All creation, heavens, earth and birds, submits to God.

tree:1tgpt9c0gg4k2u.why: Whenever or all that is shared in three unrelated sentences.

tree:0qqcb2s1p01q22.why: By no means! It is: a word he says (23:100), a blazing fire (70:15), a reminder (80:11). Short ayat a memorizer mixes.
tree:0qqcb2s1p01q22.relation: No second chance for the dead, fire for the guilty, a reminder for the living.

tree:0tzhyd61kkexdu.why: The owner already dropped the pair 2:75 and 9:6: hearing God's word is a rare phrase but the subjects differ. 48:15 does not change that.

tree:0z2ipya1hynqly.why: How many is shared in three unrelated sentences: a small army, destroyed towns and angels.

tree:0r0b9ds06jx720.why: And be among the grateful (7:144, 39:66) or among those who prostrate (15:98). A memorizer set of commands to Musa and the Prophet.
tree:0r0b9ds06jx720.relation: Gratitude and prostration as the right response to God's gifts.

tree:0nw3qc20e86efk.why: We were doers, three times in al-Anbiya (21:17, 21:79, 21:104) with different lead-ins. A memorizer set in one surah.
tree:0nw3qc20e86efk.relation: God does what He wills: creation, favours to prophets, and resurrection.

tree:19i9vbh1q43msz.why: All three rows stay. 'We are we ...' is the same structure (the verb with the emphatic pronoun and a plural noun): if we are the victors (7:113, 26:41), and We were the inheritors (28:58). Same words, different subject. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:19i9vbh1q43msz.relation: The magicians wanted to be the victors; God is the inheritor of all.

tree:0z6i9bw0o0vkp0.why: Other than what we used to do: the deniers on the Day (7:53) and in Hell (35:37) ask to go back and act differently; at death they deny doing any evil (16:28).
tree:0z6i9bw0o0vkp0.relation: Too late, the deniers wish they had acted differently.

tree:0kofqn40hdl3he.why: Taste the punishment for what you earned: 7:39, 10:52, 39:24. A memorizer closing set.
tree:0kofqn40hdl3he.relation: The punishment is the fruit of their own deeds.

tree:01b2xol0huj7rp.why: What you were promised: this is your Day (21:103) and the Paradise (41:30) for believers, and this is Hell for the deniers (36:63).
tree:01b2xol0huj7rp.relation: Contrast: the same words announce Paradise or Hell.

tree:1mokikb1rodyvn.why: You were on is shared in three unrelated sentences: travelling, the brink of fire, turning on your heels.

tree:18713b71y5n3t5.why: All three rows stay. 'You are ill' is the same words in all three: the dry ablution ruling, if you are ill or on a journey (4:43, 5:6), and the prayer of fear, if you are ill you may lay down your arms (4:102). Same words, different ruling.
tree:18713b71y5n3t5.relation: Illness lightens both purification and the burden of arms.

tree:03gwucv1t6mkk7.why: As He wills: He shapes you in the womb (3:6), He spends (5:64), He spreads the clouds (30:48). God acts freely in creation and provision.
tree:03gwucv1t6mkk7.relation: God shapes, gives and sends rain as He wills.

check.why: Keep is right: 'as He wills' carries God's free action in all three.

tree:0lafuw4103zxui.why: I associate none with Him: 13:36, 18:38 and 72:20 with small differences. A memorizer set.
tree:0lafuw4103zxui.relation: The believer's pure declaration of tawhid.

tree:1d7oixl114pu8h.why: I do not worship: what you worship besides God (10:104, 109:2), and why should I not worship the One who created me (36:22).
tree:1d7oixl114pu8h.relation: Rejecting false worship and turning to the Creator.

tree:196y4mt1vt4yo3.why: I do not know the unseen: the Prophet (6:50) and Nuh (11:31), and Isa: I do not know what is in Your self (5:116).
tree:196y4mt1vt4yo3.relation: Prophets disclaim knowledge of the unseen.

tree:15wzoar0ucl86t.why: All three rows stay. 'I do not say' is the same words: I do not say to you I have God's treasures (6:50, 11:31), and Moses: I say nothing about God but the truth (7:105). Same words, different subject.
tree:15wzoar0ucl86t.relation: What messengers say and do not say: no claim to treasure, nothing about God but truth.

tree:0fqll8l0n412uv.why: Your wealth and your children: they do not bring you near to God (34:37), will not help you on the Day (60:3), must not distract you from His remembrance (63:9).
tree:0fqll8l0n412uv.relation: Wealth and children are no substitute for faith and deeds.

tree:0xkqh4f0mxg4e1.why: 2:254 and 14:31 warn of a day with no trade and no friendship, differing in one word; 24:37 praises men whom trade does not distract from remembrance.
tree:0xkqh4f0mxg4e1.relation: Those not distracted by trade now are ready for the day when there is no trade.

tree:0ym3pgv0qqkwu1.why: You do not see: the fire in front of them (52:15), death's nearness (56:85), what you do not see (69:39). A memorizer closing set.
tree:0ym3pgv0qqkwu1.relation: Beyond what people see lie death, fire and the unseen.

tree:1s1we7b03vdjsx.why: Our Lord, do not place us: with the wrongdoers (7:47), as a trial for the wrongdoers (10:85) or for the disbelievers (60:5). A memorizer set of prayers.
tree:1s1we7b03vdjsx.relation: Believers ask not to share the wrongdoers' fate nor become a trial for them.

tree:1nokqqq1nsk436.why: Do not enter: by one gate (12:67), houses not your own without permission (24:27), the Prophet's houses uninvited (33:53). Same prohibition in close wording.
tree:1nokqqq1nsk436.relation: Manners of entering, from Yaqub's caution to the etiquette of houses.

tree:1qbt3c91soj2ah.why: Do not call on another god with God (26:213, 28:88), or on what neither helps nor harms besides God (10:106). A memorizer set.
tree:1qbt3c91soj2ah.relation: Calling on anything besides God is wrongdoing and leads to punishment.

tree:12kcpk41n3o1x0.why: Do not sell My signs (2:41, 5:44) or God's covenant (16:95) for a small price. A memorizer set.
tree:12kcpk41n3o1x0.relation: God's word and covenant are not to be traded for worldly gain.

tree:1aqyow60h8rpfq.why: You do not perceive: the martyrs are alive (2:154), punishment comes suddenly (39:55), your deeds may be voided (49:2). A memorizer closing set.

tree:1pmvbjf1jmz9r7.why: Make no excuses: to the mocking hypocrites (9:66), to those who stayed behind (9:94), to the disbelievers on the Day (66:7).
tree:1pmvbjf1jmz9r7.relation: Excuses are refused when the deed is plain or the Day has come.

tree:1p4pfl31nhq297.why: Then you will not be helped (11:113, 39:54) and you will not be helped by Us (23:65). A memorizer closing set.
tree:1p4pfl31nhq297.relation: No help against God for those who lean on wrongdoers or delay repentance.

tree:0vro72a0di302k.why: Plot against me and give me no respite: the Prophet (7:195), Nuh (10:71), Hud (11:55). Prophets challenge their people in the same words.
tree:0vro72a0di302k.relation: The prophets' trust in God against all their people's plots.

tree:05xdail0e3uqjh.why: Do not weaken: nor grieve, you are superior (3:139); in pursuing the enemy (4:104); and call for peace (47:35). A memorizer set.

tree:0cowr5p0g1bbhp.why: Let not hatred of a people lead you (5:2, 5:8), and let not opposition to me lead you (Shuayb, 11:89). Same construction, a memorizer set.

tree:0urpwhu0aq1y6w.why: What does not hear: the herd that hears only noise (2:171), idols (19:42), the deaf (21:45).

tree:1eb6viv09bcw7v.why: Rabbana ma in four unrelated contexts (creation, denial, the companion, the jinn).

tree:1qqhct60r3ilcs.why: 'Why was no sign sent down to him from his Lord? Say: ...' with three answers (6:37, 13:27, 29:50). In 39:9 'his Lord' follows 'the mercy of', and 'say' opens another question, a different structure.
tree:1qqhct60r3ilcs.relation: The same demand for a sign, answered three ways.

tree:1cuk51j1d54eb5.why: Kafaru rabbahum ala bu'dan li-Ad in 11:60 vs li-Thamud in 11:68, plus 11:18 and 41:54.

tree:0ue3xvq0qmh4ic.why: 6:4 and 36:46 are the same ayah: no sign of their Lord comes to them but they turn away from it. In 18:55 and 35:39 'their Lord, except' follows other words (ask forgiveness of their Lord / with their Lord), a different structure.
tree:0ue3xvq0qmh4ic.changes: Removed 18:55 and 35:39: a different structure. The rows that read on are kept.
tree:0ue3xvq0qmh4ic.relation: Every sign is met with turning away.

tree:1xtt7wg0gtlbg4.why: Lakini alladhina ittaqaw rabbahum lahum jannatun in 3:198 vs ghurafun in 39:20, plus rabbihim lahum in 45:11 and 57:19.

tree:0n8d9pp0lfpbtx.why: Rabbi a'lamu bi-man ja'a bil-huda in 28:37 vs a'lamu man ja'a in 28:85, plus 18:22 and 26:188.

tree:033vqbu14redqs.why: Rahmata Allahi is a stock phrase in four unrelated contexts.

tree:1dvfw151ok3zqh.why: Rahmatan minna with different continuations: wa kana amran, wa mata'an, wa dhikra, min ba'di darra'.

tree:1gwsvuh0v981nt.why: Rizqan hasanan twice in al-Nahl (16:67, 16:75), plus 11:88 and 22:58.

tree:1aymim71waven7.why: Consolation: kudhdhiba rusulun min qablika in 3:184, 6:34 and 35:4, plus ja'akum rusulun min qabli in 3:183.

tree:16ggczl1w7y8nj.why: 'Obey God and His Messenger, and do not' turn away (8:20) / dispute (8:46), in the same surah. In 9:16 'nor His Messenger nor the believers' and in 9:29 'what God and His Messenger forbade, and they do not' the words have a different structure.
tree:16ggczl1w7y8nj.relation: Obedience and unity, with the warnings that go with them.

check.why: Removing 9:16 and 9:29 is right: the shared words are a different structure there.

tree:1259mu71eu3ya1.why: La yasta'khiruna sa'atan wa la yastaqdimun with la in 7:34 and 16:61 vs fa-la in 10:49, and la tasta'khiruna in 34:30.

tree:1xapfcx0k7omib.why: Subhana alladhi: asra, khalaqa al-azwaja, fa-subhana alladhi biyadihi, sakhkhara lana.

tree:1fr1tv2060s6ma.why: Sab'a samawatin: wa huwa in 2:29, wa min al-ardi in 65:12, tibaqan in 67:3 and 71:15.

tree:1gj6c9x0cnwt8f.why: Sirran wa alaniyatan with four continuations: fa-lahum, wa yadra'una, min qabli, yarjuna.

tree:10fslw91rv6nln.why: Arsalna Musa bi-ayatina wa sultanin mubin in 11:96, 23:45 and 40:23, then ila Fir'awn; 37:156 sultanun mubin.

tree:19x2r281llpt84.why: Sami'na wa ata'na: ghufranaka in 2:285, wa ittaqu in 5:7, wa ula'ika in 24:51, vs sami'na wa asayna in 4:46.

tree:0fpedfo0b6gyeo.why: Sharrun makanan wa adallu in 5:60 and 25:34 vs wa Allahu a'lamu in 12:77 and wa ad'afu jundan in 19:75.

tree:1mcq07k0bjairw.why: Shuraka'iya alladhina kuntum taz'umun in 28:62 and 28:74 vs tushaqquna in 16:27 and za'amtum in 18:52.

tree:1lwn2th0uhzzpr.why: La-fi shakkin mimma tad'una ilayhi murib in 11:62 vs 14:9, plus fi shakkin mimma in 10:94 and 40:34.

tree:12c5dks1iv1dey.why: Shay'in hatta is glue across four unrelated contexts.

tree:0naq7np1rkfxe3.why: Wasi'a rabbi kulla shay'in ilman in 6:80 vs rabbuna in 7:89, plus 20:98 and 65:12.

tree:1hkp34l1wbvkvv.why: Nothing is hidden from God in the earth or the heaven (3:5, 14:38), nothing can frustrate Him in the heavens or the earth (35:44, order reversed). In 8:60 'whatever you spend of anything in God's way' has a conditional 'what' and another sense of 'in'.
tree:1hkp34l1wbvkvv.changes: Removed 8:60: a different structure. The rows that read on are kept.
tree:1hkp34l1wbvkvv.relation: Nothing in heaven or earth escapes God.

tree:0oeudyz1k9glbl.why: All four rows stay. 'Anything, while they ...' is the same structure in all four: a negation with 'anything', then 'while they' and a present verb. Idols create nothing while they are created (7:191, 16:20, 25:3), and 'the Jews are on nothing, while they recite the Book' (2:113). Same words, different subject. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:0oeudyz1k9glbl.relation: Idols create nothing; communities dismiss each other though they read the same Book.

tree:01w76c41mpae26.why: Closing siratan mustaqiman: wa la-hadaynahum, yahdihim ilayhi, yahdiyaka, yahdiyakum.

tree:0z5o9f01szerzi.why: Al-Nisa' endings dalalan ba'idan: an yudillahum, fa-qad dalla twice, qad dallu.

tree:1080w6a0n9qmoa.why: Taba'a Allahu alayha in 4:155 vs ala qulubihim in 9:93, 16:108 and 47:16, with different continuations.

tree:1lnwjq70mvcn6n.why: Wa idha tallaqtumu al-nisa'a fa-balaghna ajalahunna in 2:231 vs 2:232, plus in tallaqtum in 2:236 and 65:1.

tree:18j6nvk1ax0ojc.why: Closing adhabi al-sa'ir after ila (22:4, 31:21), min (34:12), lahum (67:5).

tree:0xv04w10eyjcb3.why: Adhaba jahannama: inna adhabaha, khalidun, wa bi'sa al-masir, wa lahum adhabu al-hariq.

tree:0wjxzfz1wc9fup.why: Closing adhabin ghaliz after min (11:58, 41:50), wa min wara'ihi (14:17), ila (31:24).

tree:17r07o31e0muaf.why: Closing adhaban muhinan: wa a'tadna lil-kafirina in 4:37 and 4:151, inna Allaha a'adda in 4:102, wa a'adda lahum in 33:57.

tree:0vhs6rg0vq9gdm.why: Afa Allahu anhum, amma salaf, anha, anka: four forgiveness clauses, two ending ghafurun halim.

tree:1oucj1h1mmt1dz.why: Allamu al-ghuyub: innaka anta in 5:109 and 5:116, wa anna Allaha in 9:78, yaqdhifu bil-haqqi in 34:48.

tree:10sf7ln1m1cucf.why: Ala al-ard is a generic phrase in four unrelated contexts.

tree:0juw91s07k5my8.why: Revelation on a man from among them: dhikrun min rabbikum ala rajulin minkum in 7:63 vs 7:69, plus the disbelievers' ala rajulin in 34:7 and 43:31.

tree:17k06gw19j6nz6.why: Paradise couches ala sururin: mutaqabilin in 15:47 and 37:44, masfufatin in 52:20, mawdunatin in 56:15.

tree:16f4stz0ampfx7.why: 'He does not urge the feeding of the poor' (69:34, 107:3) and 'you do not urge one another' (89:18). In 2:61 'we cannot endure one kind of food' has another governing verb and sense.
tree:16f4stz0ampfx7.changes: Removed 2:61: a different governing verb. The rows that read on are kept.
tree:16f4stz0ampfx7.relation: Neglecting the poor marks the denier.

tree:1y37y8t1b7olt9.why: 'Thus God / We seal the hearts of' the deniers (7:101), the transgressors (10:74), those who do not know (30:59). In 47:24 'or are there locks upon hearts' is a different structure.

check.why: Removing 47:24 is right: there 'or upon hearts are their locks' is a different structure.

tree:1um4l4f1n4dpkl.why: 'He came out to his people': Zechariah from the sanctuary (19:11), Qarun in his finery (28:79). In 6:83 ('against his people') and 36:28 ('We sent down upon his people') the preposition has another sense and verb.
tree:1um4l4f1n4dpkl.changes: Removed 6:83 and 36:28: different governing verbs and sense.
tree:1um4l4f1n4dpkl.relation: Contrast: a prophet comes out with worship, a rich man with show.

check.why: Removing 6:83 and 36:28 is right: 'upon his people' follows different verbs there.

tree:0jr9j180g2pubk.why: Wa lamma dakhalu ala Yusufa awa ilayhi akhahu in 12:69 vs abawayhi in 12:99, plus 12:11 and 12:84.

tree:0lljtln18tweq5.why: Alaykum fi is particle glue; the fi al-kitab pair has its own card.

tree:0y1myee0io1uck.why: Ma alfayna (2:170) vs ma wajadna (5:104, 31:21) alayhi aba'ana, and 10:78 an ma wajadna.

tree:1x8tiu71yjxzt1.why: All four rows stay. 'For it a wage' is the same words and sense: I ask you no wage for it (6:90, 11:51, 42:23), and Moses to Khidr: you could have taken a wage for it (18:77). Same words, different subject. The row that reads on stays as it is.
tree:1x8tiu71yjxzt1.relation: Messengers take no wage; Khidr too worked for none.

tree:0mb3k4z0i0qfhj.why: The as-Saffat refrain 'We left for him among later generations' (37:78, 37:108, 37:129), each followed by a different 'peace be upon'. In 13:17 'what they heat in the fire' is a different structure.
tree:0mb3k4z0i0qfhj.changes: Removed 13:17: a different structure. The rows that read on are kept.
tree:0mb3k4z0i0qfhj.relation: Each prophet left a good name and a greeting of peace.

tree:0ol1lno037dnco.why: Fa-inna ma yadillu alayha wa ma ana alaykum bi-hafiz or anta bi-wakil, and wa ma rabbuka in 41:46.

tree:1c8puru0ljooes.why: Alayhim inna is glue; the yatuba alayhim pair has its own card, and 9:103 and 29:51 are a different structure.

tree:0xhxfj91n72dqp.why: Amma kanu ya'malun in 2:134, 2:141 and 15:93 vs amma kanu yaftarun in 29:13.

tree:0ccmzrd00bw4hz.why: La yanhakum vs innama yanhakum Allahu an alladhina in 60:8 and 60:9, plus 4:107 and 22:38, both ending la yuhibbu khawwanan.

check.why: Keep is acceptable. It holds two pairs (60:8 with 60:9, and 4:107 with 22:38), so a split into those two cards would read better.

tree:0ohp8sa1x0vp8u.why: An al-yamini wa an al-shimali in 50:17 and 70:37 vs wa al-shama'il in 16:48, plus 37:28.

tree:0z20odr0u3sqqz.why: Defying the command: atau an amri rabbihim (7:77, 51:44), fasaqa an amri rabbihi (18:50), atat an amri rabbiha (65:8).

tree:15kpnvc0sejmje.why: Inda rabbihi in four unrelated contexts; a stock phrase.

tree:0ou7rkh0lbn2wr.why: Indahu ilmu al-kitab in 13:43 vs ilmun min al-kitab in 27:40, and indahu ilmu al-sa'a in 31:34 and 43:85.

tree:0xh1l8313v2non.why: Nukaffir (or yukaffir) ankum sayyi'atikum with wa nudkhilkum or wa yaghfir lakum continuations.

tree:0xfn4ti1tz0x5k.why: Wa ghadiba Allahu alayhi wa la'anahu in 4:93 vs alayhim in 48:6, and qawman ghadiba Allahu alayhim in 58:14 and 60:13.

tree:0bt1dby16l78dy.why: Ajrun ghayru mamnun: lahum in 41:8 and 84:25, fa-lahum in 95:6, la-ajran in 68:3. The 84:25 run-on crosses into surah 85.

tree:104t2ga0dq7skg.why: Idhhab ila Fir'awna innahu tagha in 20:24 and 79:17 vs idhhaba in 20:43, plus 44:31.

tree:0xw3c031davkah.why: Fir'awn wa Haman: wa junudahuma in 28:6 and 28:8, with Qarun in 29:39 and 40:24 in a different order.

tree:0r47j400fibn52.why: Fariqan min is glue across unrelated contexts; the fariqan min al-mu'minin pair (8:5, 34:20) has its own card.

check.why: Drop is right: I checked that the 8:5 with 34:20 pair is kept in W1 (tree:1twlexf1cj8pd3), and the rest is glue.

tree:0lqwt7s1w9dr48.why: Fashiltum wa tanaza'tum fi al-amr in 3:152 vs la-fashiltum wa la-tanaza'tum in 8:43, plus 3:159 and 22:67.

tree:0arrar00na0rja.why: Yusari'una fi al-khayrat: wa ula'ika, wa yad'unana, wa hum laha sabiqun, and nusari'u lahum in 23:56.

tree:1hyf1n319k3wc9.why: All four rows stay. 'In yourselves' is the same words and sense in all four: what you conceal in yourselves (2:235), what is in yourselves God will reckon (2:284), signs in yourselves (51:21), and no affliction in yourselves but it is written (57:22). Same words, different subject.
tree:1hyf1n319k3wc9.relation: Within yourselves: hidden intentions God reckons, signs to see, and trials already written.

tree:1kbc6t003oam5m.why: 2:164 and 3:190 open the same way and a memorizer must keep apart the long list in 2:164 from the short one in 3:190. 3:191 and 67:3 carry the same call to look into creation.
tree:1kbc6t003oam5m.relation: Creation as a sign: listed, then reflected on by the people of understanding, then shown to have no flaw.

tree:0qqlksl0bmc77f.why: All four rows stay. 'In that' is the same words and structure (a fronted 'in that' with its noun) in all four: in that was a great trial from your Lord, after the rescue from Pharaoh (2:49, 7:141, 14:6, with one verb differing each time), and in that are signs for people who believe (6:99). Same words, different subject. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:0qqlksl0bmc77f.relation: In God's acts there is both a trial and a sign.

tree:1khadwg043i6ja.why: All four rows stay. 'In your breasts' is the same words and sense: what is in your breasts God knows and tests (3:29, 3:154), something great in your breasts (17:51), a need in your breasts (40:80). Same words, different subject.
tree:1khadwg043i6ja.relation: What lies in the breast: secrets God knows, and needs He meets.

tree:19pkro31ojd2l7.why: All four are about heedlessness before the Hour: two describe people heedless now, two have them confess on the Day that they were heedless.
tree:19pkro31ojd2l7.relation: Heedless in this life, then the confession on the Day when the cover is lifted.

tree:1rpenay0pme6zk.why: All four are about the benefits God put in cattle; a memorizer must tell apart how each one continues.
tree:1rpenay0pme6zk.relation: The favour of cattle, each time joined to a different lesson: the sacrifice, the drink, thanks, and travel.

tree:01dqdc919ilz8p.why: Only a speech opener with a conditional is shared; the speakers and subjects are unrelated (Pharaoh, Noah, Moses, a denier).

tree:0qxg2j51b5c9qf.why: 15:57 and 51:31 are Ibrahim's identical question to the angels, and 20:95 is Moses asking the Samiri in the same form; 20:51 is Pharaoh's question in the same surah. Useful for a memorizer keeping these questions apart.

tree:1jhhjif0mcvgnz.why: A set of the sayings the Quran reports from the Jews, each answered; worth seeing together.
tree:1jhhjif0mcvgnz.relation: The claims of the People of the Book, one after another, and how each is refuted.

tree:1bph3e91gpmirj.why: Four women addressing their Lord: the mother of Maryam, Maryam, the Queen of Sheba and the wife of Pharaoh.
tree:1bph3e91gpmirj.relation: Women's prayers in the Quran: a vow, wonder at a promise, repentance, and a plea for a house in Paradise.

tree:0ajr3em06590bs.why: The deniers' question about being raised after turning to bones and dust, repeated with small differences a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:0ajr3em06590bs.relation: The same denial of resurrection and the answers given to it.

tree:089wtfu0cz7nm8.why: Peoples answering their prophets with the same question (Hud twice, Moses and Ibrahim); 7:70 and 46:22 even end the same way.
tree:089wtfu0cz7nm8.relation: Different prophets, the same rejection: you came to turn us from what our fathers worshipped.

tree:1pow2rw1uuiwte.why: All four rows stay. 'They said: peace' is the same words in all four: the angels greeting Abraham, each time with a different reply (11:69, 15:52, 51:25), and the servants of the Merciful answering the ignorant (25:63). Same words, different scene. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:1pow2rw1uuiwte.relation: Peace as a greeting from angels and as the believers' answer to ignorance.

tree:1vin96l098p9hb.why: 26:116 and 26:167 are the threats to Noah and to Lot in the same mould; 7:149 and 12:14 share the opening and the losers ending. Good for a memorizer.

tree:0nf8oxt02h8jdt.why: The cry of woe of those who see the punishment or the resurrection, each followed by a different confession.
tree:0nf8oxt02h8jdt.relation: Confessions at the moment of truth: we were wrongdoers, we were transgressors, this is the Day of Judgement.

tree:1cex98g1ctkpgq.why: Only a time phrase is shared; the subjects are unrelated (news of the unseen, Salih's people, Maryam in labour, a challenge to idolaters).

tree:1v7h4ty1dlundw.why: What true success is: the believers, the one who purifies himself, while Pharaoh's magicians claim success goes to whoever dominates today.
tree:1v7h4ty1dlundw.relation: Contrast: the magicians' worldly idea of success against the success of purification and faith.

tree:0s22xu312yui61.why: 6:31 and 10:45 are the same sentence about those who deny meeting God; 6:140 and 4:119 name others who lost. Useful for a memorizer.
tree:0s22xu312yui61.relation: Who the losers are: deniers of the meeting with God, killers of their children, followers of Satan.

tree:0c9x5a20ji88ky.why: A common phrase about going astray, said of different groups in unrelated contexts; nothing to learn from the grouping.

tree:1k11fsb18arc3h.why: The Quran described as an Arabic Quran, each time with a different purpose; 20:113 and 42:7 open the same way, which a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:1k11fsb18arc3h.relation: Why the Quran came in Arabic: so they may be mindful, so people who know understand, to warn the mother of towns.

tree:1q5lh4v1sv9kyb.why: Towns God destroyed, each mention adding something: the sudden punishment, their not believing, their not returning, their ruins.
tree:1q5lh4v1sv9kyb.relation: The destroyed towns as a lesson, seen from four sides.

tree:0ftuney0pnblw8.why: 17:56 and 34:22 are the same challenge to call on the false gods; 7:195 is the same challenge. 17:110, in the same surah, tells them to call on God by His names.
tree:0ftuney0pnblw8.relation: Contrast: call on the false gods and see they own nothing; call on God by any of His beautiful names.

tree:11v5dir1cu3mb9.why: The challenge to bring a scripture: the Torah, one surah, ten surahs, a better book. A memorizer must keep the amounts apart.
tree:11v5dir1cu3mb9.relation: The graded challenge to the deniers of the revelation.

tree:14h6goy0e0aul0.why: All four rows stay. 'Say: never' is the same words and structure: you will never go out with me (9:83), you will never follow us (48:15), nothing will befall us but what God wrote (9:51), fleeing will never benefit you (33:16). Same words, different subject.
tree:14h6goy0e0aul0.relation: The replies to those who stay behind and those who fear: nothing comes but what God wrote.

tree:0v0mdjg12ep2sa.why: Only the end of one clause and the start of a closing are shared; the subjects (regret of the hypocrites, the mosque of harm, Moses' people) are unrelated.

tree:1i5c7od0b2gtpl.why: Each ayah commands decent, proper speech in a delicate setting: to a woman in her waiting period, to those unable to manage wealth, to relatives at the division of an estate, and by the Prophet's wives to men. 4:5 and 4:8 end the same way, a trap for memorizers.
tree:1i5c7od0b2gtpl.relation: Proper speech as a duty wherever money, marriage or modesty is at stake.

tree:05f7yv50uhb46d.why: 7:109 and 7:127 open the same way in one surah; 26:11 and 44:17 name the same people as the ones Moses was sent to.
tree:05f7yv50uhb46d.relation: Pharaoh's people: their chiefs' accusation and plotting, and God's sending Moses to them as a trial.

tree:189ctge1xbns5m.why: Only a phrase about the prophet's people is shared; the subjects are unrelated (unseen news, Moses' mission, the calf, Noah's mission).

tree:0umiy9c1vupsyy.why: Two different words share 'his people, what'. As a negation: the chiefs of Noah's people, 'we see you only as a man like us' (11:27, 23:24). As a question: Abraham to his father and people, 'what are these statues / what do you worship' (21:52, 26:70). Each pair is a clean memorizer card.
tree:0umiy9c1vupsyy.changes: Split by the word: the negation (11:27, 23:24) and the question (21:52, 26:70).
tree:0umiy9c1vupsyy.relation: The chiefs dismiss the messenger; Abraham questions the idols.

tree:0ceo6v11uxxgfd.why: All four rows stay. 'He is possessed of' is the same words and structure in all four: even if he is a relative, in testimony (5:106), justice (6:152) and burden (35:18), and because he is possessed of wealth and sons (68:14). Same words, different subject.
tree:0ceo6v11uxxgfd.relation: Neither kinship nor wealth changes what is right.

tree:1nfuua60nst24i.why: All four rows stay. 'It was for us' is the same words: not for us to associate (12:38), not for us to bring authority (14:11), we had no authority over you (37:30), and the hypocrites' 'if we had any say in the matter' (3:154), which has the same shape as 37:30. Same words, different subject.
tree:1nfuua60nst24i.relation: What is and is not in human hands.

tree:1h47p280pvz9c8.why: Hope in meeting God as the motive for action; 33:21 and 60:6 are near-identical lines about a good example (the Prophet, then Ibrahim), a memorizer trap.
tree:1h47p280pvz9c8.relation: Who hopes for God and the Last Day has a model to follow and deeds to do.

tree:1mu3l7t0je5b43.why: Only a stock closing about what people used to do is shared; the subjects are unrelated (the Children of Israel, sects, Noah's people, the disbelievers' reward).

tree:0yj07el0imtyxt.why: The Quran described as a blessed Book God sent down, each time with a different purpose; 6:92 and 6:155 in one surah open the same way.
tree:0yj07el0imtyxt.relation: The blessed Book: to confirm what came before, to be followed, to bring people to light, to be pondered.

tree:1jd27ea0fmcuuk.why: Thamud's denial, told in four short openings that differ in what they denied; easy to mix up.
tree:1jd27ea0fmcuuk.relation: The same denial seen four ways: the messengers, the warnings, the Hour, out of their arrogance.

tree:115vnec0tc35mw.why: A common phrase for denying the signs, said of unrelated subjects (Pharaoh's people, a warning to the Prophet, the evildoers' end, those given the Torah).

tree:0r12ejn1j7b3a3.why: Each ayah says evil deeds were made to seem fair to someone: the disbelievers, the idolaters killing their children, the wasteful, Pharaoh.
tree:0r12ejn1j7b3a3.relation: How falsehood is made attractive to those who follow it.

tree:0q20doo033nebw.why: All four rows stay. 'Disbelieved in God' is the same words in all four: three times the reason for the hypocrites' rejection, with small differences (9:54, 9:80, 9:84), and those who believed in falsehood and disbelieved in God are the losers (29:52). Same words, different subject.
tree:0q20doo033nebw.relation: Disbelief in God as the root of the hypocrites' fate and of all loss.

tree:0a4c48017985ms.why: What is said of those who disbelieve in their Lord: they set up equals, they wear chains, their deeds are ashes, they have Hell. The phrase is distinctive and the four continuations are easy to confuse.
tree:0a4c48017985ms.relation: The state and end of those who disbelieve in their Lord.

tree:16pfaou030wjvs.why: All four rows stay. 'No indeed! Indeed ...' opens all four in the same words: the record of the wicked and of the righteous (83:7, 83:18, a matched pair), Moses: with me is my Lord (26:62), and man transgresses (96:6). Same words, different subject; the grouping rests on a short opening.
tree:16pfaou030wjvs.relation: The same sharp 'no indeed' answers despair (Moses), arrogance (man), and sets the two records apart.

tree:0zvdo6o00gcsbi.why: 'Eat of it' leads two unrelated things: the Children of Israel entering the town (2:58, 7:161, a classic memorizer pair), and eating of the sacrificial animals in Hajj (22:28, 22:36). Two clean pairs, so the split is fair.
tree:0zvdo6o00gcsbi.changes: Split: the town (2:58, 7:161) and the sacrifice (22:28, 22:36).
tree:0zvdo6o00gcsbi.relation: Eat and give thanks: in the town given to Israel, and from the sacrifice.

tree:17zwzph19ok6w1.why: Three ayat are excuses or disclaimers of heedlessness, and 23:17 says God is never heedless of His creation.
tree:17zwzph19ok6w1.relation: Contrast: people plead they were heedless, while God is never heedless.

tree:0p4dr9v1wzal8p.why: The question on the Day about the partners they claimed; 28:62 and 28:74 are identical in one surah.
tree:0p4dr9v1wzal8p.relation: The false partners abandon their worshippers on the Day.

tree:0wp41hk09w5t6k.why: A warning form: how will it be when they are gathered, when witnesses are brought, when calamity strikes, when the angels take them.
tree:0wp41hk09w5t6k.relation: Four moments of reckoning, each introduced the same way.

tree:0mz33hn13tkilt.why: All four rows stay. 'I do not possess' is the same verb and structure: power to benefit or harm myself (7:188, 10:49, order swapped), harm or guidance for you (72:21), and Moses: I possess only myself and my brother (5:25). Same words, different subject.
tree:0mz33hn13tkilt.relation: The limits of the messengers' power.

tree:0ksvih017cowf2.why: 'Nor are you' leads two unrelated things: no fear on you nor will you grieve, said to the people of Paradise (7:49, 43:68), and the repeated line 'nor will you worship what I worship' in al-Kafirun (109:3, 109:5). Different structures and subjects, two clean pairs.
tree:0ksvih017cowf2.changes: Split: the Paradise pair and the repetition in surah 109. The rows that read on are kept.
tree:0ksvih017cowf2.relation: Reassurance to the people of Paradise; a clear line between worships.

check.why: Right split: no fear on the people of Paradise (7:49, 43:68) and the repeated lines of surah 109, with every row kept.

tree:11jepkl187sdv1.why: All four rows stay. 'Do not make' is the same words and structure in all four: three commands in al-Isra with similar threats (17:22, 17:29, 17:39), and the prayer 'do not put in our hearts rancour' (59:10). Same words, different subject.
tree:11jepkl187sdv1.relation: Do not set up a god with God, do not be tight-fisted, and ask God not to let rancour into the heart.

tree:0tjmepc1kqdx6c.why: All four rows stay. 'Do not make' is the same prohibition and structure in all four: do not set up rivals or another god with God (2:22, 51:51), do not make God an excuse in your oaths (2:224), do not make calling the Messenger like calling one another (24:63). Same words, different subject.
tree:0tjmepc1kqdx6c.relation: What must not be made of God and His Messenger: rivals, an excuse, an equal among people.

tree:1i07ulu189dz1y.why: All four rows stay. 'You will not be wronged' is the same verb in all four: what you spend is repaid in full (2:272, 8:60, almost the same words), your capital in the usury ruling (2:279), and not wronged a thread (4:77). Same words, different subject. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:1i07ulu189dz1y.relation: God's full justice in repayment: for spending, for capital, for every deed.

tree:1x2ya9a048o13k.why: No protector or intercessor besides God, said four times with different continuations; a memorizer set and a clear theme.
tree:1x2ya9a048o13k.relation: No one can intercede for a soul except by God's leave.

tree:1cqf67c0ukf4mo.why: All four lift blame from those with a real excuse: the weak, the sick, the poor, the blind and the lame. 24:61 and 48:17 open identically and then go to different subjects (eating in houses, staying from battle), a memorizer trap.
tree:1cqf67c0ukf4mo.relation: Who is excused, and from what: from fighting, and from the rules of eating together.

tree:1ey6zz009o1i8y.why: 6:160, 28:84 and 40:40 state the same justice: an evil deed is repaid only by its like, while good is multiplied, a close memorizer set. In 31:33 the verb is active ('no father will avail his child'), a different word.
tree:1ey6zz009o1i8y.changes: Removed 31:33: the verb is active, a different word.
tree:1ey6zz009o1i8y.relation: Evil repaid by its like, good multiplied.

tree:13x93cp1afczdp.why: Four prohibitions in the rulings on women and marriage: concealing pregnancy, taking back the dower, inheriting women by force, and new marriages for the Prophet.
tree:13x93cp1afczdp.relation: What is not lawful in marriage, for wives, husbands and the Prophet.

tree:0oa8zqd040ggg7.why: All four rows stay. 'He does not fear' is the same verb and structure: the believer fears no injustice (20:112, 72:13, a memorizer pair in matched words), the messengers do not fear in My presence (27:10), and He does not fear its consequence (91:15). Same words, different subject.
tree:0oa8zqd040ggg7.relation: Who need not fear: the believer, the messengers, and God Himself.

tree:1p19bf105qu9yz.why: God never breaks His promise, said four ways; the endings differ (the appointment, His promise) and a memorizer must keep them apart.
tree:1p19bf105qu9yz.relation: Certainty of God's promise: the gathering, the punishment, victory, and Paradise.

tree:0qbzuam1myh73y.why: Each ayah denies that two groups are equal: those who strive and those who sit, the bad and the good, those who spent before the victory and after, the people of the Fire and of Paradise.
tree:0qbzuam1myh73y.relation: The Quran's scale of who is not equal to whom.

tree:09zhyv41j8cvls.why: Who is questioned and who is not: God is not questioned while they are (21:23), the criminals are not asked about their sins (28:78, 55:39). In 70:10 the verb is active ('no friend will ask after a friend'), a different word.
tree:09zhyv41j8cvls.changes: Removed 70:10: an active verb, a different word.
tree:09zhyv41j8cvls.relation: God is not questioned; on the Day the guilty are known without asking.

check.why: In 70:10, the verb means a friend asking after a friend, not being called to account. A different word sense, so removing it is right.

tree:00ehd0c0pmjkvo.why: The enemies of the believers will not be helped: 3:111 and 59:12 end the same way about turning their backs; 28:41 and 41:16 say it of Pharaoh's people and of Ad in the Hereafter.
tree:00ehd0c0pmjkvo.relation: Those who fight God's people end without help, here and in the Hereafter.

tree:0p3z5lq0g8y2wy.why: Ibrahim confronting his father and people, four times with different wording; a classic memorizer set.
tree:0p3z5lq0g8y2wy.relation: Ibrahim's challenge to idol worship, from questioning to disowning.

tree:0awe2fv1i40219.why: God's oath to fill Hell, said to Iblis (7:18, 38:85) and as His decreed word (11:119, 32:13); the endings differ in ways a memorizer must hold.
tree:0awe2fv1i40219.relation: The decree that Hell will be filled, from Iblis' followers among jinn and men.

tree:0oinr331gcwm9p.why: The descent of Adam with enmity between them, told three times with different continuations; 43:67 turns the same words to friends who become enemies on the Day.
tree:0oinr331gcwm9p.relation: Enmity on earth since the fall, and the friends who turn enemies on the Day except the God-fearing.

tree:0t2dwiy1dyueh6.why: Submitting to the Lord of the worlds: Abraham's answer (2:131) and the Prophet's command (6:71, 40:66). In 83:6 'people will stand before the Lord of the worlds' has another governing verb and sense of the preposition.
tree:0t2dwiy1dyueh6.changes: Removed 83:6: a different governing verb and sense. The rows that read on are kept.
tree:0t2dwiy1dyueh6.relation: Submission to the Lord of the worlds, from Abraham to the Prophet.

tree:13a2m461scp1a2.why: God telling that He sent down clear signs, with different continuations; 24:34 and 24:46 in one surah are a memorizer trap.
tree:13a2m461scp1a2.relation: Clear revelation, and who benefits from it and who rejects it.

tree:0po3g9u11vm86k.why: The proof had already reached them: a messenger, Moses, guidance, warning news. Each time the people turned away anyway.
tree:0po3g9u11vm86k.relation: No excuse remains: guidance came, and was rejected.

tree:1s2rnwe05vgg30.why: 'You know well': Lot's people to Lot (11:79), Moses to Pharaoh (17:102), Abraham's people admitting the idols cannot speak (21:65). In 37:158 the verb is third person ('the jinn know'), a different word.
tree:1s2rnwe05vgg30.changes: Removed 37:158: a third-person verb, a different word.
tree:1s2rnwe05vgg30.relation: Opponents made to admit what they already know.

check.why: In 37:158, the verb is third person feminine ('the jinn know'), not 'you know well'. A different word, so removing it is right.

tree:10xz6bu1u4h8uo.why: A stock closing about people of certainty, after unrelated subjects (demands for a sign, judgement, creation, the Quran as insight).

tree:0ijz7qe1r23eba.why: All four rows stay. 'To his people: O my people' is the same words in all four: Moses three times with different messages (2:54, 5:20, 61:5), and Noah (10:71). Same words, different prophet: a real slip.
tree:0ijz7qe1r23eba.relation: Prophets calling their people in the same tender words.

tree:0wl7y3m0bmtmjc.why: All four rows stay. 'For everything' is the same words and sense: a scripture that details everything (6:154, 7:145, 16:89), and God has set a measure for everything (65:3). Same words, different subject.
tree:0wl7y3m0bmtmjc.relation: Everything has its explanation in the Book and its measure with God.

tree:1e11yto0taka30.why: 'For us our deeds, and for you your deeds' in 2:139, 28:55 and 42:15, each with a different ending. In 33:71 'He will amend for you your deeds' makes 'for you' depend on a verb, a different structure.
tree:1e11yto0taka30.relation: A line of separation drawn in peace.

tree:03e2w031w2oofl.why: Two unrelated subjects meet only on a short phrase: speaking without knowledge, and rain bringing out crops. The real pairs are kept elsewhere.

tree:15n3grz19nd0b7.why: 'What is with you? How do you judge?' in 37:154 and 68:36, and in 10:35 after another clause. In 14:45 'it became clear to you how We dealt with them' is a different structure.
tree:15n3grz19nd0b7.changes: Removed 14:45: a different structure. The rows that read on are kept.
tree:15n3grz19nd0b7.relation: The same rebuke to those who judge without reason.

tree:1jhwx9u0yymjay.why: 'I am to you from Him a warner' in 11:2, 51:50 and 51:51 (back to back). In 16:10 'for you from it is drink' is a different structure. 51:51 appeared twice (as the run-on of 51:50 and as its own row); each ayah may appear only once.
tree:1jhwx9u0yymjay.changes: Removed 16:10: a different structure. 51:51 now appears once, in its own row reading on into 51:52; the 51:50 row ends at 51:50.
tree:1jhwx9u0yymjay.relation: The Prophet's role: a clear warner from God.

tree:1ahlfyq03q4clq.why: The reward of those who do good; 16:30 and 39:10 share the same clause, a memorizer pair.
tree:1ahlfyq03q4clq.relation: Good done is repaid with good, in this world and more in the next.

tree:1ejedju0oiehk8.why: The weak blaming the arrogant leaders on the Day; 14:21 and 40:47 open identically.
tree:1ejedju0oiehk8.relation: Followers and leaders turn on each other when they face the punishment.

tree:12apeh01iaxsy4.why: The same threat with small changes a memorizer must hold apart: the verb of preparing and the kind of punishment. 4:37 and 4:151 are identical in one surah.

check.why: Keep is acceptable: the threat 'We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment' is identical twice in one surah, with variants of the verb and the punishment.

tree:1r8iume1hang92.why: 'We have set forth / varied for people in this Quran every kind of example' (17:89, 30:58, 39:27), each with a different response. In 2:159 'made clear for people in the Book' follows another verb, a different structure.
tree:1r8iume1hang92.relation: Every example given, met with refusal or remembrance.

tree:0ojbc6y1jvcegu.why: Only a stock closing (God makes things clear to people so that they may...) is shared; the subjects are unrelated rulings and parables.

tree:01xag7a01pbr4w.why: 'All power / all honour belongs to God' in 2:165, 4:139 and 10:65. In 14:21 'they will appear before God, all together' is a different sense of the words.
tree:01xag7a01pbr4w.changes: Removed 14:21: a different sense. The row that reads on (4:140) is kept.
tree:01xag7a01pbr4w.relation: Power and honour are God's alone.

tree:0sbazzt08ipkb5.why: A plain negation of belief, in four unrelated contexts; nothing to learn from the grouping.

tree:1ye8skf0sjc8jl.why: All four rows stay. 'They did not respond' is the same verb in all four: the partners called on the Day do not answer (18:52, 28:64, the same scene), those who did not respond to their Lord (13:18), and if they do not respond to you (28:50). Same words, different subject.
tree:1ye8skf0sjc8jl.relation: Those who did not answer God's call find no answer from their partners.

tree:0w9g77j00lotfl.why: Only a short negation is shared; the subjects are unrelated (God changing a favour, Ibrahim, man's creation, late faith).

tree:1ourtmg1du1zji.why: The brothers' entries in the story of Yusuf, in order; 12:69 and 12:99 are parallel (he takes in his brother, then his parents), a memorizer trap and a turning point of the story.
tree:1ourtmg1du1zji.relation: The stages of the reunion: entering the city, meeting Yusuf, pleading, and the family taken in.

tree:0uwktw410o2jl2.why: Only a time clause is shared; four unrelated scenes (Satan's speech, Moses' term, Zayd's marriage, the jinn).

tree:04hvwvc02x1qv8.why: All four rows stay. 'Surely of the wrongdoers' is the same words and structure in all four: a speaker who would then be a wrongdoer (2:145, 5:107, 11:31), and Abraham's people: whoever did this is surely of the wrongdoers (21:59). Same words, different subject. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:04hvwvc02x1qv8.relation: Who is the wrongdoer: the one who follows desires after knowledge, or, in the idolaters' eyes, the one who broke the idols.

tree:129n1u01fdwch6.why: Only 33:21 and 60:6 belong together, and that pair is already in the card about hoping for God. 50:37 and 54:14 share only a short relative clause.

tree:1v8fckk1deci14.why: All four rows stay. 'You will never be able' is the same words and structure in all four: Khidr's warning to Moses and its two reminders (18:67, 18:72, 18:75), and in the same surah the garden owner's water sinking so you will never be able to seek it (18:41). Same words, different story: a real slip within one surah. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:1v8fckk1deci14.relation: What cannot be done: patience with what one does not understand, and recovering a lost blessing.

tree:1va13411tkmy13.why: All four rows stay. 'Will never avail' is the same verb and structure: wealth and children will never avail the deniers (3:10, 3:116, 58:17, nearly identical), and your host will never avail you however many (8:19). Same words, different subject.
tree:1va13411tkmy13.relation: Neither wealth, children nor numbers avail against God.

tree:1x3eoni158ps4o.why: Prayers for forgiveness of sins with different additions; 12:97 has Yusuf's brothers ask their father to seek it for them.
tree:1x3eoni158ps4o.relation: Seeking forgiveness: the believers directly, the brothers through their father.

tree:1k6clnz19z9zlt.why: All praise belongs to God, in the first life and the last, in heavens and earth; four close variants a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:1k6clnz19z9zlt.relation: God's praise without limit of time or place.

tree:1afwzp81jl5dzg.why: All four rows stay. 'For him is a punishment' is the same words in all four: transgressing after a concession (2:178, 5:94), disobeying God and crossing His limits (4:14), and leading the slander (24:11). Same words, different subject. The rows that read on stay as they are.
tree:1afwzp81jl5dzg.relation: Punishment for crossing limits, in retaliation, hunting, inheritance and slander.

tree:01j5ajk0as0w5g.why: Only a short phrase is shared; the subjects are unrelated (a garden burnt, worldly desire, mosques, good deeds).

tree:1mnuh2c1o9403g.why: 'He has a child' is said of two unrelated things: the heir's child in the inheritance rules (4:11, 4:176) and the denial that God has a son (4:171, 6:101). Two clean pairs, so the split is fair.
tree:1mnuh2c1o9403g.changes: Split: inheritance (4:11, 4:176) and God has no son (4:171, 6:101).
tree:1mnuh2c1o9403g.relation: The inheritance of one who leaves a child, and God who has no child.

tree:12546oh1y8icuj.why: People invited to come and refusing: to fight, to God's revelation and the Messenger (4:61 and 5:104 open identically), to be prayed for.
tree:12546oh1y8icuj.relation: Each invitation met with turning away, out of hypocrisy, inherited custom or pride.

tree:0vmcgwr194glwx.why: The particle is a prohibition in some and a negation in others; no shared clause or subject.

tree:09ksne709ij1cn.why: All four rows stay. 'For them, nor' is the same structure in all four: a negation with 'for them', then 'nor' with a second negation. God will not forgive them nor guide them (4:137, 4:168, differing in the last word), no helper for them nor will they be saved (36:43), they are not lawful for them nor are they lawful for them (60:10). Same words, different subject.
tree:09ksne709ij1cn.relation: Double closings: no forgiveness and no guidance, no helper and no rescue.

tree:1feysbx1f8k9uh.why: The real pair (24:12, 24:16) is its own card; 6:43 and 18:39 share only the reproach form with other subjects.

tree:1sv4eeb0d8hu8z.why: The purpose of the return to God: to reward the believers who do good, each time with a different addition; 53:31 sets both rewards side by side.
tree:1sv4eeb0d8hu8z.relation: Why the creation is brought back: just and generous reward.

tree:09ty4m51mox3kx.why: People called to God's judgment: some turn away (3:23, 24:48), the believers say we hear and obey (24:51). In 16:124 the particle is the emphatic one ('your Lord will surely judge between them'), not 'that He may judge': a different word.
tree:09ty4m51mox3kx.relation: Contrast: two answers to the call to judgment.

check.why: In 16:124 the lam is emphatic ('your Lord will surely judge'), not the lam of purpose ('to judge between them'). A different word, so removing it is right.

tree:14ssbj61e6tuyy.why: No blame on the excused: the believers for what they ate before the ban, the weak and sick, the blind and lame. 24:61 and 48:17 open identically. It overlaps another card on the same theme.
tree:14ssbj61e6tuyy.relation: Who carries no blame, and why.

check.why: Keep is right: 'there is no blame on' the excused, with 24:61 and 48:17 opening identically.

tree:0i5wj6b1sg8gdx.why: Only a short phrase is shared; the subjects are unrelated.

tree:00sf7e41kwp5pw.why: How people meet what God gave them: some hide it, some envy others for it, some should be content with it, and the righteous take it gladly.
tree:00sf7e41kwp5pw.relation: Attitudes to God's bounty: hiding, envy, contentment, acceptance.

tree:1p1wj820d15lji.why: The four groups of al-Waqi'a introduced with the same refrain; a memorizer must keep the order and names apart.
tree:1p1wj820d15lji.relation: The right and the left, named twice in the surah with different words.

tree:14aj86k0gilig2.why: 'Whatever you spend': where it goes (2:215), God knows it (2:270), He replaces it (34:39). In 60:10 'what' is a relative ('ask for what you spent'), not the condition: a different word.
tree:14aj86k0gilig2.relation: Spending: its place, its witness, and its return.

tree:17j2nh51gi5wnb.why: The real pair (28:60, 42:36) is its own card; 3:73 and 17:85 share only a short phrase about what you were given.

tree:1qf206t049qx3f.why: 'What you call on besides God': Abraham leaves it (19:48), the challenge about it (39:38, 46:4). In 6:41 'what you call Him for' is the distress they ask God to remove, a different sense.
tree:1qf206t049qx3f.relation: The idols cannot remove harm or create anything.

check.why: In 6:41, 'what you call on Him for' is the distress to be lifted, with a different preposition. A different sense, so removing it is right.

tree:0xrjr1a1tsozly.why: Each ayah blames division or sin on people after clear proofs had already come to them.
tree:0xrjr1a1tsozly.relation: Division comes not from ignorance but after knowledge.

tree:14s7mri1hwd6hw.why: Three surahs say the People of the Book differed only after knowledge came, out of rivalry; 3:105 warns believers not to be like them. A close memorizer set.
tree:14s7mri1hwd6hw.relation: Division out of rivalry after knowledge, and the warning not to repeat it.

tree:0b0z1gp0qw2h21.why: A negation of what God made or decreed, in unrelated rulings (a truce, forbidden cattle, ease in religion, adoption).

tree:10ghe7f10qgflh.why: All four rows stay. 'We did not make' is the same negation and verb in all four: the old qibla, the vision and the number of Hell's keepers made only as a test (2:143, 17:60, 74:31), and We did not grant any human before you eternity (21:34). Same words, different subject.
tree:10ghe7f10qgflh.relation: What God made a test, and what He gave no one: eternal life.

tree:18y9srt027m1n5.why: Your Lord is not unaware of what you do, and not unjust to His servants; four surah endings a memorizer must keep apart (what they do, what you do, unjust).
tree:18y9srt027m1n5.relation: God watches every deed and wrongs no one.

tree:01n481v0mxake1.why: All four rows stay. 'What they earned' is the same relative and verb in all four: the evil of what they earned comes back on them (39:48, 39:51, 45:10), and Satan made them slip through some of what they had earned (3:155). Same words, different subject.
tree:01n481v0mxake1.relation: What people earn comes back to them, though God may pardon.

tree:01g4u701piz6b2.why: 2:120 and 13:37 give the same warning about following their desires after knowledge came, differing in the last word. In 12:11 and 15:32 'what is with you' is a question, a different word.
tree:01g4u701piz6b2.changes: Removed 12:11 and 15:32: interrogative, a different word.

tree:1u9neph09krqcp.why: A short phrase at the end of unrelated ayat, and a question in 99:3; nothing shared in meaning.

tree:16svd0o1c58nfq.why: The same words are a relative clause in some and a negation in others, across unrelated subjects.

tree:0gqeeop0hkjk5f.why: All four rows stay. 'What is recited' is the same relative and verb in all four: cattle are lawful except what is recited to you (5:1, 22:30, the same ruling), what is recited to you in the Book about orphan women (4:127), and what is recited in your houses (33:34). Same words, different subject.
tree:0gqeeop0hkjk5f.relation: What is recited carries the rulings and wisdom people must follow.

tree:0o5n9wp0owy5tz.why: The clean set of endings about God doing what He wills is its own card; 5:6 is a negation with another meaning.

tree:0kp6hjr1wvqxrf.why: Pairs that are not equal: the two seas, the blind and the seeing, the living and the dead; 35:19 and 40:58 open alike and differ after.
tree:0kp6hjr1wvqxrf.relation: Parables of inequality between belief and disbelief.

tree:19o4dth0tk3kut.why: 'Leaving them and what they worship': the youths of the cave (18:16) and Abraham (19:49), each rewarded; and on the Day God gathers them and what they worship besides God (25:17), word for word like 19:49. In 11:109 'what' is a negation ('they worship only as their fathers did'), a different word.
tree:19o4dth0tk3kut.changes: Removed only 11:109: its 'what' is a negation. 25:17 stays: same relative and words, a different subject.
tree:19o4dth0tk3kut.relation: Leaving false worship brings God's gift; on the Day the worshipped are gathered with their worshippers.

tree:0jhdc4314mt93h.why: Seeing what they were promised: 19:75 and 72:24 open the same way and end differently; 23:93 and 46:35 are the Prophet's side of the same threat.
tree:0jhdc4314mt93h.relation: When the promised punishment comes, they will know who was weaker.

tree:02dj4h91ckvudb.why: The same verdict with four different endings that a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:02dj4h91ckvudb.relation: The Fire as the home of the wrongdoers, for different sins.

check.why: Keep is right: 'their refuge is the Fire' with four different endings, a memorizer set.

tree:1lp4tok0k2m6ww.why: The Prophet's mission: bearer of good news and warner, with or without witness; two close pairs (17:105/25:56 and 33:45/48:8).
tree:1lp4tok0k2m6ww.relation: What the Prophet was sent as.

tree:074xn570qk3b6f.why: Messengers sent as bearers of good news and warners, each time with a different purpose stated; 6:48 and 18:56 open identically.
tree:074xn570qk3b6f.relation: Why messengers were sent: to judge, to leave no excuse, and how people received them.

check.why: Keep is right: 'bearers of good news and warners', with 6:48 and 18:56 opening identically and different purposes after.

tree:0ssyeia018jyo2.why: Man's response when harm touches him: despair, long prayers, panic; 17:83 and 41:51 open identically and part at the end.
tree:0ssyeia018jyo2.relation: The fickle nature of man in ease and hardship.

tree:0y5369p0z0v1ap.why: Prayers and commands about whose company one keeps: with the righteous, never with the wrongdoers; 7:47 and 7:150 are prayers in the same surah.
tree:0y5369p0z0v1ap.relation: Contrast: hoping to be with the righteous, asking not to be with the wrongdoers.

tree:1d2y0jr1xb6b5b.why: 5:104 and 31:21 are the same answer to the call to revelation: what we found our fathers on, each rebutted. In 7:102 and 51:36 'what' is a negation ('We did not find'), a different word.
tree:1d2y0jr1xb6b5b.changes: Removed 7:102 and 51:36: their 'what' is a negation.
tree:1d2y0jr1xb6b5b.relation: Blind following of the fathers, rebutted twice.

check.why: In 7:102 and 51:36, ma is a negation ('We did not find'), not the relative 'what we found our fathers on'. A different particle function, so removing them is right, though the agent gives subject as the reason.

tree:0jhb3tf0g0k6rp.why: Two parables of deeds lost, the bare rock (2:264) and ashes in the wind (14:18), say they have no power over anything of what they earned, with the order swapped; and 'a share of what they earned' (2:202) has the same partitive. In 42:22 'fearful of what they earned' uses another sense of the particle.
tree:0jhb3tf0g0k6rp.changes: Removed only 42:22: a different sense of the particle. 2:202 stays: same words and sense, a different subject.
tree:0jhb3tf0g0k6rp.relation: What people earn: a share for those who seek both worlds, lost for those who show off or deny.

tree:16d4iq51ii16kb.why: All four rows stay. 'Of Our signs' is the same words and sense in all four: to show him of Our signs (17:1, 20:23, the Night Journey and Moses' call), the people of the cave were of Our signs (18:9), and when he learns anything of Our signs he mocks it (45:9). Same words, different subject.
tree:16d4iq51ii16kb.relation: Signs shown to prophets, the cave as a sign, and signs mocked.

tree:148hk0u1ia0l1e.why: Following God's guidance and what it brings: peace, safety from going astray, forgiveness. Close wording a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:148hk0u1ia0l1e.relation: Whoever follows the guidance is safe and guided.

tree:18uxdk80zlyns6.why: Only the word for spouses is shared; the subjects are unrelated (offspring, Lot's people, lost dowries, family as a trial).

tree:1ew7a9h1j545ov.why: Who is further astray: the one who follows his desire, the one who opposes the truth, the one who calls on what cannot answer; 25:42 has the deniers ask it of the believers.
tree:1ew7a9h1j545ov.relation: The Quran's answer to who is truly astray.

tree:07li8va05ockpo.why: Two senses of 'from / of the Garden'. Out of the Garden: Satan getting Adam and his wife expelled (7:27, 20:117). A place in the Garden: the believers lodged in it (29:58, 39:74, ending the same way). Different senses of the particle, so the split follows them.
tree:07li8va05ockpo.changes: Split: the expulsion (7:27, 20:117) and the reward (29:58, 39:74).
tree:07li8va05ockpo.relation: Contrast: expelled from the Garden by Satan, given a home in it by God.

check.why: The split is right: expulsion from the Garden (7:27, 20:117) and lodging in the Garden (29:58, 39:74) are two real pairs, and every row is kept.

tree:1izavay0191e08.why: Moses, Noah, Yusuf and the Prophet are each kept from acting like the ignorant; worth reflecting on together.
tree:1izavay0191e08.relation: Prophets guarded from ignorance: mockery, wrong requests, temptation, impatience.

tree:195yo1l1o7idd5.why: Only a name of God after a preposition is shared; the subjects are unrelated.

tree:0fl7lgt17ntcwt.why: A common ending about witnesses, in unrelated settings (the prophets' covenant, the disciples, Ibrahim, Moses' story).

tree:0y2f1nf1epud85.why: Lot's wife left behind, told in three surahs with the verb changing (was / We decreed), a classic memorizer set. 29:33 appeared twice (as the run-on of 29:32 and as its own row); each ayah may appear only once.
tree:0y2f1nf1epud85.changes: 29:33 now appears once, in its own row reading on into 29:34; the 29:32 row ends at 29:32. The other rows that read on are kept.
tree:0y2f1nf1epud85.relation: Lot's wife among those left behind, told three times.

tree:1plt9n512ykvyb.why: Only the word for water is shared; the subjects are unrelated.

tree:0ug9f8804q8ufq.why: 'Of the good-doers': we see you are of the good-doers, said to Joseph by the prisoners and by his brothers (12:36, 12:78), and 'that I might be of the good-doers', the regret at seeing the punishment (39:58), the same partitive. In 7:56 'near to the good-doers' follows 'near', a different sense of the particle.
tree:0ug9f8804q8ufq.changes: Removed only 7:56: a different sense of the particle. 39:58 stays. The rows that read on are kept.
tree:0ug9f8804q8ufq.relation: Being among the good-doers: seen in Joseph, wished for too late by the sinner.

tree:114czq01wckq2k.why: A common ending about messengers in mixed contexts; the real Moses pair is its own card.

tree:1ui8tgk1b119o4.why: The truth is from your Lord, so do not doubt: four times, with a small change in the verb form that a memorizer must catch.
tree:1ui8tgk1b119o4.relation: Certainty in the revelation, repeated to the Prophet.

tree:0mbzena0wx2vsq.why: The same words mean God's decree, His command and His affair in unrelated contexts.

tree:1dgnvjd1wtx7wx.why: 'No nation precedes its term' (15:5, 23:43, the same sentence), and 'there is no nation but a warner passed among it' (35:24), with the same negation and particle. In 16:92 'more than a nation' is a comparison, a different sense.
tree:1dgnvjd1wtx7wx.changes: Removed only 16:92: a comparative, a different sense. 35:24 stays. The rows that read on are kept.
tree:1dgnvjd1wtx7wx.relation: Every nation has a term and a warner.

tree:0i6w60k1jde2m8.why: Mixed senses of the same phrase; the 4:35 and 12:26 pair is its own card.

tree:0aiwumk12431dc.why: No protectors besides God, said four times with different continuations; 11:20 and 11:113 in one surah.
tree:0aiwumk12431dc.relation: No protector besides God, whatever they hoped for.

tree:1ejvz7v0butp5j.why: Only a time phrase is shared; the subjects are unrelated (Jacob, Moses, Solomon, Jesus).

tree:0bcl0p204ix3um.why: A common phrase of kinship or likeness in unrelated contexts.

check.why: Drop is right: 'some of you are from others' is a common phrase of kinship in unrelated contexts.

tree:1s1tkov1rgyphd.why: 'From among us': the same envious objection, was the message sent to him from among us (38:8, 54:25), and has God favoured these from among us (6:53). In 41:5 'between us and you a screen' is a different sense.
tree:1s1tkov1rgyphd.relation: Envy of the chosen: why him and not us?

tree:1f1bwyv15ke98h.why: All four rows stay. 'Whom You will' is the same words and structure in all four: God gives and withholds kingship, provision and guidance as He wills (3:26, 3:27, 7:155), and the Prophet may defer whom he wills of his wives (33:51). Same words, different subject.
tree:1f1bwyv15ke98h.relation: God's will over kingship and guidance, and the choice He granted the Prophet.

tree:0n74dv01496qzy.why: Only a short relative clause about turning away is shared, in unrelated contexts.

tree:0nvzeau0lrl2ba.why: Pharaoh's threat to the magicians in three surahs, with small differences a memorizer must catch, and 5:33 the same penalty as God's law for those who wage war on Him.
tree:0nvzeau0lrl2ba.relation: Contrast: the same penalty threatened by a tyrant against believers, and set by God against those who spread corruption.

tree:04xe24v1tkg5bb.why: Protection on every side: guardian angels before and behind man (13:11), the Quran untouched by falsehood before or behind it (41:42), watchers before and behind the messenger (72:27). In 46:21 'before him and after him' is about time (warners came before and after), a different sense.
tree:04xe24v1tkg5bb.relation: What God guards from every side.

check.why: In 46:21, 'before him and after him' is about time (warners who came before and after), not protection on every side. A different word sense, so removing it is right.

tree:05m5k3e09yir7a.why: Only a short spatial phrase is shared; the subjects are unrelated.

tree:19vsyad1pfvt33.why: Driving people out of their homes: forbidden in the covenant, a test few would pass, and in 60:8 and 60:9 the line between those to treat justly and those not to befriend.
tree:19vsyad1pfvt33.relation: Expulsion from homes as a sin, a test, and the measure for how to treat non-believers.

tree:0cnu20r1gv5bzp.why: All four rows stay. 'Of His mercy' is the same words in all four: night and day (28:73) and the winds (30:46), ending with the same two clauses, and your Lord will spread for you of His mercy (18:16), and He will give you a double share of His mercy (57:28). Same words, different subject.
tree:0cnu20r1gv5bzp.relation: God's mercy in night and day, wind, shelter, and a double share for the believers.

tree:1q6wadw1rrtpkw.why: Man's creation from clay, three times in al-Hijr with the same words and once in ar-Rahman with a different image.
tree:1q6wadw1rrtpkw.relation: The clay of man's creation, and Iblis' pride in it.

tree:03qlay808lah7q.why: 'Of the work of Satan': intoxicants and gambling (5:90), and Moses' fatal blow (28:15). In 10:61 and 25:23 'of a deed' is a different structure ('you do not do any deed', 'what they did of deeds').

check.why: In 10:61 and 25:23, 'of a deed' is indefinite and partitive, not the construct 'the work of Satan'. That is a different structure, so removing them is right, though the agent's stated reason (subject) is the wrong one.

tree:0ha3txs1f1ybs2.why: Only a phrase meaning from Him is shared; the subjects are unrelated.

tree:1roc0ft1ely415.why: All four rows stay. 'Without' is the same words and structure: Moses' hand coming out white without harm, three times (20:22, 27:12, 28:32), and were they created without anything (52:35). Same words, different subject.
tree:1roc0ft1ely415.relation: A sign without harm; a creation not without a Creator.

tree:1j7og5r10e7iv9.why: Silver in Paradise for the righteous (three times in al-Insan) set against 43:33, silver roofs God would give disbelievers if not for the trial.
tree:1j7og5r10e7iv9.relation: Contrast: silver as a worthless worldly gift, and silver as an honour in Paradise.

tree:0kuavp219cu0q4.why: No escape: said by the followers in Hell, of the idolaters, of those who dispute God's signs, and of past nations.
tree:0kuavp219cu0q4.relation: There is no escape from God's reckoning.

check.why: Keep is right: 'no escape' is a rare word, with 41:48 and 42:35 sharing 'they have no escape', all on one theme.

tree:01ebj6i1huntzo.why: A common phrase about prophets in scattered contexts; the real 7:94 and 43:7 slip is its own card.

tree:12nlzx207prxqa.why: Gardens of palms and vines: a parable of loss, a demand of the deniers, and twice a favour from God; close wording a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:12nlzx207prxqa.relation: Gardens as gift, as parable, and as a demand of disbelief.

tree:12uhuf11v5oaj9.why: Promises to whoever fears God: three in at-Talaq, each different, and Yusuf's lesson from his life.
tree:12uhuf11v5oaj9.relation: What God gives the one who fears Him: a way out, ease, forgiveness, reward.

tree:1yc5ctr00qsunb.why: 'Whoever turns away': God is the Free of need, the Praised (57:24, 60:6, identical endings), and He will punish him (48:17). In 5:56 the verb means 'takes as ally' (whoever takes God and His Messenger as allies), a different sense.
tree:1yc5ctr00qsunb.changes: Removed 5:56: a different sense of the verb. The rows that read on are kept.
tree:1yc5ctr00qsunb.relation: Turning away harms only oneself; God needs no one.

tree:0cbvpgz1jtt8ct.why: 'Among people is one who disputes about God without knowledge' (22:3, 22:8, 31:20). In 4:109 'who' is a question ('who will argue for them with God?'), a different word.
tree:0cbvpgz1jtt8ct.changes: Removed 4:109: an interrogative, a different word. The rows that read on are kept.
tree:0cbvpgz1jtt8ct.relation: Arguing about God without knowledge, guidance or Book.

tree:11ws5r91wuzvsz.why: Only a conditional about willing is shared, in four unrelated contexts.

tree:02wfglz1lwenuh.why: Only a short phrase is shared; the subjects are unrelated.

tree:0gf38qn0jyd6zb.why: 'Many of them are defiantly disobedient': in 5:81 and three times in al-Hadid, with different lead-ins. 57:27 appeared twice (as the run-on of 57:26 and as its own row); each ayah may appear only once.
tree:0gf38qn0jyd6zb.changes: 57:27 now appears once, in its own row reading on into 57:28; the 57:26 row ends at 57:26. The other rows that read on are kept.
tree:0gf38qn0jyd6zb.relation: Among the People of the Book some are guided, many are defiant.

tree:0uvw1xn132zzlh.why: Only two short particles are shared; nothing in meaning.

tree:1oikvnn0i3jh7v.why: The weighing of deeds, told twice with the same opening and different endings; a classic memorizer pair.
tree:1oikvnn0i3jh7v.relation: Heavy scales and light scales, and what each brings.

tree:1nkr1e802y8sny.why: 2:136 and 3:84 are the same creed with small differences a memorizer must catch; 33:7 and 42:13 name the same great prophets in the covenant and the shared religion.
tree:1nkr1e802y8sny.relation: One faith across the prophets, believed in without distinction.

tree:07eb12a01qu66m.why: What serves as an admonition for the God-fearing: a punishment, the Quran, the Gospel, the clear signs. Same closing a memorizer must place.
tree:07eb12a01qu66m.relation: Lessons for the God-fearing in history and in scripture.

tree:0xnjbd606comvk.why: Prophets calling on their Lord: Zakariyya twice and Ayyub twice, with different wording.
tree:0xnjbd606comvk.relation: The prayers of Zakariyya and Ayyub in distress.

tree:0yad75m0x93en8.why: Noah saved with his family from the great distress, and Lot with his family except an old woman; the same verb with different endings in each.
tree:0yad75m0x93en8.relation: God's rescue of His prophets and their families.

tree:16oj1b710qjo7z.why: God varies the signs, with four different endings a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:16oj1b710qjo7z.relation: The signs varied, and people's different responses.

tree:13e5l5b0xgr33f.why: The word half is shared across unrelated rulings (dowry, a husband's inheritance, a slave woman's penalty, a sister's share); the real slip is kept in a smaller card.

tree:0lshmvq000dnua.why: All four rows stay. 'A portion of' is the same words and structure: those given a portion of the Book, three times going three ways (3:23, 4:44, 4:51), and the followers in Hell: will you take from us a portion of the Fire (40:47). Same words, different subject.
tree:0lshmvq000dnua.relation: Contrast: a portion of the Book misused, and a portion of the Fire begged to be lifted.

tree:1hwriar1lwpfhb.why: 2:48 and 2:123 are the classic pair with swapped clauses; 21:47 and 36:54 add that no soul will be wronged in the least on that Day.
tree:1hwriar1lwpfhb.relation: On the Day each soul stands alone, and none is wronged.

tree:0grt48h0jicg49.why: No power to benefit or harm: the Prophet himself, the false gods, and people on the Day; the order of the two words flips, a memorizer trap.
tree:0grt48h0jicg49.relation: Only God controls benefit and harm.

tree:1al44hy1w99wle.why: People going back to what they were forbidden: usury, the Sabbath, secret talk, and the deniers who would return if sent back.
tree:1al44hy1w99wle.relation: Returning to the forbidden after being warned, and its punishment.

tree:1m15vou1xwycyc.why: Only the verb of God guiding is shared, in four unrelated contexts.

tree:0qd1u170mz7ktf.why: Four peoples calling the clear truth magic, in close wording: Pharaoh's people, Quraysh twice, and the Children of Israel to Jesus.
tree:0qd1u170mz7ktf.relation: Every messenger's clear signs called magic.

tree:1va2a2r0h29g7n.why: Only a demonstrative and a preposition are shared; nothing in meaning.

tree:0bhhdzi0isgg30.why: Are they equal: the blind and the seeing (6:50 and 13:16), the helpless and the just man, those who know and those who do not.
tree:0bhhdzi0isgg30.relation: Questions of inequality between guidance and blindness, knowledge and ignorance.

tree:0ykdcv91o6escn.why: Who the winners are: those who strive, those who were patient, those who obey, the people of Paradise. Same closing with different lead-ins.

tree:0qr6te40guwsdi.why: The verdict on the deniers' motive, with different last words; 51:53 and 52:32 both end with transgressors.
tree:0qr6te40guwsdi.relation: Behind their arguments: they are a people who equate, argue, transgress.
