tree:1fj3igb1brorcb.why: All five use the negated 'you will not find' with an object. 7:17 (you will not find most of them grateful) and 58:22 (you will not find a people who believe...) have the same words and structure; only what is not found differs, which does not justify removing them.
tree:1fj3igb1brorcb.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 7:17 and 58:22 have the same structure.
tree:1fj3igb1brorcb.relation: What you will not find: a helper, a change in God's way, an advocate, gratitude, believers who love God's enemies.

tree:0xz2qdn0gw89y7.why: Do not think: that the martyrs are dead, that the boasters escape, that God is unaware, that He breaks His promise, that the disbelievers escape.
tree:0xz2qdn0gw89y7.relation: Correcting what people assume about God and the unseen.

tree:1oit5un05q30df.why: Do not go near: prayer while drunk, indecencies, the orphan's wealth (6:152 and 17:34 a pair), adultery.
tree:1oit5un05q30df.relation: The commands to keep away from what leads to sin.

tree:0gzqwaw07fj996.why: Do not say: a word of mockery, that martyrs are dead, that a greeter is not a believer, more than the truth about God, lies about lawful and unlawful.

tree:14w60v20a0m694.why: No doubt: 11:22 and 16:109 are the classic pair (the greatest losers, the losers), and the other three state other certainties.
tree:14w60v20a0m694.relation: Certain outcomes stated with the same emphatic opening.

tree:1g8fmnx1uguxmz.why: They do not see: the hypocrites in darkness, the heedless with eyes, the idols, the blind who look at the Prophet, those barred.

tree:01mynfv0km4f3b.why: Let them not grieve you: those rushing into disbelief (3:176, 5:41), their words, their disbelief.
tree:01mynfv0km4f3b.relation: Comfort for the Prophet against the deniers.

check.why: Keep is right: 'let them not grieve you' as comfort to the Prophet, with 3:176 and 5:41 near-identical.

tree:1tp5huo0aqd5t2.why: All five use 'they do not return' in the same sense. 28:39 ('that they would not be returned to Us') has the same structure as 36:31 ('that they do not return to them'); 2:18 and 36:67 use the same verb in the same sense. Subject differences do not justify removing them. All rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:1tp5huo0aqd5t2.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three use the same verb in the same sense.
tree:1tp5huo0aqd5t2.relation: Those who do not return: the destroyed towns, the deaf and blind, Pharaoh's host in their belief, the transformed.

tree:0i1c97500x98bp.why: They are not too proud: the angels and those near God (7:206, 21:19, 16:49), the believers who fall prostrate, and Christians who weep at the revelation.
tree:0i1c97500x98bp.relation: Humility before God as a mark of those near Him.

tree:18wp5oh1lrouxp.why: The real pair (10:18, 13:33) is kept in another card; the rest use the verb in unrelated senses.

tree:01t7s9b1850rd9.why: What has no power: idols over harm, benefit or provision, the calf, people on the Day, the false intercessors.
tree:01t7s9b1850rd9.relation: Nothing besides God controls harm, benefit, provision or intercession.

tree:0ksbhzi0u49vy2.why: On that Day nothing benefits: late faith, wealth and sons, excuses (30:57 and 40:52 close), faith on the day of victory.
tree:0ksbhzi0u49vy2.relation: What will be of no use on the Day.

tree:0vut45i1ypyjvg.why: Two groups: 'neither ... nor are they guided' after another negated verb (2:170, 5:104 the fathers, 4:98 the helpless who cannot find a way), and the Queen of Sheba's people (27:24, 27:41). 4:98 has the same structure as 2:170 ('they cannot ... nor are they guided'). Rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:0vut45i1ypyjvg.changes: Split into the two groups as the first agent did, but kept 4:98 in the first group instead of removing it.
tree:0vut45i1ypyjvg.relation: Not guided: the fathers, the helpless, and the Queen's people before she was tested.

tree:1wu8pwl0n9q7nr.why: Only a stock closing about people of understanding is shared, after unrelated subjects.

tree:0k8llgj1jpwkez.why: All five use 'evil indeed is what' followed by a verb. 2:102 ('evil indeed is what they sold themselves for') has the same words and structure; only the subject differs, which does not justify removing it.
tree:0k8llgj1jpwkez.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 2:102 has the same structure.
tree:0k8llgj1jpwkez.relation: Evil indeed is what they did, made, forwarded for themselves, and sold themselves for.

tree:0hk3yjv1nyqobj.why: 17:2, 32:23, 43:59 and 3:93 use 'for the Children of Israel' as the beneficiary: 'We made it a guidance for', 'We made him an example for', 'lawful for'. 43:59 has the same structure as 17:2. In 17:104 the particle marks the addressee ('We said to the Children of Israel'): a different sense. 32:23 and 43:59 read on into the next ayah.
tree:0hk3yjv1nyqobj.changes: Kept 3:93 and 43:59, which the first agent removed. Removed 17:104: the particle marks the addressee.
tree:0hk3yjv1nyqobj.relation: What was made for the Children of Israel: guidance, an example, lawful food.

tree:0w3qhdj1al1svp.why: God is kind and merciful to people, said after the qibla, the burdens carried by cattle, the threat delayed, the subjected earth and the revelation; three forms a memorizer must keep apart (to people, your Lord, to you).
tree:0w3qhdj1al1svp.relation: God's kindness shown in law, nature and revelation.

tree:1pa2wop0r76ek7.why: The punishment of the Hereafter is harder, more lasting, greater, more shameful: five places with different comparatives.
tree:1pa2wop0r76ek7.relation: Worldly punishment is small next to the punishment of the Hereafter.

tree:06hhgnk13j54lu.why: God's curse: on the disbelievers, on those who die as disbelievers (2:161, 3:87 a pair), on the wrongdoers (7:44, 11:18 a pair that read on into the same description).

tree:0eid2i10y8t39j.why: There was in it a sign, a lesson, a good example: Yusuf's story at its start and end, the Prophet and Ibrahim as models (33:21, 60:6), Saba as a sign.
tree:0eid2i10y8t39j.relation: Where the Quran points for lessons and models.

tree:0k6v2sx0pmwrif.why: Were it not for a prior word from your Lord, it would have been judged between them: five places, 11:110 and 41:45 identical.
tree:0k6v2sx0pmwrif.relation: God's delay of judgement on those who differ.

tree:1mtucsl0ojb771.why: 11:46, 17:36, 29:8 and 31:15 share 'what you have no knowledge of'. In 17:86 the words are 'you would find for yourself, in it, against Us': 'for you' and 'with it' belong to a different verb and structure.
tree:1mtucsl0ojb771.relation: What you have no knowledge of: not to ask for it, not to follow it, not to associate it with God.

tree:0ufb9dg1vo57w4.why: 2:229, 4:19, 33:53 and 27:60 share 'it is not (lawful / for) you to' followed by a verb. 27:60 ('it was not for you to make its trees grow') has the same structure as 33:53. In 4:176 'God makes clear to you, lest you go astray' is a different structure.
tree:0ufb9dg1vo57w4.changes: Kept 27:60, which the first agent removed: the same structure. Removed 4:176.
tree:0ufb9dg1vo57w4.relation: What is not for you to do: take back the dower, inherit women, hurt the Prophet, make trees grow.

tree:1m1f9tw1qk3dfs.why: All five close a clause with 'for you' and open a contrasting conditional with 'and if'. 3:160 ('no victor over you; and if He forsakes you') and 24:28 ('until permission is given you; and if you are told') have the same structure; only the subject differs.
tree:1m1f9tw1qk3dfs.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 3:160 and 24:28 have the same structure.
tree:1m1f9tw1qk3dfs.relation: Two outcomes set side by side: if you do this it is better for you, and if not.

tree:1wq5f55115xvyx.why: Only a relative clause with a negation is shared, followed by unrelated verbs and subjects.

tree:0rd3aho1767lre.why: All five say 'and for the disbelievers is a punishment' with different endings. The old rows repeated 58:5 as a run-on of 58:4 and as its own row; each ayah should appear once. 2:90 and 2:104 read on into the next ayah.
tree:0rd3aho1767lre.changes: Gave 58:4 and 58:5 one row each, as the first agent did.
tree:0rd3aho1767lre.relation: For the disbelievers a punishment: humiliating, painful, of the Fire.

check.why: Keep is right: 'and for the disbelievers is a punishment' with endings that change, twice in two surahs. Fixing the duplicated 58:5 row is right.

tree:0pyen4k0phiwy0.why: If you do not find: water (4:43, 5:6 a pair), a scribe, anyone at home, something to give; each followed by an easier way.
tree:0pyen4k0phiwy0.relation: The ease the law gives when one cannot find what is required.

tree:02vkr8j09d3anx.why: All five use 'you were not' followed by a predicate. 4:23, 16:7 and 37:29 have the same words and structure; only what is denied differs, which does not justify removing them. 2:151 and 2:239 read on into the next ayah.
tree:02vkr8j09d3anx.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same structure.
tree:02vkr8j09d3anx.relation: What you were not: knowing, consummated, able to reach a land, believers.

tree:0r6br9i0b8uljk.why: All five open 'when he saw' followed by what was seen. 11:70, 12:28 and 33:22 have the same words and structure; only the story differs, which does not justify removing them. 6:76 does not contain the shared words (its verb follows another clause), so it is not added.
tree:0r6br9i0b8uljk.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same structure, and 6:76 lacks the shared words.
tree:0r6br9i0b8uljk.relation: When he saw: the moon and the sun, the guests' hands, the torn shirt, the confederates.

tree:056ga4y1ym193w.why: When they saw the punishment: they hid regret (10:54, 34:33), they believed too late (40:84, 40:85), they asked for a way back.
tree:056ga4y1ym193w.relation: Faith and regret that come when the punishment is seen are of no use.

tree:0szubqq16weaye.why: You are among the messengers, and Elias, Lot and Jonah among the messengers: the same phrase for the Prophet and for three prophets in as-Saffat.
tree:0szubqq16weaye.relation: The Prophet named in the line of the messengers.

tree:1f33kpr0fjqlef.why: It is not for us to: return to idolatry, associate, bring a proof without leave, speak a slander, take protectors besides God. Each said by believers or the worshipped.
tree:1f33kpr0fjqlef.relation: What is not fitting for the believers and the righteous.

tree:02anlwq07l23n6.why: All five say 'his / to Him is the dominion' with the same words and structure. In 2:247 the people object 'how can he have dominion over us': the same word for rule, said of a man. The contrast between God's dominion and a man's is worth keeping, and a subject difference does not justify removing it.
tree:02anlwq07l23n6.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 2:247 has the same words and structure.
tree:02anlwq07l23n6.relation: Dominion belongs to God; the people dispute it for Talut.

tree:00tgo9h1daw06l.why: Only a pronoun and a preposition are shared; five unrelated contexts.

tree:1vdoxjw1wv3gho.why: Their reward: unfailing (41:8, 84:25, 95:6 with a small change), great, generous.
tree:1vdoxjw1wv3gho.relation: The reward of faith and good deeds and of spending.

tree:0961wa50yogs5t.why: Satan made their deeds seem good to them: five places with different consequences; 27:24 and 29:38 a close pair.

tree:1cxu5x11v71909.why: All five close a clause with 'for / to them' and give the reason with 'indeed'. 9:7, 24:30 and 63:6 have the same structure ('be upright to them; indeed God loves', 'purer for them; indeed God is aware', 'forgive them; indeed God does not guide'); only the subject differs. 7:183 and 68:45 read on into the next ayah.
tree:1cxu5x11v71909.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same structure.
tree:1cxu5x11v71909.relation: Something done for them, then 'indeed' and the reason: My plan is firm, God loves, God knows, God does not guide.

tree:0gdscle169xyxa.why: 4:157, 18:5, 22:71 and 53:28 share 'they have no knowledge of it' (negation, 'for them', 'of it', knowledge). In 9:120 the words are 'a good deed is recorded for them by it': no negation and no knowledge, a different structure.
tree:0gdscle169xyxa.relation: They have no knowledge of it: the Messiah's killing, the claim of a son, their idols, the angels.

check.why: In 9:120, 'there is written for them by it a good deed' is a different construction from 'they have no knowledge of it'. Removing it is right.

tree:05tiryh0z7sj19.why: 13:18, 13:25, 27:5 and 40:52 say 'for them is the evil' of the reckoning, the home, the punishment: 'for them' is the predicate. In 9:37 'for them' belongs to the verb 'was made fair-seeming', and 'evil of their deeds' is its subject: a different structure. 13:25 and 40:52 read on into the next ayah.
tree:05tiryh0z7sj19.changes: Removed 9:37: a different governing verb and structure.
tree:05tiryh0z7sj19.relation: Theirs is the evil: reckoning, home, punishment.

tree:1bjivm40rl8ojk.why: If you ask them who created, they will say God: five places with different answers to their admission.
tree:1bjivm40rl8ojk.relation: The idolaters' own admission used against them.

tree:1od7wlm0epyrtg.why: In 16:64, 20:2 and 36:28 the particle is negation: 'We did not send down'. In 2:159 and 8:41 it is relative: 'what We sent down'. A different particle, so those two are a different structure. 36:28 has the same negation; only the subject differs.
tree:1od7wlm0epyrtg.changes: Kept 36:28, which the first agent removed: the same negation. Removed 2:159 and 8:41: the particle is relative.
tree:1od7wlm0epyrtg.relation: What God did not send down: the Book to make the Prophet miserable or only to explain, and no host against a people.

tree:0rfnnvc08eomzi.why: All five use 'what was given' with the same relative and passive verb. The split separates the creed of belief in what the prophets were given (2:136, 3:84) from wanting the like of what others were given (6:124, 28:48, 28:79), and keeps every row.
tree:0rfnnvc08eomzi.changes: Split into the creed pair and the set about wanting what others were given, as the first agent did.
tree:0rfnnvc08eomzi.relation: What the prophets were given, believed in; and what others were given, envied.

check.why: The split is right: the creed (2:136, 3:84) and wanting what others were given (6:124, 28:48, 28:79), with every row kept.

tree:1rw3l5z14s0djn.why: 6:106, 18:27, 29:45 and 6:145 share 'what was revealed to' with the passive verb. 6:145 ('I do not find in what was revealed to me') has the same relative and passive verb; only the subject differs. In 53:10 the verb is active, 'He revealed to His servant what He revealed': a different form.
tree:1rw3l5z14s0djn.changes: Kept 6:145, which the first agent removed: the same structure. Removed 53:10: the verb is active.
tree:1rw3l5z14s0djn.relation: What was revealed to the Prophet: to follow, to recite, and to judge by.

tree:13pzalb0jsdu5x.why: The same two words with two particles: relative 'what he left' in the inheritance shares (4:11, 4:12, 4:176), and negating 'He would not leave' a creature (16:61, 35:45). The split keeps every row.
tree:13pzalb0jsdu5x.changes: Split by the particle into the inheritance set and the pair on God's delay, as the first agent did.
tree:13pzalb0jsdu5x.relation: What the deceased left, and God not leaving a single creature.

check.why: Right split: inheritance shares and 'He would not leave a creature', two different uses of the verb, with every row kept.

tree:11oxpun1odfsel.why: What God forbade, in unrelated contexts (Israel's self-ban, food, the ten commands, the People of the Book, the calendar); nothing ties them.

tree:04n1l8m17ctsq0.why: We did not create the heavens and earth in play or in vain but with truth: five places with small changes (heaven or heavens, playing or vain).

tree:1o5tgsy04zwzr2.why: Two structures: 'what is in it' as the object of a verb (2:63, 7:171 remember, 7:169 they studied), and 'that in which there is' followed by its own subject (44:33 a clear trial, 54:4 a deterrent). 7:169 has the same structure as 2:63; only the subject differs. 2:63 and 7:171 read on into the next ayah.
tree:1o5tgsy04zwzr2.changes: Kept 7:169 with 2:63 and 7:171, and kept 44:33 and 54:4 as their own card instead of removing them.
tree:1o5tgsy04zwzr2.relation: What is in the Book, remembered and studied; and news in which there is a trial or a deterrent.

tree:1f0yfz81tfq4fs.why: The except-what-has-passed set is its own card; the others share only two words.

tree:1ufs7ct0uscx0l.why: What a soul or one's hands sent ahead, five times: evil sent ahead, forgotten, to be examined for tomorrow, seen on the Day, known on the Day.
tree:1ufs7ct0uscx0l.relation: Every deed sent ahead will be met.

check.why: Keep is acceptable: 'what a soul or hands sent ahead' is a recurring clause with one theme, deeds met later.

tree:00gp14n025g88f.why: They have whatever they wish, in Paradise or with their Lord, with different endings; a memorizer set.
tree:00gp14n025g88f.relation: The fulfilment of every wish in Paradise.

tree:07kry780wzsxio.why: They died while disbelievers or defiant: five places, with consequences that differ.
tree:07kry780wzsxio.relation: Dying in disbelief seals the outcome.

tree:17glh171srpdz1.why: All five use 'forgiveness from' their Lord or God, mostly paired with the Garden or His pleasure. 3:136, 47:15 and 57:20 have the same words and structure; only the frame differs, which does not justify removing them.
tree:17glh171srpdz1.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same phrase.
tree:17glh171srpdz1.relation: Forgiveness from the Lord, paired with the Garden: raced to, given as reward, promised, against severe punishment.

tree:132jhkc1cjmnlo.why: Forgiveness and a reward great or large, five times after different deeds (faith, patience, lowered voices, fear unseen).
tree:132jhkc1cjmnlo.relation: The deeds that earn forgiveness and great reward.

check.why: Keep is right: 'forgiveness and a great/large reward' after different deeds is a memorizer trap on the adjective.

tree:0px15tc00at31s.why: All five use 'of what was left' by someone. 2:248 ('a remnant of what the family of Moses left') has the same words and structure; only the subject differs, which does not justify removing it.
tree:0px15tc00at31s.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 2:248 has the same structure.
tree:0px15tc00at31s.relation: What was left behind: by parents and kin for the heirs, and by the families of Moses and Harun in the Ark.

tree:0h01fpw0brhs4u.why: The three ayat on the rescue from Pharaoh's people are already a card; 19:6 and 40:28 only mention a family.

tree:0qa4f8b1k3wj1b.why: 2:138, 4:125, 5:50 and 41:33 ask 'who is better than', with the interrogative and the comparative. In 18:30 the words are the relative 'whoever does good work', with a verb: a different word in a different structure.
tree:0qa4f8b1k3wj1b.changes: Removed 18:30: a relative and a verb, not the question.
tree:0qa4f8b1k3wj1b.relation: Who is better than: God's colouring, the religion of Ibrahim, God's judgement, one who calls to God.

tree:1m07gcf1bbe1hl.why: The word matter means different things here; the real same-surah pairs are their own cards.

tree:08ogfce0ezdp7s.why: All five use 'of the fruits' with the same partitive sense. 7:130 ('a lessening of the fruits') has the same words and structure; only what is done with the fruits differs, which does not justify removing it.
tree:08ogfce0ezdp7s.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 7:130 has the same phrase in the same sense.
tree:08ogfce0ezdp7s.relation: Fruits: brought out by rain, prayed for by Ibrahim, and taken away from Pharaoh's people.

tree:1jtma7y0fzhpw4.why: 15:82, 16:68, 26:149 and 16:81 share a verb of making or carving followed by 'of the mountains' and the dwelling made: houses, homes, shelters. 16:81 ('He made for you of the mountains shelters') has the same structure; only the subject differs. In 35:27 'and of the mountains are streaks' is a fronted predicate: a different structure.
tree:1jtma7y0fzhpw4.changes: Kept 16:81, which the first agent removed: the same structure. Removed 35:27.
tree:1jtma7y0fzhpw4.relation: Dwellings from the mountains: carved by Thamud, taken by the bee, given as shelter.

tree:09mok911fxb3cd.why: Vows to be among the grateful when in danger (6:63, 7:189, 10:22), each broken after rescue, and the command to be among the grateful (7:144, 39:66).
tree:09mok911fxb3cd.relation: Contrast: gratitude promised in danger and forgotten, and gratitude commanded.

tree:0h08ybm0aysrny.why: All five use 'of the worlds' in the same sense, and 5:20 and 5:115 even share 'anyone of the worlds' with 7:80 and 29:28. The same words and structure; only the subject differs, which does not justify removing them. All rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:0h08ybm0aysrny.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 5:20 and 5:115 have the same phrase and structure.
tree:0h08ybm0aysrny.relation: Unlike anyone of the worlds: Lot's people's deed, Israel's favour, the punishment for denying the table.

tree:18hekzr0wwp4ad.why: A common ending about liars, in unrelated scenes; nothing to learn from the grouping.

tree:0ewvavj1dt7l03.why: 2:34, 38:74, 39:59 and 26:19 say someone was or is 'among the disbelievers': the same predicate. 26:19 (Pharaoh to Moses, 'you are among the ungrateful') has the same structure; only the subject differs. In 71:26 'of the disbelievers' is partitive before 'a single dweller': a different structure. All four rows read on.
tree:0ewvavj1dt7l03.changes: Kept 26:19, which the first agent removed: the same structure. Removed 71:26.
tree:0ewvavj1dt7l03.relation: Among the disbelievers: Iblis twice, the denier on the Day, and Moses in Pharaoh's charge.

tree:1dbxpc816i3elm.why: Two structures: a number 'of the angels' sent as help (3:124, 3:125, 8:9), and a verb taking 'from the angels' an object, females or messengers (17:40, 22:75). The words keep their sense in both, so 17:40 and 22:75 are kept as their own card rather than removed.
tree:1dbxpc816i3elm.changes: Kept the first agent's card and added 17:40 and 22:75 as a second card instead of removing them.
tree:1dbxpc816i3elm.relation: Angels sent as help in thousands, and angels taken as daughters or chosen as messengers.

tree:0tecah40jvx1cq.why: All five use 'from yourselves' in the same sense, 'from among you'. 9:128 (a messenger from yourselves) and 30:28 ('He set forth for you an example from yourselves') have the same words, and 30:28 the same verb-object shape as 16:72; only the subject differs.
tree:0tecah40jvx1cq.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 9:128 and 30:28 have the same phrase in the same sense.
tree:0tecah40jvx1cq.relation: From among yourselves: spouses, a messenger, an example.

tree:0bnf62l09hkbwx.why: The phrase from themselves is used in different senses in five unrelated contexts.

tree:05g0dj5059bf5j.why: 10:108, 17:15, 27:92 and 39:41 use the conditional 'whoever is guided' with its consequence. In 20:135 the particle is interrogative: 'you will know who are the people of the straight path and who is guided'. A different particle, so a different structure.
tree:05g0dj5059bf5j.relation: Whoever is guided is guided for himself; whoever strays strays against himself.

check.why: In 20:135, 'and who is guided' is a question, not the condition 'whoever is guided'. A different structure, so removing it is right.

tree:0kb3fnj0u1d5in.why: Only a common connective about descent from someone is shared; the ayat speak of unrelated people and events, nothing to learn together.

tree:1pu6xow03ubjnk.why: 6:6, 7:43, 10:9 and 18:31 have 'flow beneath them' with the rivers. In 39:16 'and beneath them' is a fronted predicate for 'canopies' of fire, with no verb of flowing: a different structure.
tree:1pu6xow03ubjnk.relation: Rivers flowing beneath them: the destroyed nations' gardens and the gardens of Paradise.

check.why: In 39:16, 'beneath them' is 'and beneath them canopies', not after 'flow'. A different construction, so removing it is right.

tree:13t8qlw1o6z4m6.why: 6:160, 27:89, 27:90 and 28:84 use the conditional 'whoever comes with' a good or evil deed and its recompense. In 28:85 'my Lord knows best who comes with guidance' uses the particle as a relative or interrogative: a different structure.
tree:13t8qlw1o6z4m6.relation: Whoever brings a good deed gets better; whoever brings an evil deed is repaid in kind.

tree:0q04mn11pzav4p.why: The only real pair here (6:70 and 10:4) is already kept in tree:1yo8mkx04s805j; the other rows share a stock phrase on different subjects.

tree:05qdfzc1dikypk.why: Two groups with the same words in the same sense: 'from before them and from behind them' (7:17, 36:9, 41:14), and those left 'behind them' (3:170 those who have not joined them, 4:9 offspring left behind). The words keep their sense, so 3:170 and 4:9 are kept as their own card rather than removed.
tree:05qdfzc1dikypk.changes: Kept the first agent's card and added 3:170 and 4:9 as a second card instead of removing them.
tree:05qdfzc1dikypk.relation: From before and behind them; and those left behind them.

tree:0oap6oz19iyajr.why: 29:61, 31:25, 39:38 and 43:9 ask 'who created the heavens and the earth', with the interrogative particle. In 67:14 'does He who created not know' uses it as a relative, the subject of 'know': a different particle and structure.
tree:0oap6oz19iyajr.relation: If you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will say God.

tree:1fjolaj07mivt1.why: Male or female: the promise that no believer's deed is lost whether man or woman, and 49:13 which says all were created from a male and a female. Useful for memorizers and a clear theme of equal standing.
tree:1fjolaj07mivt1.relation: Men and women stand equal in origin and in the reward for deeds.

tree:0cm7vfr0bqbnnh.why: Bracelets of gold are the adornment of Paradise in several ayat, and in 43:53 Pharaoh mocks Musa because no bracelets of gold were thrown on him. The same rare words set worldly vanity against the reward of the believers.
tree:0cm7vfr0bqbnnh.relation: Contrast: gold Pharaoh demanded as proof, and gold given to the believers in Paradise.

tree:0dy619i0f68f2i.why: The shared words are a common connective used in unrelated contexts; no story, theme or confusion to learn from.

tree:1crluti140ysgw.why: Two structures: the negation 'there is no way' against or for someone (9:91, 42:41, 42:46), and the question 'is there any way' back or out (40:11, 42:44). 42:46 ('he has no way') has the same negation as 42:41; only the subject differs. Rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:1crluti140ysgw.changes: Split into the two groups as the first agent did, but kept 42:46 in the first group instead of removing it.
tree:1crluti140ysgw.relation: No way against the good or the wronged, no way for the one God sends astray; and the wrongdoers asking for a way out.

tree:0yocs9r17nmqdl.why: Only a short common phrase is shared; the ayat speak of different subjects with nothing to compare or confuse.

tree:022kibv02k5f8x.why: The repeated seeking of refuge from evil in Al-Falaq, with the same opening in An-Nas. A memorizer must keep the four evils of 113 in order and not run into 114:4.
tree:022kibv02k5f8x.relation: The two refuge surahs: evils from outside (113) and the whisperer within (114).

tree:0kt377j10yuj37.why: The four ayat with the guidance-for-himself principle are already kept in tree:05g0dj5059bf5j. 5:105 uses the straying word in another structure (those who stray cannot harm you), so this card adds nothing.

tree:0qec7k40gn6jdm.why: Two senses of the same words: 'from your presence' after a verb of leaving (4:81, 47:16), and 'from you' as a source (4:78 this is from you, 8:32 the truth from You, 28:27 it is of your own accord). The sense differs, so the split is right, and the second group keeps its rows.
tree:0qec7k40gn6jdm.changes: Kept the first agent's pair and added 4:78, 8:32 and 28:27 as a second card instead of removing them.
tree:0qec7k40gn6jdm.relation: Leaving the Prophet's presence; and what comes from someone.

tree:0bziwds0dxhuws.why: The shared words are generic (of a book) and the five ayat are on unrelated subjects; nothing to confuse or ponder together.

tree:1ru03m30lf3cff.why: Only a relative pronoun with a negation is shared; the subjects are unrelated and nothing would be confused.

tree:11773t60pk59wy.why: All five name a prophet or Pharaoh 'and whoever was with him' as a joined object. 7:131 ('they took an ill omen from Moses and whoever was with him') has the same words and structure; only the verb's subject differs, which does not justify removing it.
tree:11773t60pk59wy.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 7:131 has the same structure.
tree:11773t60pk59wy.relation: Those with him: saved with Nuh and Musa, drowned with Pharaoh, blamed with Musa.

tree:07r8p1j1mdrrjt.why: Two structures: 'to warn a people to whom no warner came before you' (28:46, 32:3), and 'We sent no warner' to a town or to them (34:34, 43:23, 34:44). 34:44 has the same negation and verb as 34:34; only the subject differs. 34:44 reads on into the next ayah.
tree:07r8p1j1mdrrjt.changes: Split into the two groups as the first agent did, but kept 34:44 in the second group instead of removing it.
tree:07r8p1j1mdrrjt.relation: No warner came before you; and no warner was sent to a town but its affluent rejected him.

tree:10zfmxk0yohity.why: 21:97, 23:63 and 50:22 say 'in heedlessness / a flood of this', with the particle meaning 'of, about'. In 18:24 ('nearer than this') and 43:52 ('better than this') the particle is comparative: a different sense of the particle.
tree:10zfmxk0yohity.changes: Removed 18:24 and 43:52: the particle is comparative.
tree:10zfmxk0yohity.relation: Heedless of this: on the Day they admit it, and now their hearts are flooded by it.

tree:1reufx313rbwyr.why: From behind is shared, but the subjects differ: Ishaq and Yaqub, a screen with the Prophet's wives, God speaking from behind a veil, calls from behind the rooms, fighting from behind walls. A rare phrase alone with different subjects.

tree:0r34rfb1fonimd.why: And of them you eat closes several lists of God's gifts in livestock and fruit (16:5, 23:19, 23:21, 40:79), and in 43:73 the fruit of Paradise. Memorizers must place each closing; the last row sets worldly provision beside Paradise.
tree:0r34rfb1fonimd.relation: Gifts of this world and of Paradise named in the same words.

tree:06ce0231co2ahv.why: All five open 'We know best' followed by the object of knowing. 29:32 ('we know best who is in it') has the same words and structure, with a relative for persons instead of things; only the subject differs, which does not justify removing it.
tree:06ce0231co2ahv.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 29:32 has the same structure.
tree:06ce0231co2ahv.relation: We know best: what the deniers say and describe, and who is in Lot's town.

tree:0lqx9rl0cemn03.why: No soul is burdened beyond its capacity: said in four places with we or God as subject, and in 65:7 as beyond what He gave it. A clear memorizer set and a principle worth pondering.
tree:0lqx9rl0cemn03.relation: God asks of each soul only what it can bear.

tree:0hu8k0c0t8lke0.why: We relate to you: God telling the Prophet the stories of towns, messengers, Yusuf and the cave youths. Similar openings to keep apart, and the purpose of the stories is stated (to make firm your heart).
tree:0hu8k0c0t8lke0.relation: Why the Quran tells stories: to strengthen the Prophet and remind.

tree:1l5c11x0vgvb23.why: Those who believed, emigrated and strove: five places that differ in what follows (in the way of God, with wealth and lives, with you) and in the reward named. A classic memorizer set, and it shows the rank of the emigrants.
tree:1l5c11x0vgvb23.relation: Faith, emigration and striving together earn mercy, true faith and the highest rank.

tree:0kbrt0q0qxtgr8.why: Prophets asking their Lord to grant them: Zakariyya a good offspring, Ibrahim wisdom and a righteous son, Sulayman a kingdom. Similar openings a memorizer must separate, and the prayers show what each prophet sought.
tree:0kbrt0q0qxtgr8.relation: What the prophets asked for: offspring, wisdom, righteous children, a kingdom.

tree:0y5lg4b0ub7nn5.why: God's guidance is the only guidance (2:120, 3:73, 6:71) and that is God's guidance by which He guides whom He wills (6:88, 39:23). Two near-identical pairs plus a variant, a strong memorizer set.
tree:0y5lg4b0ub7nn5.relation: True guidance comes only from God, against the claims of the People of the Book and the idolaters.

tree:10y4ild1rstvdb.why: All five use 'this town' as the object of a verb or genitive. The split separates the command to Bani Israil to enter or dwell in the town (2:58, 7:161) from the town of wrongdoers (4:75, 29:31, 29:34), and keeps every row.
tree:10y4ild1rstvdb.changes: Split into the Bani Israil pair and the town-of-wrongdoers set, as the first agent did.
tree:10y4ild1rstvdb.relation: This town: to be entered with humility, and to be left or destroyed for its wrongdoing.

check.why: The split is right: the Bani Israil command (2:58, 7:161) and the town of wrongdoers (4:75, 29:31, 29:34), with every row kept.

tree:1xcx4y31b5faf1.why: Only divine names at the end of ayat are shared (the Wise, the All-Aware or All-Knowing). The ayat themselves are on different subjects; a stock closing is not enough for a card.

tree:0ohb9jn14cv6fh.why: All five end with 'He is the Most High' followed by a second name (the Great, the Mighty). 2:255, 34:23 and 42:4 have the same words and structure; the second name differs, which is exactly what a memorizer must keep apart. All rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:0ohb9jn14cv6fh.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same closing.
tree:0ohb9jn14cv6fh.relation: He is the Most High: the Great or the Mighty.

tree:1u4bic90yp02u1.why: All five say 'He is the Rich', mostly 'the Rich, the Praised'. 10:68, 31:26 and 35:15 have the same words and structure; only what leads up to them differs, which does not justify removing them. Most rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:1u4bic90yp02u1.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same closing.
tree:1u4bic90yp02u1.relation: God is the Rich, needing no son, no thanks and no one.

tree:1y4izzg16g8heu.why: All five say 'He is the Lord of' with a genitive: the Throne, all things, Sirius. 6:164 and 53:49 have the same words and structure; only what He is Lord of differs, which does not justify removing them. 9:129 and 27:26 read on into the next ayah.
tree:1y4izzg16g8heu.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 6:164 and 53:49 have the same structure.
tree:1y4izzg16g8heu.relation: He is the Lord of the Throne, of all things, of Sirius.

tree:0slfcup19tlj5j.why: Two senses of the particle: 'it is from' God or yourselves (3:37, 3:78, 3:165), and 'he is among' the liars or the truthful (12:26, 12:27). The sense differs, so the split is right, and 12:26 and 12:27 are themselves a close pair that a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:0slfcup19tlj5j.changes: Kept the first agent's card and added 12:26 and 12:27 as a second card instead of removing them.
tree:0slfcup19tlj5j.relation: It is from God or from yourselves; and he is among the liars or the truthful.

tree:05g897119jo1t5.why: Woe to those who: the distorters of scripture, and the deniers from the Day, the Fire and their promised day. 19:37 and 43:65 open identically (the factions differed among themselves) and end differently, a key memorizer pair.
tree:05g897119jo1t5.relation: The threats of woe and what each is tied to.

tree:0ifb6jr0u3bic3.why: The calls to the children of Adam in Al-A'raf right after Adam's story, and the reminder of the covenant in 36:60. Together they show the lessons drawn from Adam and Iblis.
tree:0ifb6jr0u3bic3.relation: After Adam's fall, his children are warned against Satan and told to keep covered and follow the messengers.

tree:0p86umn1qlkviz.why: Those who dispute about God and His signs: three times in Ghafir with different endings, plus 13:13 and 42:35. A memorizer set and a clear theme of arrogance behind the dispute.
tree:0p86umn1qlkviz.relation: Disputing God's signs without authority comes from pride and leaves no escape.

tree:0psz2s70fwn3b1.why: God making something is a common phrase; the objects and subjects (a way for women, good in a disliked thing, no way for disbelievers, filth, light) are unrelated.

tree:0eb6na80kmewok.why: All five use 'comes out from' with the same verb and sense. 4:100 (whoever goes out from his house), 16:69 (drink comes out from their bellies) and 86:7 (comes out from between the backbone and ribs) have the same words and structure; only the subject differs.
tree:0eb6na80kmewok.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same verb in the same sense.
tree:0eb6na80kmewok.relation: What comes out from within: rain from clouds, drink from bees, a person from home, water from the loins.

tree:1px4hgl1sh28ef.why: Those who fear their Lord, three times with 'unseen' (21:49, 35:18, 67:12) and twice without. Easy to confuse, and the set shows what fear of the unseen brings: the warning benefits them, and they get forgiveness.
tree:1px4hgl1sh28ef.relation: Fearing God unseen is the mark of those who benefit from the reminder.

tree:17vrgwj0m8r6qf.why: Have they not seen: the shadows prostrating, the birds held in the sky (16:79 and 67:19, nearly the same), the plants of the earth, the sky and earth around them. A memorizer set calling to look at creation.
tree:17vrgwj0m8r6qf.relation: Invitations to look at creation: none holds the birds up but God.

tree:0nvcz1c02i8f00.why: Have they not seen that We: reduce the land, made night and day, made a safe sanctuary, drive water to dry land, created livestock. Same opening with different signs, a good memorizer and pondering set.
tree:0nvcz1c02i8f00.relation: Signs of God's care that people see and still ignore.

tree:1jn2sa205xdfc8.why: The shared words are only 'whom He wills, and He is' followed by different divine names, on unrelated subjects. A stock closing pattern.

tree:13gqo430gtxpcj.why: Thus God leads astray: whom He wills (14:4, 74:31, near-identical wording), the wrongdoers, the excessive doubter, the disbelievers. The set shows whom God leaves to stray, a point worth pondering.
tree:13gqo430gtxpcj.relation: God leads astray those who chose wrongdoing, excess and doubt.

tree:09crx2u072cypu.why: Two structures with the same words: 'God will never forgive them' (9:80, 47:34, 63:6), and the hope 'that God forgive you' (12:92, 24:22). The split keeps every row.
tree:09crx2u072cypu.changes: Split into the never-forgiven set and the forgive-to-be-forgiven pair, as the first agent did.
tree:09crx2u072cypu.relation: God will never forgive the hypocrites; and forgive others so God forgives you.

tree:1ass6qp0hpdzc1.why: All five say 'does what' followed by a verb. 12:32 ('if he does not do what I order him') has the same verb and relative; only the subject differs, and the contrast between God doing what He wills and Yusuf refusing an order is worth keeping. Rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:1ass6qp0hpdzc1.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 12:32 has the same structure.
tree:1ass6qp0hpdzc1.relation: God does what He wills or intends; Yusuf would not do what he was ordered.

tree:1rvlikq0s32muq.why: All five use 'he has (not)' with the verb 'be', 'to him' and a noun. 4:11 ('if he has no child') has the same words and structure as 17:111 ('He has no partner'); 4:85 ('he has a share') is the same structure, positive. Only the subject differs.
tree:1rvlikq0s32muq.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 4:11 and 4:85 have the same structure.
tree:1rvlikq0s32muq.relation: What one has or has not: God no partner and no equal; the deceased no child; the intercessor a share.

tree:03oh6vg1jkgflo.why: Then He will inform them of what they did: with 'used to do' in three forms. Easy to confuse, and each ties God's knowledge to the final account.
tree:03oh6vg1jkgflo.relation: Every deed, forgotten by people, is counted and shown on the Day.

tree:06sr55r1gzxg35.why: The Day of Sorting in five places: the day you denied, the appointed time for all, what will make you know, gathered with the first ones. Short close wordings that a memorizer mixes.
tree:06sr55r1gzxg35.relation: The Day of Judgment named as the day of separation and its appointed time.

tree:1dq9s510aq3np7.why: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day: 2:62 and 5:69 nearly identical (with word-order and ending differences), and the same phrase defining piety, the builders of mosques and the strivers. A core memorizer set.
tree:1dq9s510aq3np7.relation: Faith in God and the Last Day as the measure of righteousness, beyond lineage or service at the Sanctuary.

tree:07p59r90mgw1wp.why: Two structures: the demand 'why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord' (6:37, 10:20, 13:7, 13:27), and 'no sign of the signs of their Lord comes to them but they turn away' (6:4, 36:46). The words keep their sense, so 6:4 and 36:46 form their own card rather than being removed. Both read on.
tree:07p59r90mgw1wp.changes: Kept the first agent's card and added 6:4 and 36:46 as a second card instead of removing them.
tree:07p59r90mgw1wp.relation: The deniers demand a sign, and turn away from every sign that comes.

tree:0dmxh2j0st9fid.why: Make for me: Zakariyya asking for a sign (3:41 and 19:10, nearly identical, three days against three nights), and prophets asking for authority, a helper and an honoured name. Pharaoh uses the same words to order a tower to reach Musa's God.
tree:0dmxh2j0st9fid.relation: Contrast: prophets ask God to make things for them; Pharaoh asks Haman.

check.why: Keep is right: 'make for me' as a request, with the near-twin 3:41 and 19:10 and Pharaoh's order in the same words as a contrast.

tree:1ftoon00u0367w.why: 2:285, 7:80, 9:6, 29:28 and 33:40 use 'any one of' a group with the partitive particle: of His messengers, of the worlds, of the idolaters, of your men. The same words and structure; only the group differs. In 35:41 'anyone after Him' uses the particle in a temporal sense, a different sense. 7:80 and 29:28 read on.
tree:1ftoon00u0367w.changes: Kept 2:285, 9:6 and 33:40, which the first agent removed: the same partitive structure. Removed 35:41: a temporal sense.
tree:1ftoon00u0367w.relation: Any one of: the messengers, the worlds, the idolaters, your men.

tree:10zww0512xsxmf.why: All six open '(and) when ... said' with a feminine subject. 7:164 ('when a community of them said') and 33:13 ('when a party of them said') have the same words and structure; only the speaker differs, which does not justify removing them.
tree:10zww0512xsxmf.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 7:164 and 33:13 have the same structure.
tree:10zww0512xsxmf.relation: When she or they said: the wife of Imran, the angels to Maryam, Pharaoh's wife, a community, a party.

tree:1de297g1a3z81o.why: All six open 'and when We said' followed by the address. 2:58 ('enter this town') and 17:60 ('to you: your Lord encompasses the people') have the same words and structure; only what was said differs, which does not justify removing them. 20:116 reads on into the next ayah.
tree:1de297g1a3z81o.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 2:58 and 17:60 have the same structure.
tree:1de297g1a3z81o.relation: When We said: to the angels to prostrate, to Israel to enter the town, to the Prophet that his Lord encompasses the people.

tree:1batbim13wylm4.why: All six say 'We sent Nuh'. 57:26 ('We sent Nuh and Ibrahim') has the same verb and object; only what follows differs, which does not justify removing it.
tree:1batbim13wylm4.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 57:26 has the same words and structure.
tree:1batbim13wylm4.relation: We sent Nuh: to his people five times, and with Ibrahim once.

tree:1ygbgbb13vmzg5.why: Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq: lists of prophets in faith declarations (2:136 and 3:84 nearly identical with small differences), Yaqub's sons' answer, and Ibrahim's thanks for his two sons. A core memorizer set.
tree:1ygbgbb13vmzg5.relation: One line of prophets, all Muslims, against claims they were Jews or Christians.

tree:06s65uv0pgu033.why: Stronger than them in power (four places) or in might (two places): past nations stronger than the Quraysh were destroyed. Classic memorizer set with a clear lesson.
tree:06s65uv0pgu033.relation: Strength did not save the nations before.

tree:0t5jsqa02ohn6g.why: All six use 'the companions of Hellfire' in the same sense. 9:113 ('it has become clear to them that they are the companions of Hellfire') uses it as a predicate like 5:10; 2:119 ('you will not be asked about the companions of Hellfire') keeps the same sense. Rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:0t5jsqa02ohn6g.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 2:119 and 9:113 use the phrase in the same sense.
tree:0t5jsqa02ohn6g.relation: The companions of Hellfire: the deniers, the obstructers, the idolaters not to be prayed for.

tree:1ckahkb1mm8aod.why: Obey God and obey the Messenger: six places with different continuations (those in authority, beware, if you turn away, do not void your deeds). A core memorizer set on the duty of obedience.
tree:1ckahkb1mm8aod.relation: Obedience to the Messenger joined to obedience to God, and the Messenger's only duty is to convey.

tree:1mtpnuo0fzcm56.why: He has prepared for them: gardens and a noble reward for the believers, humiliating punishment, blazing fire and Hell for the deniers. The same verb sets the two ends side by side.
tree:1mtpnuo0fzcm56.relation: Contrast: what God has prepared for the foremost believers and for those who harm Him and His Messenger.

tree:0n8c7z40b6zgfe.why: A plain comparison (greater than) in unrelated contexts: fighting in the sacred month, wine, the demand to see God, creation, signs. Nothing shared in meaning.

tree:1d18dlj06jqsiv.why: The Messenger's only duty is to convey: six places, four with 'clear', with different lead-ins. A memorizer set and a principle worth pondering.
tree:1d18dlj06jqsiv.relation: Guidance is God's; the messengers only deliver the message.

tree:0z1wdmc0i0k12i.why: Two structures with the same opening 'surely they': with the separating pronoun and a definite predicate, 'they are the corrupters / fools / liars' (2:12, 2:13, 58:18), and with a verb or phrase (11:5 they fold their breasts, 37:151 they say from their lie, 41:54 they are in doubt). The rows keep their words, so the second group is a card of its own.
tree:0z1wdmc0i0k12i.changes: Kept the first agent's card and added 11:5, 37:151 and 41:54 as a second card instead of removing them.
tree:0z1wdmc0i0k12i.relation: Surely they: the hypocrites named for what they are, and the deniers for what they do.

tree:0bjaods0tg1l1o.why: The refrain of Ash-Shu'ara: each prophet's brother calls 'will you not fear God', I am a trustworthy messenger, I ask no reward. Shu'ayb lacks 'their brother', and Ilyas in 37:124 shares the call. A key memorizer set showing all prophets with one message.
tree:0bjaods0tg1l1o.relation: Every prophet came with the same call and the same refusal of payment.

tree:0crx6qd1iskkdl.why: No sign, messenger or reminder comes to them but they turn away or mock: six places differing in a word or two (sign, messenger, reminder, prophet; turning away or mocking). A strong memorizer set.
tree:0crx6qd1iskkdl.relation: The constant answer of deniers to every sign and messenger.

tree:0eav5lq0xmamhk.why: I am only a warner: clear, a bringer of good news, to you. Six places where the Prophet or Nuh describe their role, with small differences a memorizer must keep.
tree:0eav5lq0xmamhk.relation: The messenger is a warner, not a madman or one who knows the unseen.

tree:0oi2wnm1cg5lik.why: Three pairs with the same shape, the earth closing a clause and 'and God' opening an attribute: God knows what is in the heavens and the earth (3:29, 49:16), His is the kingdom (3:189, 85:9), and 'God is aware / sees what you do' (3:180, 49:18). 3:180 and 49:18 have the same structure and form their own pair. Rows read on.
tree:0oi2wnm1cg5lik.changes: Split into the two pairs as the first agent did, and kept 3:180 and 49:18 as a third pair instead of removing them.
tree:0oi2wnm1cg5lik.relation: The heavens and the earth, then God's power, knowledge and sight.

tree:0g3whfi1vzorz4.why: He is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful, closing the repentance of Adam, of Bani Israil after the calf, Ibrahim's prayer, those who repent and make amends, and the three who stayed behind. The lead-ins differ, a memorizer set, and the stories share the theme.
tree:0g3whfi1vzorz4.relation: Repentance accepted across the stories, from Adam to the three left behind.

tree:09qah1d1p9b1cf.why: The Home of the Hereafter: for whom it is (not exclusively for a people, for the God-fearing, for those who seek no arrogance), seeking it over this life, and the real life it holds. The ayat show what earns it.
tree:09qah1d1p9b1cf.relation: The Hereafter is the true life and belongs to the humble and God-fearing.

check.why: Keep is right: 'the Home of the Hereafter', in rows that share one theme, who earns it.

tree:0ghkucw0d80qt8.why: Good in this world: asked for in prayer (2:201, 7:156) and promised to those who do good and emigrate (16:30, 16:41, 39:10), with different second halves about the Hereafter. A memorizer set.
tree:0ghkucw0d80qt8.relation: Good in this world, and something better in the Hereafter.

tree:1h695171rf5pi7.why: In 9:33, 48:28, 61:9, 25:48 and 35:9 the verb is active, 'He who sent' the Messenger or the winds. In 26:27 it is passive, 'your messenger who was sent to you': a different voice, so a different structure. The split into the messenger set and the winds pair keeps the rest.
tree:1h695171rf5pi7.changes: Removed 26:27: the verb is passive. Split into the messenger set and the winds pair.
tree:1h695171rf5pi7.relation: He who sent His Messenger with guidance, and He who sent the winds with rain.

tree:0p47owe05qedyy.why: This is what you used to: be promised (said to the believers), deny, hasten, call for (said to the deniers). The same frame gives the joy of one group and the rebuke of the other.
tree:0p47owe05qedyy.relation: Contrast: the promised day welcomed by believers and the denied punishment faced by deniers.

tree:0lune3t1tyemdb.why: Those who were patient: 16:42 and 29:59 identical (and rely on their Lord), and others naming the reward of patience. A memorizer set on one theme.
tree:0lune3t1tyemdb.relation: What patience earns: forgiveness, the final home, the best reward.

tree:1jhde0n0e5wud9.why: All six use 'those who believe' with what they believe in: the unseen, what was sent down, Our signs, the Hereafter, God and the Last Day. The same words and structure throughout; cutting to one pair because of subject is not allowed.
tree:1jhde0n0e5wud9.changes: Reverted to the original rows: all rows share the same phrase.
tree:1jhde0n0e5wud9.relation: Those who believe, and in what: the unseen, the revelation, the signs, the Hereafter, God and His Messenger.

tree:1jyhoa000zwqhi.why: Those who spend their wealth: in God's way, seeking His pleasure, night and day, in ease and hardship, set against those who spend to be seen (4:38). Similar openings for a memorizer, and the set shows what makes spending accepted.
tree:1jyhoa000zwqhi.relation: Contrast: spending for God's sake multiplied, spending for show joined to Satan.

tree:1ve50is0uwv9sm.why: The Most Merciful, the Merciful is the basmala and a pair of divine names; nothing to tell apart or ponder across these places, and 1:1 with 1:3 is already a book card.

tree:0xh1f0e0r3t7em.why: The strong set (do not follow Satan's steps, he is a clear enemy) is already kept in cmp:1rm4ewm1v4bask and tree:1fbag1f0p0iwul; 28:15 is Musa's own words in his story. This card repeats them.

tree:15junsi04ctsk8.why: All six end with 'the painful punishment' in the same sense. 15:50, 37:38 and 51:37 have the same words; the frame differs (My punishment is, you will taste, those who fear), which does not justify removing them. All rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:15junsi04ctsk8.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same phrase.
tree:15junsi04ctsk8.relation: The painful punishment: until they see it, God's own, to be tasted, feared.

tree:0wwfj4b0g93xm3.why: All six end with 'the Mighty, the All-Knowing'. 27:78, 40:2 and 43:9 have the same names in the same structure; the frame differs (He is, from God, created them), which does not justify removing them. All rows read on into the next ayah.
tree:0wwfj4b0g93xm3.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same closing.
tree:0wwfj4b0g93xm3.relation: The Mighty, the All-Knowing: who measures the cosmos, judges, sends the Book, and created the heavens.

tree:0aec80n0ocpunj.why: Two structures: 'the Book' as a subject followed by a negation (2:2, 10:37, 32:2 no doubt in it; 18:49 it leaves nothing small or great), and the vocative 'People of the Book, do not exceed' (4:171, 5:77). 18:49 has the same structure as 2:2; only the book differs. 10:37 and 32:2 read on.
tree:0aec80n0ocpunj.changes: Split into the two sets as the first agent did, but kept 18:49 in the first set instead of removing it.
tree:0aec80n0ocpunj.relation: A Book with no doubt in it and a record that leaves nothing out; and the People of the Book told not to exceed bounds.

tree:1k7ihyw1yjehwq.why: Only God's name followed by 'those' is shared; the ayat are about different people and themes.

tree:0anx5k00zlwuzu.why: 22:3, 22:8, 31:20, 40:35 and 40:56 share 'disputes about God (or God's signs) without' knowledge or authority. In 31:6 'God' is the genitive of 'the way of God' after 'to mislead from', and 'without knowledge' belongs to another verb: a different governing word and structure. 22:8 and 31:20 read on.
tree:0anx5k00zlwuzu.relation: Those who dispute about God and His signs without knowledge or authority.

tree:0awmz110s1qomh.why: God is self-sufficient: forbearing, praiseworthy, free of need of the worlds or of you. Each ends a call to give, perform Hajj or be grateful. A memorizer set with a clear lesson.
tree:0awmz110s1qomh.relation: God needs nothing from His servants; their charity, thanks and worship benefit them.

tree:0v3b2zu0kblsr4.why: Two structures: God's name closing a phrase, then a prohibition 'so do not' (2:187 do not approach them, 2:229 do not transgress them, 16:1 do not hasten it), and a conditional whose answer is 'there is no' (3:160 no victor over you, 7:186 no guide for him). In 7:99 'so none feels safe ... except' is a negated statement with an exception: a different structure.
tree:0v3b2zu0kblsr4.changes: Kept 16:1 with the limits pair, and kept 3:160 and 7:186 as their own card instead of removing them. Removed 7:99.
tree:0v3b2zu0kblsr4.relation: God's limits and command, not to be approached or hastened; and whom God helps or leaves astray, none can overcome or guide.

tree:02q7suw1bg9ak4.why: 'God has' and 'they have strayed' in unrelated contexts (Talut, killing children, Qarun, the arrogant in Hell). Nothing shared in meaning.

tree:09ty1j400nx8eu.why: The east and the west belong to God: the qibla verses (2:115, 2:142, 2:177) and the Lord of the east and west (26:28, 70:40, 73:9). A memorizer set and a lesson that direction is God's.
tree:09ty1j400nx8eu.relation: God owns every direction; righteousness is not in facing east or west.

tree:1d0det50y28jd7.why: All six read 'the people, but most people / most of them do not' followed by a verb. 40:57 has the same words and structure; it ends 'do not know' instead of 'do not give thanks', exactly the kind of ending a memorizer must keep apart. Its subject differs, which does not justify removing it. Rows read on.
tree:1d0det50y28jd7.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 40:57 has the same structure.
tree:1d0det50y28jd7.relation: Most people do not give thanks for God's bounty, and do not know the greatness of His creation.

tree:1bftk0z1r4odyf.why: 'One to another' describes unrelated scenes (hypocrites in private, spouses, devils whispering, the weak and the arrogant). Nothing to learn together.

tree:0ixfbce1d9tsv0.why: All six use 'to your Lord' with the same preposition and sense, toward Him. 7:164 (an excuse to your Lord) and 39:54 (turn to your Lord) keep the sense; the different governing word is what a memorizer must keep apart from 'then to your Lord is your return'. Rows read on.
tree:0ixfbce1d9tsv0.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 7:164 and 39:54 use the phrase in the same sense.
tree:0ixfbce1d9tsv0.relation: To your Lord: the return, an excuse, and turning in repentance.

tree:06yz80p0b6qbtp.why: Two structures: 'what was sent down / revealed to you and what' (2:4, 4:60, 4:162, 42:13), a relative pair, and 'We reveal it to you, and you were not' with them (3:44, 12:102), where 'and not' is a negation. 42:13 ('what We revealed to you and what We enjoined') has the same structure as 2:4; only the subject differs.
tree:06yz80p0b6qbtp.changes: Split into the two sets as the first agent did, but kept 42:13 in the first set instead of removing it.
tree:06yz80p0b6qbtp.relation: What was revealed to you and to those before; and news of the unseen you did not witness.

tree:0731njx0ie0ga1.why: 2:6, 26:136, 36:10 and 63:6 use 'or not' after 'it is the same to them whether': the paired alternative. In 23:69 and 53:36 the particle opens a question, 'or have they not known / been told': a different use of the particle, so a different structure. 2:6 and 36:10 read on.
tree:0731njx0ie0ga1.changes: Removed 23:69 and 53:36: the particle opens a question there.
tree:0731njx0ie0ga1.relation: It is the same to them whether you warn, preach or seek forgiveness, or not.

tree:0h9346i18as0um.why: 3:10, 3:116, 9:55 and 58:17 say 'their wealth nor their children', with 'nor' joining a second noun. In 4:2 and 4:6 'and do not' opens a new prohibition after 'their wealth': a different structure.
tree:0h9346i18as0um.changes: Removed 4:2 and 4:6: 'and do not' begins a new prohibition there.
tree:0h9346i18as0um.relation: Their wealth and children will not avail them, and are not to be admired.

check.why: In 4:2 and 4:6, 'their wealth, and do not' goes on to a prohibition, not 'nor their children'. A different structure, so removing them is right.

tree:03m2aih0o3ewh9.why: All six say 'that I be' followed by what. 2:67 (I seek refuge in God from being among the ignorant) and 5:31 (unable to be like this crow) have the same words and structure; the governing verb differs, which is what a memorizer must keep apart from 'I was commanded to be'. Subject differences do not justify removing them.
tree:03m2aih0o3ewh9.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 2:67 and 5:31 have the same structure.
tree:03m2aih0o3ewh9.relation: What one is to be: among the Muslims and believers by command; never among the ignorant; even like the crow.

tree:0jczwud01wlgj7.why: Two structures: 'except that X come to them, or Y comes' (6:158, 16:33, 18:55), and the Hour or overwhelming punishment coming on them suddenly (12:107, 43:66, 47:18). 18:55 ('except that the way of the ancients come to them, or the punishment') has the same structure as 6:158; only the subject differs.
tree:0jczwud01wlgj7.changes: Split into the two groups as the first agent did, but kept 18:55 in the first group instead of removing it.
tree:0jczwud01wlgj7.relation: What they wait for: the angels, the command, the fate of the ancients; and the Hour coming suddenly.

tree:0oaxnm50r4fiwv.why: 'That it be' is a grammatical frame across unrelated subjects; the trade pair (2:282, 4:29) has its own card.

tree:16geeit0r13jkl.why: 'If you fear' opens unrelated rulings (divorce, prayer in fear, orphans, marital discord, travel, poverty). Nothing to compare.

tree:1jsdtsl1vhz0xj.why: All six use 'that to God belongs' followed by what. 8:41 ('that to God belongs a fifth of it') has the same words and structure; only what belongs differs, which does not justify removing it.
tree:1jsdtsl1vhz0xj.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 8:41 has the same structure.
tree:1jsdtsl1vhz0xj.relation: To God belongs all in the heavens and the earth, and a fifth of the spoils.

tree:1dhoj831tyi2k5.why: The refrain of As-Saffat: thus We reward the doers of good, after each prophet, against 'thus We deal with the criminals' (37:34). The run-ons show which prophet is called a believing servant. A key memorizer set.
tree:1dhoj831tyi2k5.relation: Contrast: the same 'thus We' for the reward of prophets and the punishment of criminals.

tree:1pagndw001lc7c.why: In 3:199, 5:68, 7:3, 29:46 and 39:55 the verb is passive, 'what was sent down to you'. In 6:114 it is active, 'He who sent down to you the Book': a different voice, so a different structure.
tree:1pagndw001lc7c.relation: What was sent down to you from your Lord: to follow, to establish, to believe in.

tree:1vh5qqb0jqz0ql.why: 15:22, 23:18, 25:48, 31:10 and 78:14 say 'We sent down from' the sky or the clouds water, with the particle meaning 'from'. In 2:159 'what We sent down of the clear proofs' uses the particle to explain what was sent: a different sense of the particle.
tree:1vh5qqb0jqz0ql.changes: Removed 2:159: a different sense of the particle.
tree:1vh5qqb0jqz0ql.relation: We sent down water from the sky: fertilising, measured, pure, bringing pairs, pouring.

check.why: In 2:159, 'what We sent down of the clear proofs' is relative with a partitive min, not 'sent down from the sky'. A different word sense, so removing it is right.

tree:1djzav00ezv8as.why: Spend from what We provided: 13:22 and 35:29 identical (secretly and openly), with calls to spend before the Day, and the deniers' answer in 36:47 (shall we feed those God could feed). A memorizer set and a contrast.
tree:1djzav00ezv8as.relation: Contrast: believers spend from God's provision; deniers mock the call to feed the poor.

tree:06hnasw0azr0n0.why: All six say 'you are among' a group. 28:31 (Musa: you are among the safe) and 39:8 (you are among the companions of the Fire) have the same words and structure; only the one addressed differs, which does not justify removing them. Several rows read on.
tree:06hnasw0azr0n0.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 28:31 and 39:8 have the same structure.
tree:06hnasw0azr0n0.relation: You are among: the abased and those granted respite (Iblis), the safe (Musa), the companions of the Fire.

tree:0bde5o00tlcz9u.why: 3:18, 10:90, 16:2, 21:25 and 47:19 say 'that there is no god but', where the particle denies a whole category. In 7:148 'that it does not speak to them' the particle negates a verb: a different use of the particle and a different structure.
tree:0bde5o00tlcz9u.changes: Removed 7:148: the particle negates a verb there.
tree:0bde5o00tlcz9u.relation: That there is no god but He: God's testimony, the revelation to the messengers, the command to know it, Pharaoh's late confession.

tree:01er4ea00epyym.why: All six say 'I am with you' with the same words and structure. In 5:12 God says it as a promise of support; in the others the messengers say it while waiting. The difference is the speaker and the subject, which does not justify removing it. Rows read on.
tree:01er4ea00epyym.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 5:12 has the same words and structure.
tree:01er4ea00epyym.relation: 'I am with you': God's promise to Israel, and the messengers waiting with the deniers.

tree:0sisdh31gsxmfr.why: All six ask 'how can there be for' someone something. 2:247 ('how can he have kingship over us') has the same words and structure as 6:101 ('how can He have a son'); only the subject differs, which does not justify removing it.
tree:0sisdh31gsxmfr.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 2:247 has the same structure.
tree:0sisdh31gsxmfr.relation: How can there be: a son for the aged and the virgin, a son for God, kingship for Talut.

tree:1hwvijk1lvxk9e.why: All six use 'or what' with a relative clause, and 24:61 even shares the verb 'possess' ('or what you possess the keys of'). 6:146 ('or what is mixed with bone') is the same particle and relative; only the subject differs. Rows read on.
tree:1hwvijk1lvxk9e.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 6:146 and 24:61 have the same structure.
tree:1hwvijk1lvxk9e.relation: Or what is possessed: right hands, keys, and fat mixed with bone.

tree:1edxeg60uxdm2u.why: It was revealed to me in unrelated statements (the Quran as warning, false claimants, food rulings, Nuh, the jinn). The shared verb is common.

tree:1bs6dqt0naxqzt.why: What was revealed to you: follow it, recite it, hold fast to it. 18:27 and 29:45 differ in 'from the Book of your Lord' and 'from the Book'. A memorizer set on the Prophet's duty to the revelation.
tree:1bs6dqt0naxqzt.relation: Hold to the revelation, recite it, follow it.

tree:0mty4t11d52b03.why: All six use 'allies besides' with the same words and sense. 17:97 ('you will not find for them allies besides Him') has the same structure; only the verb (find instead of take) differs, which is what a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:0mty4t11d52b03.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 17:97 has the same phrase.
tree:0mty4t11d52b03.relation: Allies besides God or the believers: taken by some, not found by those He sends astray.

tree:1vv0mp81nt78mo.why: And of the Hereafter they are certain (2:4, 27:3, 31:4) against and of the Hereafter they are disbelievers (11:19, 12:37, 41:7). Same frame, opposite ends.
tree:1vv0mp81nt78mo.relation: Contrast: certainty of the Hereafter marks the guided; denying it marks those who block God's way.

tree:0wnll7m0tgx1qm.why: Believe in God and His messengers: 4:150 and 4:152 contrast those who divide between the messengers with those who do not, and 57:19 and 57:21 promise their reward. A memorizer set with a contrast.
tree:0wnll7m0tgx1qm.relation: Contrast: faith in some messengers only, and faith in all of them.

tree:1t6vvpb1kztmon.why: All six say 'believe in God and what' was sent down or came. 8:41 ('if you believe in God and what We sent down to Our servant') has the same words and structure; only the subject differs, which does not justify removing it.
tree:1t6vvpb1kztmon.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 8:41 has the same structure.
tree:1t6vvpb1kztmon.relation: Believing in God and what was sent down: the creed, the faithful of the People of the Book, and the condition on the spoils.

tree:0soimc71gc7pc5.why: 'The signs of their Lord' is a common phrase; the rows mix destroyed nations and praised believers with no shared sentence to learn.

tree:1ie41oj1r0ue0x.why: I am free of what you associate / do / commit: Ibrahim, Hud and the Prophet disowning their people's deeds. Endings differ by one word, a memorizer set and a lesson in disavowal.
tree:1ie41oj1r0ue0x.relation: The messengers disown shirk and sin, not the people.

tree:1kvoiom1qbjaly.why: A human like you: said by messengers of themselves (14:11, 18:110, 41:6) and by deniers as an accusation (21:3, 23:24, 23:33). 18:110 and 41:6 nearly identical.
tree:1kvoiom1qbjaly.relation: Contrast: the messengers' humble claim and the deniers' reason for rejection, in the same words.

tree:0ua15kt0276wvz.why: All six use 'some of you to others' in the same sense. 25:20 (a trial to one another), 34:42 (no benefit to one another) and 49:2 (loud to one another) have the same words and structure; only what passes between them differs. Rows read on.
tree:0ua15kt0276wvz.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same phrase.
tree:0ua15kt0276wvz.relation: Some of you to others: enemies, a trial, no help, loud speech.

tree:0dpbkei014w24e.why: 'With what they did not' in unrelated contexts (praise for what they did not do, the Samiri, the hoopoe, greetings). No shared meaning.

tree:11ch2zl1y4gcf5.why: 7:71, 12:40, 53:23, 7:80 and 29:28 share a negation, then 'with it', then the particle introducing an indefinite: 'God sent down no authority for it', 'none preceded you in it'. 7:80 and 29:28 have the same structure and cannot be removed because another card holds them. In 2:258 'bring it from the west' uses the particle for a place: a different sense.
tree:11ch2zl1y4gcf5.changes: Kept 7:80 and 29:28 with their run-ons, which the first agent removed. Removed 2:258: a different sense of the particle.
tree:11ch2zl1y4gcf5.relation: None before: no authority sent for the idols, and no one before Lut's people in their deed.

tree:1d4mj1f0ds11gv.why: All six use 'between me and you' in the same sense. 6:58 ('the matter would have been decided between me and you') has the same words; the frame differs, which is what a memorizer must keep apart from 'God is witness between me and you'.
tree:1d4mj1f0ds11gv.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 6:58 has the same phrase.
tree:1d4mj1f0ds11gv.relation: Between me and you: God as witness, and the matter decided.

tree:0k5hkqx1sapi1b.why: Worship none but God / none but Him: the call of Nuh, Hud, Yusuf and the messengers, and the command in 17:23. 11:26 and 46:21 nearly identical. A memorizer set on the one message.
tree:0k5hkqx1sapi1b.relation: Every messenger began with the same call to worship God alone.

tree:1udh20z0iao2aj.why: 'Then did not' in unrelated rulings and parables; nothing shared in meaning.

tree:14mnfly192fjy2.why: When Our command came: the refrain of Hud's stories (Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut, Shu'ayb) with 23:27. 11:58 and 11:94 open with 'and when', 11:66 and 11:82 with 'so when'. A key memorizer set.
tree:14mnfly192fjy2.relation: The same moment in every story: the command comes, the believers are saved, the deniers seized.

tree:0qdsfe40yl64i0.why: All six say 'has come to you of' with the particle introducing what came: knowledge, the truth, the news of the messengers. 6:34 has the same words and structure; only what came differs, which does not justify removing it.
tree:0qdsfe40yl64i0.changes: Reverted to the original rows: 6:34 has the same structure.
tree:0qdsfe40yl64i0.relation: What has come to you: knowledge, the truth, the news of the messengers.

tree:0y43nak1tuc3s2.why: All six have 'all' closing a phrase and 'then' opening the next step. 2:29, 11:55 and 70:14 have the same words and structure; only the subject differs, which does not justify removing them.
tree:0y43nak1tuc3s2.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same structure.
tree:0y43nak1tuc3s2.relation: All of them, then: gathered and questioned, created then the heaven formed, plot then no respite, ransom then rescue.

tree:04wuymj0hhxlgr.why: All six end with 'until a time' in the same sense. 12:35, 23:25, 23:54 and 51:43 have the same words and structure; only the verb before differs (imprison, wait, leave, enjoy), which is what a memorizer must keep apart. All rows read on.
tree:04wuymj0hhxlgr.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other four have the same phrase.
tree:04wuymj0hhxlgr.relation: Until a time: imprisoned, waited on, left in their heedlessness, given enjoyment, turned away from.

tree:0553qnv1r4o9eb.why: All six use 'God has forbidden / made sacred' with the same verb, voice and sense. 5:72 (God has forbidden him the Garden), 9:29 and 9:37 (what God forbade) have the same words and structure; only the object differs, which does not justify removing them.
tree:0553qnv1r4o9eb.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same verb in the same sense.
tree:0553qnv1r4o9eb.relation: What God has made sacred or forbidden: the soul, the Garden to the associator, the sacred months.

tree:0wjnfgq05ten66.why: Man was created: weak, from a drop, of haste, from clay like pottery, from a clinging clot. Short ayat a memorizer mixes, and together a portrait of man's nature and origin.
tree:0wjnfgq05ten66.relation: What man is made of and made with: weakness, haste, clay and a clot.

tree:1ovr4un04nxojd.why: We created man: from clay, from an extract of clay, from a mingled drop, in toil, in the best form, and We know what his soul whispers. A memorizer set and a theme of man's creation.
tree:1ovr4un04nxojd.relation: Man's origin and state, from clay to the best form.

tree:1yamuea0mb5bv8.why: 'Better or' is a common rhetorical frame; the comparisons are unrelated (a mosque, gods, Paradise, Tubba's people). No shared sentence to confuse.

tree:1cbgoey0dtjqj4.why: All six open 'that is for what'. The split separates 'that is because they disobeyed and transgressed' (2:61, 3:112, 5:78) from 'that is for what your hands sent forth, and God is not unjust' (3:182, 8:51, 22:10), and keeps every row with its run-on.
tree:1cbgoey0dtjqj4.changes: Split into the two sets, as the first agent did.
tree:1cbgoey0dtjqj4.relation: The reason for their punishment: their disobedience, and what their hands sent forth.

tree:0njqpl80l57dy2.why: Two structures: 'what is below that, for whom He wills' (4:48, 4:116), where 'that' is governed by 'below', and 'that is for whoever' (14:14, 98:8, 2:196, 4:25), where 'that' is the subject. 2:196 and 4:25 have the same structure as 14:14, and 4:25 even shares 'whoever fears' with 98:8; their rulings do not justify removing them.
tree:0njqpl80l57dy2.changes: Split into the two groups as the first agent did, but kept 2:196 and 4:25 in the second group instead of removing them.
tree:0njqpl80l57dy2.relation: God forgives what is below shirk for whom He wills; and each reward or ruling is for whoever meets its condition.

tree:1p2rdtp1dnfa2n.why: Lord of the Throne: the Mighty (9:129, 23:86, 27:26), the Noble (23:116), and 'exalted above what they describe' in 21:22 and 43:82. A memorizer set on God's lordship against shirk.
tree:1p2rdtp1dnfa2n.relation: God, Lord of the Throne, above every partner they ascribe.

tree:1n2l9f90t87dnp.why: 'Your Lord, and not' joins words from unrelated ayat (qibla, stones of Lut, the destroyed, Khidr, Ad-Duha). Nothing in common.

tree:1v4votj1dl0mln.why: Only the address 'our Lord, You' is shared; each prayer asks or states something different. No line to confuse and no common theme beyond prayer.

tree:1vzftjn11vtgjt.why: God is my Lord and your Lord: Isa's words in four places (3:51, 19:36, 43:64 nearly identical, 5:72, 5:117) and Hud's in 11:56. Key memorizer set: Isa calls to worship God, not himself.
tree:1vzftjn11vtgjt.relation: Isa himself declared God his Lord, against those who deified him.

tree:1egnjis1851wmw.why: All six say 'a messenger from' with the source. 2:101 (from God), 9:128 (from yourselves) and 98:2 (from God) have the same words and structure; only the speaker differs, which does not justify removing them. 7:61, 7:67 and 7:104 read on.
tree:1egnjis1851wmw.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same structure.
tree:1egnjis1851wmw.relation: A messenger from the Lord of the worlds, from God, from among yourselves.

tree:1qupflf1n0wybp.why: Satan made their deeds seem fair to them: said of past nations, of Badr, of Sheba, of Aad and Thamud, with 27:24 and 29:38 sharing 'and turned them from the way'. A memorizer set on how Satan misleads.
tree:1qupflf1n0wybp.relation: Satan beautifies evil deeds and then abandons those he misled.

tree:1l0r1b91thtxnt.why: Peace be upon: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Harun, Ilyas, and the messengers in As-Saffat, with 27:59. Short closings a memorizer must place, marking each story's end.
tree:1l0r1b91thtxnt.relation: God's greeting of peace upon each prophet, closing his story.

tree:1q3aw0f1p5pyg3.why: Peace be upon you: said by the Prophet to the believers, by the angels at death and at the gates of Paradise, by the people of the heights, and by believers turning from idle talk. The greeting of Paradise and of good manners.
tree:1q3aw0f1p5pyg3.relation: The greeting of peace from the angels and in Paradise, and among believers.

tree:0pbu83s1wbv2qe.why: Has strayed from the right way: 2:108, 5:12 and 60:1 end alike, 5:60 and 5:77 with 'further astray', and Musa hoping to be guided to the right way (28:22). A memorizer set with a contrast.
tree:0pbu83s1wbv2qe.relation: Contrast: those who exchange faith for disbelief stray from the right way; Musa prays to be guided to it.

tree:13a184v1ousktr.why: 'A party of them' describes unrelated groups (hypocrites, the fear prayer, Pharaoh's victims). A common phrase, no shared theme.

tree:1wqgque12xxzue.why: Eat of the good things We provided you: Bani Israil (2:57, 7:160, 20:81) and the believers (2:172), with spend of the good things (2:267) and do not forbid them (5:87). Memorizer set with different endings.
tree:1wqgque12xxzue.relation: Provision given as good, to be eaten with thanks and without transgression.

tree:1tpargg0vyqcx2.why: All six use 'they wronged themselves' with the same verb and sense. The rows differ in frame (repentance, destruction, God not wronging them, their dwellings), which bears on the verdict, not on removing rows. Cutting to the repentance pair is cutting to the real pairs, which the brief forbids.
tree:1tpargg0vyqcx2.changes: Reverted to the original rows: all rows share the same phrase.
tree:1tpargg0vyqcx2.relation: Those who wronged themselves: some repented, some were destroyed, God did not wrong them.

tree:0mudj3p0go2hzb.why: The refrain of al-Qamar: 'how was My punishment and warnings' and 'taste My punishment and warnings'. The old rows repeated 54:18 as a run-on of 54:16 and as its own row; each ayah appears once. The rows read on into the next ayah, so their run-ons are kept, ending 54:16 before 54:18.
tree:0mudj3p0go2hzb.changes: Gave 54:18 one row only, as the first agent did, but kept every row's run-on.
tree:0mudj3p0go2hzb.relation: The refrain after each story in al-Qamar.

tree:08396bi0ogxtqo.why: Two senses: following 'in their footsteps' with a participle (43:22, 43:23 guided, imitating; 37:70 hastening), and sending or grieving 'after them' (5:46, 57:27 We sent after them; 18:6 consuming yourself after them). 37:70 has the same structure as 43:22, and 18:6 the same sense as 5:46; neither is removed.
tree:08396bi0ogxtqo.changes: Split into the two groups as the first agent did, but kept 37:70 in the first group and 18:6 in the second.
tree:08396bi0ogxtqo.relation: In their fathers' footsteps they follow and hasten; after them came Isa, and after them the Prophet grieves.

tree:1idadbv1r10anf.why: All six use 'over the people' with an adjective. The split separates 'give us victory over the disbelieving people' (2:250, 2:286, 3:147, 29:30) from 'do not grieve over the people' (5:26, 5:68), two different verbs with the same words, and keeps every row with its run-on.
tree:1idadbv1r10anf.changes: Split into the prayer set and the 'do not grieve' pair, as the first agent did.
tree:1idadbv1r10anf.relation: Victory over the disbelieving people, and no grief over them.

check.why: Right split: 'give us victory over the people' and 'do not grieve over the people', with every row kept and runOn rows added.

tree:1vuwp5g0pf7b1e.why: All six use 'over / at the fire' with the same preposition and sense. 51:13 ('the day they are tried over the Fire') is the same structure as 46:20; 2:175 (how patient they are over the Fire) and 20:10 (guidance at the fire) keep the words' sense, and Musa's fire against the Fire of punishment is worth keeping. 2:175 reads on.
tree:1vuwp5g0pf7b1e.changes: Reverted to the original rows: the other three have the same phrase.
tree:1vuwp5g0pf7b1e.relation: Over the fire: the disbelievers exposed and tried, their patience, and Musa finding guidance at a fire.
